articles.title: Apple alertó a diputados y funcionarios de Alemania sobre posibles ataques con software espía a sus iPhone
articles.text:
Integrantes del Bundestag, el Parlamento alemán, y del gobierno federal recibieron de Apple avisos de que sus iPhone pudieron ser atacados con un programa espía comercial. La Oficina Federal de Seguridad de la Información (BSI) recomendó a los afectados tratar sus teléfonos como comprometidos, aunque no se sabe cuántos son ni quién está detrás.
El ministro de Asuntos Digitales, Karsten Wildberger, confirmó el caso el domingo en el programa Bericht aus Berlin, de la cadena pública ARD. Habló de una notificación de Apple según la cual ciertos dispositivos pudieron ser infectados con un programa espía. No precisó cuántos políticos recibieron las alertas ni quiénes son.
Según una carta del BSI citada por Wildberger, los avisos empezaron a llegar el 29 de octubre. En ellos, Apple dice haber detectado un ataque con lo que llama mercenary spyware, es decir, programas espía desarrollados por empresas y vendidos sobre todo a gobiernos. El BSI escribió a los afectados el 30 de octubre.
El organismo aclaró que no sabe si las alertas implican infecciones reales o solo intentos de ataque. Por eso pidió suponer, por precaución, que el aparato puede estar comprometido. Apple, por su parte, no indica si el ataque tuvo éxito y no atribuye los ataques a ningún gobierno.
Qué puede hacer este tipo de programa espía
Según el BSI, estas herramientas suelen infectar el teléfono sin que el dueño haga nada: basta una mensaje preparado que ni siquiera hace falta abrir, lo que se conoce como ataque de clic cero. La víctima, advierte el organismo, normalmente no nota nada.
Con el teléfono infectado, los atacantes pueden leer mensajes, incluidos los de aplicaciones cifradas, y acceder a llamadas, contactos, calendario y ubicación. También pueden encender el micrófono y la cámara. El caso más conocido de este tipo de programa es Pegasus, de la empresa NSO Group, que menciona el propio BSI.
Apple describe sus avisos como alertas de alta confianza de que una persona fue atacada de forma individual. Según la empresa, la gran mayoría de los usuarios nunca será blanco de estos ataques.
Qué recomendó el organismo alemán
El BSI aconsejó actualizar de inmediato el sistema operativo y activar el Modo de aislamiento de Apple, una función que restringe adjuntos de mensajes, vistas previas de enlaces y llamadas de FaceTime de desconocidos. El organismo aclaró que este modo dificulta nuevos ataques, pero no elimina una infección ya existente.
Para quienes consideren alto el riesgo, el organismo propuso cambiar de aparato, restablecer las cuentas usadas en él y cambiar el número de teléfono. También recomendó nuevas contraseñas, la verificación en dos pasos y, en Signal y WhatsApp, revisar los dispositivos vinculados.
El vocero del gobierno, Stefan Kornelius, dijo que Berlín se toma el incidente “muy en serio” y que las autoridades trabajan para investigar lo ocurrido y apoyar a los afectados. Se negó a decir si el canciller Friedrich Merz fue alertado.
La agencia Anadolu informó el lunes, a partir de un reporte de la revista Der Spiegel, que también recibieron avisos integrantes de la delegación que acompañó a Merz a Singapur, Japón y Corea del Sur. Según ese reporte, hubo alertas para personal de ministerios y para periodistas. Anadolu agregó que Apple envió avisos en 99 países.
Euronews informó que Apple no comentó el caso. El BSI pidió a quienes recibieron la alerta que se lo comuniquen por correo electrónico a su centro de servicio, para estimar el alcance del ataque.

articles.title: Intel réoriente une partie de sa production vers les CPU serveurs face à une demande IA record
articles.text:
Moins de processeurs Intel pour le grand public ? De toute façon, avec les prix de la mémoire vive et des SSD qui peut encore se monter un PC ?
Refrain entendu déjà des centaines de fois, l'intelligence artificielle cannibalise la production en matière de RAM et de SSD, mais elle nécessite aussi de nombreux processeurs pour animer les serveurs. Dans ce contexte, Intel a décidé de revoir sa stratégie.
Recul du PC personnel, croissance de l'IA
Ce n'est une surprise pour personne avec les prix actuels, le secteur du PC grand public recule chaque trimestre un peu plus et les prévisions en la matière ne sont guère optimistes pour l'ensemble de l'année prochaine.
Pourtant grand fournisseur de CPU pour le grand public, Intel ne semble cependant pas trop s'inquiéter de ce recul et ses principaux dirigeants estiment que la croissance du secteur de l'intelligence artificielle fera plus que compenser ces « pertes » sur le marché des ordinateurs personnels. C'est en ce sens qu'une importante réorientation de la production a été décidée.
Évoquant la demande croissante de l'IA, Lip-Bu Tan – le PDG d'Intel – a ainsi déclaré au cours d'une conférence téléphonique sur les résultats du groupe : « Le secteur continue de faire face à l'une des pénuries d'approvisionnement les plus importantes de son histoire, alimentée par une demande sans précédent en matière de superintelligence. »
« Dans ce contexte, je suis satisfait des progrès réalisés au troisième trimestre en matière d'augmentation de notre production de serveurs. Je reste néanmoins conscient des défis que nous devrons relever dans les prochains trimestres pour répondre à la demande croissante. »
Réorientation de la production Intel 18A
Une augmentation de la production en matière de CPU serveurs qui est passée par l'agrandissement de l'usine Intel Fab 24 située en Irlande, mais également par l'installation de nouveaux équipements dans l'usine Fab 62 en Arizona.
Cette réorientation de la production d'Intel ne surprend pas les analystes dans la mesure où la demande en processeurs pour serveurs continue de dépasser l'offre, malgré les augmentations évoquées précédemment. Ainsi, la division DCAI (Data Center and AI) du groupe américain a généré 7,3 milliards de dollars de chiffre d'affaires sur le seul troisième trimestre 2026, soit une progression de 17 % par rapport au trimestre précédent et de près de 80 % sur un an.
Intel anticipe donc une demande soutenue – voire en augmentation – sur les prochaines années et entend donc y répondre par un accroissement de la production de processeurs Xeon 6 « Granite Rapids », fabriqués avec la technologie de gravure Intel 3. L'agrandissement de la Fab 24 irlandaise ne suffira cependant pas et Intel entend également convertir une partie des ressources de son usine située en Oregon.
Une usine qui devait être avant tout destinée à la production de puces selon le plus récent procédé du groupe, l'Intel 18A, et qui donc va être en partie convertie vers l'Intel 3. « Pour installer Intel 3 en Oregon, nous mettons hors service des wafers de 18A, qui servent généralement à fabriquer des produits Panther Lake », a précisé Dave Zinsner, directeur financier d'Intel. « La libération de cette capacité nous permettra de produire davantage de wafers pour les centres de données ».
Clairement, Intel entend « profiter » de la baisse du marché du PC personnel et de la croissance que connaît l'activité intelligence artificielle. Pour autant, les travaux d'agrandissement et de réorientation ne produiront pas immédiatement leurs effets, on parle du second semestre 2027. Enfin, Intel entend profiter des optimisations réalisées sur le processus Intel 3 pour augmenter ses marges : il est question d'une baisse des coûts de fabrication d'environ 15 % depuis le premier trimestre 2026.
Source : Tom's Hardware

articles.title: Groundcover turns its Wand acquisition into a Kubernetes rightsizing beta - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Groundcover turns its Wand acquisition into a Kubernetes rightsizing beta
Observability company groundcover Inc. today added Autonomous Infrastructure to its platform in beta to rightsize the processor and memory requests automatically on customers’ Kubernetes workloads based on how each workload behaves in production.
The technology comes from Kubernetes resource optimization startup Wand Cloud Ltd., which groundcover acquired in September.
The release is aimed at the processor and memory requests Kubernetes has engineers set for each workload up front, usually before it has handled any real traffic, and groundcover said most teams seldom return to those numbers. When one is set too low, the first sign is often a service throwing out-of-memory errors. Padding that goes unused ends up on the monthly cloud bill.
Because the groundcover sensor has been collecting production history all along, a customer on a supported version can open Autonomous Infrastructure for the first time without installing anything and find the data the feature needs already in place. Requested processor and memory for each workload appear next to actual usage. Estimated monthly savings sit beside a count of under-provisioned workloads, and a chart tracks over time how much of the potential saving has been realized.
Dollar figures in the beta are based on a price per processor and memory unit that customers enter themselves. Public cloud pricing is the next step, according to groundcover, and billing data such as the Cost and Usage Report from Amazon Web Services Inc. will come after that.
Most resource optimization tools size each workload in isolation, groundcover argues, so a request that looks right for one service can still starve its neighbors on a crowded node. Stability is the first constraint in groundcover’s own software. Before Autonomous Infrastructure raises a request, it checks how tightly the node is already packed so one workload’s increase does not leave the rest short of resources.
Shahar Azulay, groundcover’s co-founder and chief executive, said customers can check what their clusters stand to save, from data already held in their own cloud accounts, before they let Autonomous Infrastructure “change anything.” The feature stays off until an engineer turns it on and picks the deployments, namespaces or clusters it manages.
During the beta the software touches requests only and leaves limits where they are. Each policy carries minimum and maximum bounds for processor and memory, and an audit log records who assigned each workload to a policy and when. Groundcover suggests starting with lower-risk workloads such as development namespaces and leaving alone something like a production database that needs room to grow.
The beta is available now at no additional cost to every groundcover customer running its sensor on Kubernetes, and the company is also recruiting design partners to work with its product team while it runs. Demonstrations are scheduled for KubeCon + CloudNativeCon North America in Salt Lake City Nov. 9-12.
Groundcover is a venture capital-backed startup that has raised $160 million to date, including a $100 million Series C round led by One Peak in July.

articles.title: Jewellery brand GIVA raises $100M from Multiples PE
articles.text:
Jewellery brand GIVA raises $100M from Multiples PE
Founded in 2019, Bengaluru-based GIVA focuses on everyday wear, catering primarily to Indian consumers for both self-consumption and gifting occasions. The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its leadership team, expand manufacturing and deepen its offline presence.
Multiples Alternate Asset Management along with its co-investors, has led the $100 million funding round in jewellery brand GIVA.
Founded in 2019, Bengaluru-based GIVA focuses on everyday wear, catering primarily to Indian consumers for both self-consumption and gifting occasions. The fresh capital will be used to strengthen its leadership team, expand manufacturing and deepen its offline presence.
The brand offers a diverse portfolio spanning 92.5 silver, gold and lab-grown diamond jewellery. It follows an omnichannel distribution model through its own retail stores, D2C website and leading third-party e-commerce and quick-commerce marketplaces.
Currently, the brand retails through 400+ stores across India and Sri Lanka. The latest fundraise is the largest investment in India's new-age jewellery market, according to the company.
Ishendra Agarwal, founder & CEO, GIVA said, "Multiples’ backing is a strong endorsement of what we have built at GIVA since 2019, a high-growth, design-led fine jewellery brand that Indian consumers trust for everyday wear and gifting.”
“As we enter our next phase, we are focused on scaling our omnichannel presence, strengthening our manufacturing capabilities and elevating the fine jewellery experience for modern Indian consumers. With Multiples’ experience in helping new-age businesses scale, we have the right partner for this journey. This $100 Mn+ round, the largest investment in India’s new-age jewellery market, gives us the strength to move faster.”
The company also added that India's jewellery market is estimated to grow at around 6% CAGR to reach $124 billion by 2032.
Multiples has also invested in brands such as Licious, ACKO, PVR and Arvind Fashions apart from in other sectors. Earlier this year, Multiples announced the close of a USD $430 million fund.

articles.title: Intel 14A moves closer to production as PDK 0.9 becomes available — plans to release PDK 1.0 in the first quarter of 2027
articles.text:
Intel 14A moves closer to production as PDK 0.9 becomes available — plans to release PDK 1.0 in the first quarter of 2027
PDK 1.0 due in early 2027.
Intel Foundry last week made available its Intel 14A process design kit (PDK) version 0.9, an important milestone in the development of this next-generation manufacturing technology. The company says that the production node is reaching performance and yield maturity expected at this stage of development, and the results are backed by silicon validation. Intel plans to release PDK 1.0 in the first quarter of 2027, which will validate the technology's readiness for high-volume manufacturing (HVM).
14A PDK v0.9 is here
A process design kit contains transistor models, design rules, and other information that enables chip designers to develop products for a particular manufacturing process using electronic design automation (EDA) tools. The accuracy and quality of the PDK are crucial for modelling how chips will perform once manufactured, and the release of PDK 0.9 is particularly important because it provides customers with a representation of Intel 14A based on actual silicon measurements rather than on theoretical models or simulations. At this stage, customers can proceed with product development with greater confidence that the technology will meet their requirements when it comes to performance and power consumption.
Intel says that PDK 0.9 lets customers develop designs intended to enter risk production around the time the process is certified, which — provided that PDK accurately reflects the characteristics of manufactured silicon — in many cases enables chip developers to greatly reduce the number of silicon revisions between initial tapeout and mass production. Of course, availability of PDK 0.9 does not indicate that Intel 14A is ready or even close to mass production, as the company expects to validate HVM readiness only with PDK 1.0, sometime in Q1 2027. Again, this does not mean that 14A will enter mass production in early 2027, as Intel itself expects to begin mass production using its 14A process technology in 2028, following risk production for its own products in the second half of 2027.
"From a customer perspective, the PDK 0.9 gives customers the confidence to design products on Intel 14A, as the technology is reaching the industry-standard performance and yield maturity expected at this stage of development, supported by silicon-backed validation," said Ben Sell, corporate vice president and general manager of front-end technology development at Intel Foundry.
Building on top of 18A
Intel 14A builds on top of architectural foundations introduced with Intel 18A but incorporates several substantial enhancements. These include 2nd Generation RibbonFET 2 gate-all-around (GAA) transistors, PowerDirect backside power delivery (which delivers power right to the transistor source/drain regions without using intermediate connections like TSVs used by PowerVia), and Turbo Cells (high-performance standard cells designed to accelerate timing-critical paths in CPUs and GPUs), which provide chip designers with additional ways to increase performance and optimize power efficiency. Since Intel has previously outlined advantages of these technologies, the latest announcement does not provide updates regarding transistor performance, power consumption, or transistor density figures for Intel 14A.
Beyond improvements to transistor, power delivery, and interconnect technologies, Intel is applying manufacturing experience gained during 12 months of Intel 18A production to accelerate maturation of 14A. Specifically, the company says it has increased investments in inline defect detection, modeling, and simulation to identify potential manufacturing problems earlier in the development cycle. These initiatives are intended to improve manufacturing yields, process variability, ultimately transistor performance, and reduce production cycle times. Intel also says it has introduced several strategic initiatives to accelerate technology development, although it does not quantify their impact.
New collaboration model
Another important change concerns Intel's relationships with equipment and materials suppliers. The company says it has revised its collaboration model to involve technology development teams and external suppliers earlier in the process development cycle. The goal of such close collaborations is to address manufacturing defects and improve equipment capabilities before they become obstacles for yield improvements after the technology enters mass production. Intel also conducts regular yield summit meetings with suppliers to accelerate progress on critical development objectives.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
"This has required evolving our collaboration model with equipment and material suppliers, and earlier engagement from our [technology development] leaders with suppliers to drive improvements in defects and equipment capabilities," Sell said.
A bonus of such early collaboration is that equipment and materials suppliers may incorporate Intel's requirements into their standard products and development roadmaps. This could give Intel an advantage over competitors, which would have to either adapt their manufacturing processes to equipment optimized around Intel's requirements or work with suppliers to develop alternative solutions from scratch.
Historically, Intel frequently set the direction for semiconductor manufacturing technologies as other chipmakers subsequently adopted similar approaches. One notable exception was immersion DUV lithography, which Intel adopted after TSMC, which led the development of immersion DUV lithography. By engaging equipment and materials suppliers earlier, Intel could regain some of its historical influence over the development of industry-standard manufacturing solutions, though the importance of this should not be overestimated.
Expanding design ecosystem
Meanwhile, Intel continues to expand the design ecosystem for its 14A technology. Cadence and Intel have established a design-technology co-optimization (DTCO) collaboration focused on next-generation AI-driven design tools and intellectual property, whereas Keysight, Siemens, and Synopsys have announced design-tool certifications for the process. Intel is also working with other software developers and IP providers to validate design flows and reusable building blocks required by prospective foundry customers.
Intel says it is encouraged by customer feedback regarding the progress of 14A development. However, the company has not identified any customers that have committed to manufacturing products using the technology, disclosed customer tape-outs, or announced specific manufacturing agreements, which is normal for the foundry industry. For Intel Foundry, attracting external customers remains particularly important because development costs of modern leading-edge process technologies can only be recoupled when they are used to make hundreds of millions of chips, way more than Intel sells these days. Meanwhile, the commercial success of Intel Foundry with advanced manufacturing technologies depends not only on transistor performance and manufacturing yields, but also on its ability to deliver predictable development schedules.
Looking ahead, Intel intends to continue improving performance, yields, variability, and manufacturing cycle times of 14A, though for now the company does not disclose any actual goals. Intel also plans additional process enhancements and performance refinements for 14A-E and 14A-P nodes after the initial technology becomes available. However, exact schedules for these nodes are not known at the moment.
"Our next major milestone is the Intel 14A PDK 1.0, expected in the first quarter of 2027," said Ali Farhang, corporate vice president and general manager of Intel Foundry's design technology platform organization. "I am looking forward to sustaining this level of quality across future releases and continuing to earn our customers' trust by delivering on our commitments with a customer-first mindset."

Anton Shilov is a contributing writer at Tom’s Hardware. Over the past couple of decades, he has covered everything from CPUs and GPUs to supercomputers and from modern process technologies and latest fab tools to high-tech industry trends.

articles.title: La salida a bolsa de Anthropic conseguirá algo tan poco habitual como que el 80% de su plantilla se haga millonaria
articles.text:
2026 está siendo un año de infarto para los gestores de fondos, no solo por el nivel de beneficios que está reportando a los inversores las cotizaciones estratosféricas de las grandes tecnológicas, sino por la salida a bolsa de los nuevos pesos pesados de la IA como SpaceX o Anthropic.
La salida a bolsa de SpaceX ya hizo millonarios a muchos de sus empleados, pero en el caso de Anthropic, el fenómeno se intensifica y el resultado es que ocho de cada diez empleados de Dario Amodei y sus socios serán millonarios el día después de esa salida a bolsa.
Cuatro de cada cinco. La empresa ya presentó su documento ante la SEC y, según informó Bloomberg, quiere debutar hacia mediados del mes de noviembre. Aún no se ha fijado un precio de salida para su cotización ni una fecha concreta, pero se habla de una valoración de entre 1,5 y 2 billones de dólares.
Según recoge The Observer, un informe de la plataforma financiera Hill reparte el botín de sus empleados por tramos. Sumados todos ellos, salen unos 4.250 nuevos millonarios de entre los 5.300 empleados que Anthropic declaraba en su informe S-1 ante la autoridad bursátil norteamericana. Eso representa el 80% de la plantilla, una suma que no sale de ninguna fuente oficial. SpaceX hizo algo parecido en junio, convirtiendo en millonarios a más de 4.400 empleados entre su plantilla actual y antigua, pero en este caso se trataba de una plantilla de unos 22.000 empleados. En el caso de Anthropic, la proporción de nuevos millonarios es muy superior.
Siete que ya lo eran. Los cofundadores no cuentan como nuevos millonarios porque, de hecho, ya son milmimillonarios incluso antes de la salida a bolsa de la compañía. Forbes calcula que cada uno de los siete fundadores posee cerca del 1,4% de la empresa.
Con una valoración de entre 1,5 y 2 billones en su salida a bolsa, su parte se colocaría entre los 27.000 y 29.000 millones de dólares por cabeza. Juntos controlan en torno al 10% del capital. Aun así, comparten una acción especial sin derechos económicos que concentra el 50,1% de los votos de los accionistas.
Los empleados más fieles. Un poco más abajo en el reparto de acciones (y beneficios), Hill estima que unos 50 de los primeros empleados y directivos pasarían a tener una fortuna de más de 100 millones de dólares tras la salida a bolsa por el valor de los paquetes de participaciones que han recibido como reconocimiento de "empleados fundadores". Son menos del 1% de la plantilla y entraron en Anthropic cuando la empresa aún tenía que demostrar su valía.
Más abajo estaría un segundo escalón de unos 1.200 empleados de alta cualificación e investigadores que, por las participaciones asociadas a sus paquetes salariales, acumularían más de 10 millones de dólares, casi una cuarta parte del total. Otros 3.000 empleados, con retribuciones de menor cuantía, pasarían del millón de dólares tras la salida a bolsa. Todas estas son cifras mínimas, calculadas en base a una valoración hipotética de 1,5 billones, a los que habría que sumar unos 1.000 empleados que se quedarían por debajo de ese millón de dólares.
Promesas y plazos. Los siete cofundadores prometieron donar el 80% de su patrimonio a fines filantrópicos destinados a paliar los efectos negativos de la tecnología que están desarrollando. Dario Amodei escribió que lo preocupante es "un nivel de concentración de riqueza que destruirá la sociedad". El propio folleto de la salida a bolsa de Anthropic admite que la IA "tiene el potencial de concentrar el poder y la riqueza".
No obstante, el dinero tampoco llegará de golpe a la plantilla de Anthropic, porque los empleados no podrán vender sus acciones inmediatamente después la salida a bolsa, sino que se abrirán por fases a partir de enero de 2027. Anthropic usará parte de lo que recaude para pagar impuestos de las acciones de sus empleados.

articles.title: R$ 31 milhões: Anatel fica sem dinheiro para pagar o próprio data center • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
R$ 31 milhões: Anatel fica sem dinheiro para pagar o próprio data center
Agência pediu, mas não recebeu recurso do Tesouro Nacional em outras ocasiões.
A Anatel estaria sem dinheiro para custear o próprio data center em Brasília, segundo informações do jornal Folha de São Paulo nesta terça-feira (03/11). A Agência Nacional de Telecomunicações alertou o Governo Federal de que precisa de R$ 30,76 milhões para arcar com as notas fiscais referentes ao projeto.
Além disso, a agência também estaria sem recursos para pagar contas básicas. O presidente Carlos Baigorri buscou o Ministério do Planejamento na semana passada para solicitar o desbloqueio de R$ 30 milhões. Em ocasiões anteriores, ainda segundo a Folha, o pedido não foi atendido pelo Tesouro Nacional.
A Anatel atribui a falta de recursos ao bloqueio de R$ 51,83 milhões, determinado em maio. Houve uma redução de 19% no orçamento discricionário, aquele destinado a custeio e investimentos.
Já o data center foi contratado em dezembro de 2025, ao custo de R$ 44,95 milhões em produtos e serviços. De acordo com a Folha, o contrato inclui desde equipamentos até a manutenção e garantia.
Nós buscamos a Anatel. Embora a agência não tenha comentado os valores citados na apuração da Folha, ela alertou que “a persistência das restrições orçamentárias e financeiras poderá exigir novas medidas de reprogramação de despesas”.

articles.title: Binance Reveals How Fake Job Interviews and AI Tool Abuse Led to $6.43 Billion Theft
articles.text:
Binance on Tuesday said the record-setting theft of $6.43 billion in assets from the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange was the culmination of a "sophisticated, multi-stage campaign" that involved the use of a tampered Homebrew installation and recruitment-themed social engineering attack targeting two of its engineers.
"It was not a single isolated breach or a simple phishing incident," the company said. "The attackers combined a range of techniques, including social engineering by fake recruitment interviews, malicious software downloads, compromised internal AI tooling, endpoint compromise, and an advanced transaction-authorisation method."
The starting point has been traced back to a supply chain attack targeting one of its engineers from the Wallet DevOps team (named "Engineer A"), who downloaded a trojanized Homebrew installer to install a popular artificial intelligence (AI) tool after searching for it on a search engine. The incident occurred in June 2026.
Although Binance said it detected the attack and rotated all related credentials as a precautionary step, the company said information about "Engineer A's role and his related colleagues on our wallet infrastructure team was exposed to the hacker."
The second part of the attack occurred in September 2026, with the threat actor contacting another engineer (named "Engineer B") via a legitimate job-hunting platform by disguising themselves as a Project Director.
The Project Director persona arranged a first-round interview with a human resources (HR) representative, which was then followed by a second-round interview with an individual claiming to be the CEO of a non-existent company. Binance did not disclose details of the fake company.
Over the course of the first-round video interview, the HR representative shared a social media account, including personal photos and videos posted on the platform, in an attempt to build credibility and establish trust. The second round, on the other hand, took place on a popular social chat app.
"Near the end of the interview, Engineer B was instructed to download an 'assignment' containing a malicious code repository onto his work computer," Binance said. "The repository contained malicious code that executed during the setup process, initiating a series of unauthorized activities."
The undetected malware utilized advanced obfuscation and evasion techniques, including substituting a legitimate development tool component with a poisoned version to execute commands and establish communication with an attacker-controlled external server. In addition, the threat actor took steps to cover up tracks by removing forensic artifacts related to the compromise.
The intrusion moved to the next stage on October 20, 2026, when the adversary leveraged Engineer B's compromised computer and abused an internal AI tool to gain control over Engineer A and another Wallet Software Engineer C.
"The attacker soon discovered Wallet DevOps Engineer A had a container deployment permission token on his computer," Binance explained. "On 29 October between 17:15 and 19:56, the attacker logged onto Software Engineer C's computer, used the credentials stolen from Wallet DevOps Engineer A, deployed a container, and triggered a malicious script to launch the attack."
The attack ultimately exploited its unauthorized access to an internal wallet signing service to initiate transactions outside the normal withdrawal process.
In response to the incident, Binance has reconstructed the affected wallet system in a new environment, as well as rebuilt the internal AI tool and access controls. Other steps taken as of November 3 are listed below -
- Replaced affected devices.
- Decommissioned credentials and tokens related to affected engineers.
- Completed enhanced security scans across all employee devices.
- Enhanced AI-based behavioural anomaly detection.
- Strengthened wallet-service risk controls.
- Worked with law enforcement, blockchain intelligence firms, and industry partners to trace and freeze affected assets.
"The entry points identified as having been used in the attack have been closed. Systems touched in the attack path have been rebuilt or replaced," Binance said. "We have also implemented tighter device controls, enhanced wallet-service risk controls and expanded AI-based behavioural anomaly detection."
"We are increasing investment in AI-enabled detection, endpoint protection, developer-environment security and behavioural anomaly monitoring."
Since the start of the year, Binance is estimated to have foiled 57 suspected North Korea-linked cyber threat cases, underscoring the persistent nature of the attacks targeting the cryptocurrency industry.
"The techniques include fraudulent job interviews, malicious software disguised as popular developer tools, compromised software packages and browser extensions, fake video conferencing applications, and social engineering campaigns designed to steal credentials or deploy remote access malware," Binance said.

articles.title: Black Friday : envie d’une batterie XXL ? Le nouveau POCO X8 est déjà à 279€
articles.text:
Mi-septembre, son offre de pré-lancement le plaçait à 299 €, et Amazon fait désormais mieux. Le POCO X8 en 8 + 256 Go passe à 279 € au lieu de 399,90 €, un prix qui récompense sa batterie de 8 340 mAh plus que sa photo, réduite à un seul vrai capteur.
Le POCO X8 ferme la marche de la gamme POCO de la rentrée, sous les F9 Pro et F9 Ultra. Il ne cherche pas la puissance et mise sur une batterie de 8 340 mAh, un grand écran AMOLED et une certification IP68. Amazon le propose à 279 € au lieu de 399,90 € en 8 Go + 256 Go, coloris noir, soit 120,90 € sous son prix conseillé.
C’est aussi 20 € sous l’offre de pré-lancement à 299 € que nous relevions à son annonce, valable jusqu’au 21 septembre. Il s’adresse à ceux qui veulent tenir longtemps loin d’une prise sans dépasser 300 €.
Le POCO X8 8 Go + 256 Go et sa batterie de 8 340 mAh sont à 279 € au lieu de 399,90 € chez Amazon, coloris noir.
Pourquoi choisir le POCO X8 ?
- Une batterie hors normes : Avec 8 340 mAh, sa batterie au silicium-carbone dépasse de 1 840 mAh celle du POCO X8 Pro. Elle se recharge en 67 W et dépanne un autre appareil par câble, jusqu’à 22,5 W.
- Un écran taillé pour l’extérieur : La dalle AMOLED de 6,83 pouces affiche une définition 1,5K à 120 Hz et un pic annoncé à 3 500 nits, de quoi rester lisible en plein soleil.
- Une coque qui encaisse : Certifié IP68 et protégé par un verre Gorilla Glass Victus 2, il résiste selon Xiaomi à 30 minutes d’immersion à 2 mètres en eau douce. Une vraie sécurité au quotidien.
Trajets, GPS, séries : là où sa batterie fait la différence
Cette batterie prend tout son sens pour qui passe ses journées en déplacement, guide sa voiture au GPS ou enchaîne les séries dans les transports. Le grand écran et le double haut-parleur Dolby Atmos se prêtent à la vidéo, et la charge inversée filaire remet quelques pourcents à des écouteurs ou au téléphone d’un proche. Le NFC gère le paiement sans contact, et l’émetteur infrarouge fait office de télécommande pour la télévision ou la climatisation.
Il convient aux étudiants et aux actifs qui multiplient les trajets sans vouloir y laisser 400 €. Les amateurs de photo seront moins servis : un capteur principal de 50 Mpx stabilisé, un capteur de profondeur de 2 Mpx, aucun ultra grand-angle, et une vidéo plafonnée en 1080p à 30 images par seconde. Comme nous le notions à son annonce, il rogne aussi sur les performances avec sa puce Snapdragon 6s Gen 4, ce qui oriente les joueurs exigeants ailleurs. Avec 223 g, il se manie enfin difficilement d’une main.
POCO X8 ou X8 Pro : l’endurance contre la puissance
Lancé en mars au même prix conseillé de 399,90 € en 8 + 256 Go, le POCO X8 Pro apporte une puce Dimensity 8500-Ultra plus puissante, un ultra grand-angle de 8 Mpx et une charge de 100 W. Le X8 lui oppose 8 340 mAh contre 6 500 mAh et un écran plus grand, dans un format moins compact. Pour situer ces deux modèles face au reste du marché, notre comparatif des meilleurs smartphones passe en revue les références à tous les budgets, y compris sous 300 €.
✅ Les points forts
- Batterie de 8 340 mAh, rechargée en 67 W
- Écran AMOLED 1,5K de 6,83 pouces à 120 Hz
- Certification IP68 et verre Gorilla Glass Victus 2
- NFC, émetteur infrarouge et double haut-parleur
- 256 Go de stockage en UFS 3.1
❌ Les limites
- Pas d’ultra grand-angle, vidéo limitée au 1080p à 30 i/s
- Performances de milieu de gamme, en retrait du X8 Pro
- Ni chargeur dans la boîte, ni charge sans fil
- Gabarit imposant : 223 g et 8,6 mm d’épaisseur
Vendu au même prix conseillé que le X8 Pro, le POCO X8 descend à 279 € chez Amazon, 20 € sous son offre de pré-lancement de septembre.
À 279 €, le POCO X8 devient un achat cohérent pour qui place l’autonomie au-dessus du reste. Sa batterie de 8 340 mAh, son écran lumineux et sa résistance à l’eau répondent à un usage intensif et nomade, à un prix inférieur à celui de son offre de pré-lancement. La remise de 30 % porte sur un prix conseillé que l’offre de lancement à 299 € avait déjà entamé : c’est ce repère qui compte, et il est battu.
Les photographes et les joueurs ont en revanche intérêt à regarder du côté du X8 Pro ou d’un modèle mieux équipé en photo. Le X8 ne cherche pas à tout faire, et c’est ce choix assumé qui le rend intéressant pour un étudiant ou un gros consommateur de vidéo. Pensez simplement à prévoir un bloc secteur compatible 67 W si vous n’en avez pas déjà un.

articles.title: ¿Para qué sirven las ranuras de las escaleras eléctricas? Su importante función y la razón detrás de su diseño
articles.text:
Millones de personas utilizan escaleras eléctricas cada día en centros comerciales, aeropuertos y estaciones de transporte sin reparar en un detalle que resulta clave para su seguridad: las ranuras que recorren la superficie de cada escalón. Lejos de ser un elemento decorativo, este diseño cumple una función mecánica precisa que previene atrapamientos y accidentes.
El mecanismo se activa en los extremos de la escalera, donde los escalones pasan de una forma escalonada a una superficie plana antes de desaparecer bajo el piso. En ese punto, una placa metálica fija conocida como peine, equipada con dientes alineados, se acopla con las ranuras de cada escalón como si fueran dos piezas que encajan entre sí.
Peine evita atrapamientos
Según explicó el sitio especializado Mental Floss, citando al ingeniero George R. Strakosch, autor de The Vertical Transportation Handbook, los escalones están acanalados “para que las personas que viajan con los dedos del pie contra la contrahuella no tengan sus suelas de zapatos blandas arrastradas entre los escalones a medida que estos se enderezan”. Esta descripción explica por qué el diseño resulta crítico en el momento exacto en que el escalón cambia de forma.
Los dientes del peine se introducen en las ranuras y, al hacerlo, levantan y apartan cualquier objeto pequeño que pudiera quedar atrapado, como cordones de zapatos, bolsas de plástico o el borde de una sandalia. El medio Firstpost detalló que, sin este sistema, el calzado blando podría ser succionado hacia la maquinaria interna de la escalera, con el consiguiente riesgo de lesiones graves.
Diseño que reemplazó los escalones lisos
Las primeras escaleras eléctricas no contaban con este sistema. Según consignó Mental Floss, los modelos originales tenían escalones completamente lisos, lo que generaba un problema conocido en el punto donde la escalera llegaba al piso: los usuarios debían descender de costado para evitar que algún objeto quedara atrapado en el hueco superior. La incorporación de las ranuras junto con la placa peine permitió resolver ese inconveniente y que los pasajeros bajaran de frente con mayor seguridad.
Las fuentes consultadas coinciden en que este sistema cumple, además, otras funciones complementarias:
- Drenaje de líquidos: las ranuras actúan como canales que evitan la acumulación de agua, barro o líquidos derramados sobre la superficie del escalón, lo que reduce el riesgo de resbalones en días de lluvia.
- Mejora de la tracción: al mantener la superficie más seca, el calzado logra mayor adherencia durante el trayecto.
- Reducción de tropiezos: el encastre entre los escalones evita que se formen huecos visibles mientras cambian de forma plana a escalonada.
- Guía visual: el contraste entre las ranuras y las líneas amarillas de demarcación ayuda a que los usuarios ubiquen sus pies en el centro del escalón, lejos de los bordes laterales.
Sistemas de seguridad complementarios
El diseño de las ranuras no funciona de manera aislada. De acuerdo con especificaciones técnicas de fabricantes como Mitsubishi Electric, las escaleras modernas incorporan dispositivos adicionales de seguridad vinculados al funcionamiento del peine, entre ellos sensores que detienen automáticamente el mecanismo si detectan un objeto atrapado en el espacio entre el escalón y la placa, o si identifican una falla en el nivel u orientación de algún peldaño.
Estos sistemas, combinados con el diseño acanalado de los escalones, buscan reducir los riesgos de accidentes en un dispositivo que transporta a un volumen constante de pasajeros en espacios públicos de alto tránsito.

articles.title: Adieu le petit découvert accordé sans questions : dès le 20 novembre, votre banque passera vos revenus au crible, même pour 50 euros
articles.text:
Découvert bancaire : le tour de vis arrive le 20 novembre, entre fin du forfait d'agios et contrôle des revenus
Le petit découvert de fin de mois, accordé jusqu’ici sans contrôle obligatoire, vit ses derniers jours. Dès le 20 novembre, pour 50 euros comme pour 1 000, votre banque devra vérifier que vous pouvez rembourser avant de vous accorder la moindre facilité, exactement comme pour un crédit à la consommation. La réforme réserve pourtant une bonne surprise, que certains clients verront apparaître sur leurs relevés.
Le 20 novembre 2026 entre en vigueur l'ordonnance du 3 septembre 2025 relative au crédit à la consommation. Elle transpose une directive européenne d'octobre 2023 et soumet toute nouvelle autorisation de découvert au droit du crédit à la consommation, quel que soit son montant. Jusqu'ici, les découverts inférieurs à 200 euros, ou remboursables sous un mois, échappaient à ces règles. Cette exception disparaît, une évolution dont nous avions détaillé les risques pour les ménages modestes dès l'an dernier. Devant les rumeurs d'une interdiction pure et simple, le ministère de l'Économie a publié une mise au point : le découvert reste possible, sous un cadre nettement plus strict.
Découvert bancaire : ce que votre banque devra vérifier dès le 20 novembre
Selon la note publiée par Bercy, l'obligation d'analyser la solvabilité s'étend à tous les découverts, quels que soient leur montant et leur délai de remboursement. Revenus, charges, fonctionnement du compte : la banque fondera son accord sur votre situation réelle. Le contrôle reste proportionné. Sous 200 euros, la consultation du fichier des incidents de remboursement des crédits aux particuliers (FICP) deviendra facultative. Avant la signature, l'établissement remettra aussi une information complète sur le coût du découvert, son taux annuel effectif global (TAEG) et les conditions de remboursement.
	
L'autorisation de découvert n'a jamais été automatique : il n'existe pas de droit au crédit en France.
Le quotidien ne change pas pour autant. Une fois l'autorisation inscrite dans la convention de compte, aucune nouvelle demande n'est nécessaire à chaque passage dans le rouge, dans la limite prévue. Les autorisations accordées avant le 20 novembre restent valables. Plusieurs parlementaires redoutent malgré tout que les ménages les plus serrés en fin de mois se heurtent plus souvent à un refus. Certaines offres fonctionnent déjà sans aucun filet, comme le compte Nickel, qui ne propose pas de découvert autorisé.
Fin du forfait d'agios : une économie pour les petits découverts
C'est la face plus agréable de la réforme. Certaines banques prélèvent aujourd'hui un minimum forfaitaire d'agios : un montant fixe facturé dès que le compte passe dans le rouge, sur les découverts de moins de 400 euros, et supérieur, par construction, aux intérêts réellement dus. Il vient s'ajouter à des frais bancaires déjà orientés à la hausse. Dans sa réponse au Sénat publiée le 30 avril 2026, le ministère confirme que ces forfaits disparaissent et qu'ils seront intégrés au TAEG, lui-même plafonné par le taux d'usure. Pour un client qui passe régulièrement quelques dizaines d'euros sous zéro, la note peut fondre sensiblement.
Le texte protège également le titulaire d'un découvert à durée indéterminée que la banque réduit. Il pourra rembourser, sans frais supplémentaires, la part qui dépasse le nouveau plafond avant toute procédure d'exécution.
Le bon réflexe d'ici au 20 novembre : ouvrir la brochure tarifaire de sa banque à la rubrique "découvert" et repérer la ligne "minimum" ou "forfait". Elle devrait disparaître pour tout découvert accordé à partir de cette date.

articles.title: Barracuda Flaws Could Be Chained to Bypass Authorization and Gain Root Access
articles.text:
Barracuda has disclosed details of two vulnerabilities affecting its products that, if chained together, could allow an attacker to bypass authorization controls and gain root access to a susceptible device.
The vulnerabilities, a pre-authentication authorization bypass vulnerability and a command injection vulnerability, have been assigned the CVE identifiers CVE-2026-116606 (CVSS score: 9.3) and CVE-2026-111560 (CVSS score: 8.6), respectively.
While CVE-2026-116606 only affects Email Security Gateway, CVE-2026-111560 impacts the following Barracuda products -
- Email Security Gateway
- Load Balancer Application Delivery Controller
- Message Archiver
- WAF Control Center
- Web Application Firewall
- Web Security Gateway
"Successful exploitation requires an attacker to have access to the administrative interface of an affected product," Barracuda said. "If exploited in combination, these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to bypass authorization controls and obtain root access to the device."
Barracuda said that organizations that do not expose their administrative interfaces to the internet are less vulnerable to the attack path, urging customers to follow the steps below -
- Restrict access to administrative interfaces to trusted internal networks
- Use appropriate network access controls to limit exposure
"Customers using these products should verify that their systems are running the latest firmware versions and have received all security patches," it added. "If firmware on a device is multiple versions out of date, customers may need to perform more than one update."

articles.title: Novee’s External Surface Testing checks which exposed assets attackers can actually exploit - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Novee’s External Surface Testing checks which exposed assets attackers can actually exploit
Artificial intelligence penetration testing startup Novee Cyber Security Ltd. today added External Surface Testing to its platform so its AI-driven attacks can reach a customer’s entire internet-facing footprint.
External Surface Testing is aimed at the scramble after a critical vulnerability is disclosed, when security teams have to work out which exposed assets are affected and whether any can actually be exploited. Novee argues that attackers see a target as a single environment with many ways in, including forgotten subdomains and staging servers someone left exposed.
Conventional external attack surface management products catalog a company’s exposed assets and score them by severity. Netta Rager Dan, vice president of product at Novee, said those products “show you what’s exposed, but don’t give you the full picture of real risk.” In the company’s telling, security staff are left to validate long lists of exposures on their own.
Novee’s version needs nothing more than a domain name to get started. From there the software works outward the way an outside attacker would, and it keeps track of what it learns about each asset and service as it goes. A newly disclosed vulnerability gets run against a customer’s live systems to see whether anyone could actually exploit it.
Findings exported from other vendors’ attack surface tools go through the same check. Novee says the testing also catches flaws nobody had logged, chained attack paths among them, and the customer ends up with a short, prioritized list of validated issues backed by evidence.
Until now Novee’s testing has stopped at the application layer. External Surface Testing runs on the same platform as the company’s Application Pentesting product, so a host found during external discovery can be promoted straight into a full gray-box or white-box pentest. Whatever the discovery phase learned carries over. Novee claims no other fully autonomous AI pentesting platform covers the external attack surface as well as web, mobile and AI applications.
Limits are built in to keep the testing safe. Customers approve the scope before anything runs, and the probes come from outside the perimeter without agents or customer-supplied credentials. Exploit attempts don’t use destructive payloads. Traffic is held under configured caps so testing doesn’t cause load spikes or bury the security operations center in noise.
Former national-level offensive security operators Ido Geffen, Gon Chalamish and Omer Ninburg founded Novee in May 2025. YL Ventures LP, Canaan Partners and Zeev Ventures LP backed the company when it launched in January with $51.5 million in funding.
External Surface Testing is available now as part of the Novee platform.

articles.title: 'Traditional cyber defenses alone are no longer sufficient': OpenAI is raising its bug bounty rewards for security researchers as AI attack worries grow
articles.text:
'Traditional cyber defenses alone are no longer sufficient': OpenAI is raising its bug bounty rewards for security researchers as AI attack worries grow
OpenAI announces major security initiatives
- Cathedral Systems will offer a new perspective into OpenAI vulnerabilities
- Partnering with third parties sets 'an important example' for the industry
- Bug bounty payouts set to increase 4x for critical findings
OpenAI has announced a partnership with Cathedral Systems to bring security researchers from both organizations together in a bid to test its AI infrastructure, identify potential vulnerabilities and improve existing defenses.
The ChatGPT maker hopes that enlisting a third party with add fresh perspectives to its existing research, and it's a clear sign that the company knows future threats could pose a serious issue.
"OpenAI is setting an important example by partnering with outside security firms and using its own models to continuously test and strengthen its defenses," Cathedral CEO Gavin Kliger wrote.
OpenAI is preparing to serious enhance security
The company is also improving its bug bounty program to make it more attractive for individual researchers to get involved. Though exact rewards were omitted from the announcement, OpenAI did say it was prepared to quadruple the payouts for critical findings.
When OpenAI launched its bug bounty scheme, it said it would be looking for applications across software patches, model privacy, threat detection and response, security tool integration and AI agent security.
It's not the first time the AI giant has led a major security initiative – it previously asked a quarter of its developers to set aside some time to find and fix security weaknesses. Naturally, they used Codex to speed up investigations and fixes.
"We’re building on that work because traditional cyber defenses alone are no longer sufficient," the company said, referring to its previous sprint.

articles.title: ideaForge takes flight as Q2 FY27 revenue jumps 124% to Rs 91 Cr
articles.text:
ideaForge takes flight as Q2 FY27 revenue jumps 124% to Rs 91 Cr
ideaForge achieved a Q2 FY27 financial turnaround with Rs 91.3 crore revenue and Rs 23.2 crore EBITDA, while advancing combat UAVs and securing Rs 151 crore RDI funding for heavy-lift logistics.
Strong execution and technology innovation helped drive a sharp financial turnaround for Indian drone maker ideaForge in the second quarter FY27.
“Building on the steady start of the year in Q1 FY27, Q2 FY27 saw continued progress in order book execution, new product development, and preparations to capitalise on upcoming procurement opportunities,” said Ankit Mehta, Co-founder and Chief Executive Officer of ideaForge Technology.
A return to profitability
In Q2 FY27, revenue from operations reached Rs 91.3 crore, up 124% year-on-year (YoY) from Q2 FY26. For the half-year period H1 FY27, operating revenue surged 199% YoY to a record Rs 159.9 crore from Rs 53.5 crore in H1 FY26, driven by delivering over 50% of the opening order book.
Revenue streams were led by the defence vertical, which generated Rs 65.7 crore or 72% of Q2 FY27 operating revenue. The civil and enterprise segment contributed Rs 25.6 crore or 28% in Q2 FY27, driven by mapping projects, crowd safety monitoring, and Drone-as-a-Service software subscriptions, which offer cloud-based drone operations.
The company returned to profitability, reporting a profit after tax (PAT) of Rs 6.5 crore in Q2 FY27, with a net margin of 7.1%. This compares with a loss of Rs 19.6 crore and a negative margin of 48.1% in Q2 FY26.
EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortisation) stood at Rs 23.2 crore, with a margin of 25.4%, compared with a loss of Rs 8 crore and a negative margin of 19.6% in the year-ago quarter.
Q2 FY27 total expenses rose 41.8% YoY to Rs 90.1 crore. The largest cost centre in Q2 FY27 was material costs at Rs 48.1 crore, representing 53.4% of total expenses, followed by employee benefit expenses of Rs 16.6 crore (18.4%), other expenses of Rs 16.0 crore (17.8%), depreciation and amortisation of Rs 14.7 crore (16.3%), and finance costs of Rs 1.0 crore (1.1%).
Operational hurdles and expansion
“We have maintained our execution momentum despite persistent global supply chain constraints and a few delays in customer approvals for deliveries. While these challenges remain significant, we continue to closely monitor developments and take measures to minimise their impact on our operations and deliveries,” Mehta commented.
The firm secured Rs 151 crore in research debt funding from the Technology Development Board to develop YETI, a middle-mile logistics drone carrying 200 kg payloads over 200 km.
It completed field testing for the ZOLT hybrid tactical drone, offering 100 km range and 6 hours endurance with electronic warfare resilience to withstand signal jamming during intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance missions.
Additionally, equity capital raised via QIP enabled complete debt payoff.
However, hurdles remain with global supply bottlenecks, customer delivery acceptance sign-off delays, and a shrinking order book that stood at Rs 202.2 crore by Q2 FY27 end, down from Rs 350.8 crore in Q3 FY26 as execution outpaced new contract awards.
High working capital intensity also persists, with inventory at Rs 155 crore and trade receivables at Rs 161.1 crore. Nevertheless, an estimated Rs 20,000 crore Fast Track Procurement pipeline offers strong medium-term visibility.

articles.title: Elon Musk's xAI installs eight converted jet engines to power Mississippi data center — permits allow 25 percent higher limit for pollutants, concerns raised over carbon monoxide
articles.text:
Elon Musk's xAI installs eight converted jet engines to power Mississippi data center — permits allow 25 percent higher limit for pollutants, concerns raised over carbon monoxide
Carbon dioxide-spilling converted turbines have been installed in a Mississippi xAI data center despite the known health risks.
Elon Musk's xAI is using eight converted jet engine turbines to power a Mississippi data center. While the generators have the required state-level permission and permits, there remain concerns about the impact they could have on the local environment. The permits allow for a 25% higher limit in pollutants known as volatile organic compounds, but those compounds, paired with the expulsion of carbon monoxide, have environmentalists warning that the use of jet engines to power data centers is a step in the wrong direction. The New York Times reports that the Southern Environmental Law Center has already challenged Mississippi's decision to approve the turbines for use at xAI's data center.
The group argues that xAI has failed to provide guarantees that the jet-powered turbines meet emissions standards for specific pollutants, including formaldehyde. It also accuses xAI of what the report terms the "undercounting" of projected emissions in relation to the data center's power sources. This comes after the same group sued xAI over its use of gas generators without the required permits in an area with more than 100,000 inhabitants.
The generators used by xAI are converted by ProEnergy, a Missouri-based outfit that repurposes the unused General Electric turbines that are typically found attached to Boeing airplanes. The company was quick to turn its attention to the possibility of using the jet engines to power data centers after it was identified that the demand for energy was outpacing the ability of traditional utility companies to keep up. Each turbine is capable of producing up to 50 megawatts of electricity. Normally, that would be enough to keep around 15,000 homes up and running.
The availability of energy has long been an issue for data centers, both existing and those still on the drawing board. A July 2026 report predicted that data centers would use 20% of all U.S. power by 2035, a figure that was a huge 83% increase over the same forecast that was made seven months prior. Despite that news, as of April this year, half of data center buildouts had been canceled or delayed due to, among other things, a lack of power. This is an issue for xAI especially, with Musk saying in August that xAI would increase its data center capacity by 7x before the end of 2027. Delays and cancelations have the potential to derail those plans.
Public sentiment around data centers has turned sour in recent months amid power issues and concerns over how much water these facilities use. While using converted jet engines could potentially help with one issue, it seems unlikely that the pollution they generate will help assuage the concerns of locals anytime soon.

articles.title: La UE autoriza la compra de la matriz de MediaMarkt por el gigante chino JD.com por 2.200 millones de euros
articles.text:
Si vives en España o en buena parte de Europa, seguramente conozcas MediaMarkt. Sus tiendas de electrónica, con esos característicos carteles rojos y blancos, forman parte del paisaje comercial de numerosas ciudades. Es fácil que alguna vez hayas entrado en una de ellas para comprar un móvil, un ordenador o simplemente echar un vistazo a las últimas novedades tecnológicas. Lo que probablemente te resulte menos familiar es el nombre de JD.com, un gigante chino del comercio electrónico que ahora está a punto de hacerse con el control de la empresa que está detrás de esas tiendas.
El paso decisivo ha llegado desde Bruselas. Este 3 de noviembre, la Comisión Europea ha autorizado, con condiciones, la adquisición de Ceconomy, el grupo alemán propietario de MediaMarkt y Saturn. La oferta, anunciada en julio de 2025, fijó un precio de 4,60 euros por acción y valoró la totalidad del capital en unos 2.200 millones de euros, aproximadamente 2.500 millones de dólares, una cifra que no equivale al desembolso efectivo del comprador. El visto bueno europeo despeja el último obstáculo regulatorio pendiente, pero no significa que la compra ya se haya completado. La compañía china espera cerrar la transacción a más tardar el 12 de noviembre.
Para entender el alcance de esta adquisición, conviene mirar más allá del nombre de MediaMarkt. Además de las cadenas mencionadas, Ceconomy opera en Italia bajo la marca MediaWorld, dentro de una red que supera los 1.000 establecimientos y emplea a unas 50.000 personas. En cuanto a la propiedad, JD.com ha asegurado mediante su oferta el 59,8% del capital por unos 1.300 millones de euros, mientras que Convergenta, vinculada a la familia fundadora, conservará un 25,35%. Gracias al acuerdo entre ambos accionistas, el grupo chino tendrá atribuidos los derechos de voto correspondientes a una participación conjunta del 85,2% tras el cierre de la operación.
Una expansión china bajo condiciones europeas
JD.com no es precisamente una empresa pequeña que busca abrirse camino fuera de China. Hablamos de uno de los grandes nombres del comercio electrónico del país asiático, con una importante infraestructura propia de almacenamiento y distribución. Su llegada al mercado europeo tampoco empieza con esta adquisición: en marzo de 2026 estrenó Joybuy en seis países del continente. Ahora, su interés por Ceconomy responde a una lógica comercial: complementar su experiencia en las ventas por internet y la logística con una red de establecimientos físicos que ya tiene presencia y reconocimiento entre los consumidores europeos.
La operación, sin embargo, también despertó inquietudes en Bruselas. La Comisión la examinó bajo el Reglamento sobre Subvenciones Extranjeras, una normativa que busca evitar que las ayudas procedentes de gobiernos de fuera de la UE distorsionen la competencia dentro del mercado comunitario. En su investigación identificó financiación preferente, incentivos fiscales y subvenciones recibidas por JD.com desde China, ayudas que habían contribuido al desarrollo de sus capacidades logísticas y tecnológicas. Según el organismo, estas ventajas podían reforzar la capacidad del grupo para financiar sus actividades y aplicar políticas de precios agresivas en perjuicio de otros competidores europeos.
Para obtener el visto bueno europeo, el comprador ha tenido que asumir una serie de compromisos. Entre ellos, garantizar que las operaciones económicas con Ceconomy, incluida la financiación, se realicen en condiciones de mercado, sin ventajas artificiales derivadas de las ayudas recibidas. También deberá ofrecer a otros minoristas sus servicios de almacenamiento y logística, y a terceros sus servicios tecnológicos, en las mismas condiciones que a su nueva filial. Estas obligaciones estarán vigentes durante diez años y un supervisor independiente vigilará su cumplimiento bajo la supervisión de la Comisión Europea. Con ellas, Bruselas busca impedir que las subvenciones extranjeras se traduzcan en ventajas competitivas indebidas dentro de Europa.
Para quienes compramos habitualmente en MediaMarkt, la pregunta es qué cambiará a partir de ahora. El acuerdo contempla mantener las marcas durante cinco años y establece, durante tres, restricciones a los despidos por causas operativas y al cierre de establecimientos impulsados por el comprador, aunque existen excepciones. JD.com también pretende aprovechar su infraestructura tecnológica y logística para ampliar la oferta de productos y mejorar los tiempos de entrega, objetivos cuyos resultados todavía están por verse. Lo que sí refleja esta operación es el interés del gigante chino por reforzar su presencia en el comercio europeo, esta vez apoyándose en una red de tiendas que los consumidores ya conocen.

articles.title: 5 Books you must add to your November 2026 reading list
articles.text:
5 Books you must add to your November 2026 reading list
Discover five books to add to your November 2026 reading list, from emotional literary fiction and romantic suspense to thought-provoking dystopian novels.
November is a wonderful time to discover new authors, explore different genres, and make room for stories that offer fresh perspectives.
Whether you enjoy emotional literary fiction, psychological suspense, thought-provoking dystopian novels, or stories about love and ambition, the right book can make your reading month memorable.
If you are planning your November 2026 reading list, these five books deserve your attention. Each offers a different reading experience, from complicated relationships and personal struggles to questions about technology, identity, and human connection.
5 Books worth adding to your reading list this November
1. The Correspondent by Virginia Evans
If you enjoy character-driven stories that explore relationships, memories, and the importance of communication, The Correspondent by Virginia Evans is an excellent choice.
The novel follows Sybil Van Antwerp, a retired lawyer who communicates with the people in her life through letters. Through her correspondence with family members, friends, and strangers, readers gradually discover her personality, complicated relationships, regrets, and experiences.
What makes the novel particularly interesting is its epistolary format. Instead of following a conventional narrative, the story unfolds through letters, allowing readers to understand the characters through their words and interactions.
The book explores ageing, forgiveness, grief, family connections, and the ways people make sense of their past.
Why should you read it?
If you enjoy emotionally layered stories that make you reflect on relationships and the things left unsaid, this book deserves a place on your November reading list. It is also a refreshing choice for readers who want to explore a storytelling format different from traditional novels.
2. Broken Country by Clare Leslie Hall
For readers who enjoy emotional storytelling combined with romance, family drama, and suspense, Broken Country by Clare Leslie Hall is a compelling choice.
The novel follows Beth, a woman living in the English countryside whose seemingly settled life is disrupted when Gabriel Wolfe, a man from her past, returns to her village with his young son.
His arrival brings back memories, unresolved feelings, and questions about the choices Beth made years earlier. As the story develops, a tragic incident changes everything and forces the characters to confront the consequences of their decisions.
One of the book's strongest elements is its exploration of love, loyalty, grief, and the complicated relationship between the past and the present.
Why should you read it?
If you enjoy emotionally intense stories with unexpected revelations, complicated relationships, and a touch of mystery, Broken Country is worth picking up. It is particularly suited to readers who love stories that keep them invested until the final pages.
3. The Dream Hotel by Laila Lalami
If you enjoy dystopian fiction that makes you question the future of technology and society, The Dream Hotel by Laila Lalami deserves a place on your reading list.
The novel imagines a world where technology has advanced to the point that people's dreams can be monitored and analysed. The story follows Sara, a woman whose private dreams become the basis for an algorithm's assessment of her potential risk to society.
As she finds herself caught in a system that questions her freedom and autonomy, the novel explores the frightening consequences of allowing technology to influence deeply personal aspects of human life.
Through its unsettling premise, Lalami raises important questions about privacy, surveillance, artificial intelligence, and the growing influence of algorithms on everyday decisions.
Why should you read it?
This book is an excellent choice for readers who enjoy speculative fiction with real-world relevance. If you are interested in technology, artificial intelligence, and questions about personal freedom, The Dream Hotel will give you plenty to think about.
4. Atmosphere by Taylor Jenkins Reid
Taylor Jenkins Reid is known for writing emotionally engaging novels with memorable characters, and Atmosphere is another compelling addition to her bibliography.
Set in the 1980s, the novel follows Joan Goodwin, an astronomy professor who joins NASA's space shuttle programme after pursuing an opportunity she has always dreamed about.
As Joan enters the demanding world of astronaut training, she encounters professional challenges, new relationships, and experiences that change how she understands ambition and love.
The novel explores the sacrifices involved in pursuing extraordinary dreams while examining the emotional connections that make life meaningful. It also highlights the experiences of women working in a field where they have historically been underrepresented.
Why should you read it?
If you enjoy stories about ambitious women, unexpected relationships, and the courage to pursue your dreams, Atmosphere is a wonderful choice. It combines the excitement of space exploration with an emotional story about identity, ambition, and love.
5. The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny by Kiran Desai
For readers who appreciate literary fiction that explores identity, family, culture, and belonging, The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny by Kiran Desai is a book worth considering.
The novel follows Sonia and Sunny, two young Indians whose lives unfold across different countries and cultures. As their paths intersect, the story explores their experiences with family expectations, relationships, migration, and the search for personal identity.
Through its characters, Desai examines the complicated relationship between individual ambitions and the expectations inherited from family and society.
The novel also explores loneliness and the desire to find a place where we feel understood. It raises questions about how our cultural backgrounds, relationships, and experiences influence the people we eventually become.
Why should you read it?
If you enjoy immersive literary fiction with complex characters and meaningful observations about society, this book deserves your attention. It is particularly appealing to readers interested in stories about belonging, cultural identity, and the complexities of human relationships.
Final thoughts
A good reading list should include stories that entertain you, challenge your thinking, and introduce you to perspectives you might not have considered before.
These five books offer something different for November 2026. The Correspondent explores relationships through letters, Broken Country combines romance with suspense, and The Dream Hotel examines the consequences of technological surveillance. Meanwhile, Atmosphere celebrates ambition and human connection, while The Loneliness of Sonia and Sunny explores identity, family, and belonging.
You do not necessarily have to read all five books in one month. Pick the one that matches your current reading mood, make time for a few pages every day, and enjoy discovering a new story.
Sometimes, the best way to end a month is with a book that leaves you thinking long after you have turned its final page.

articles.title: Cyberattaques IA : le pire serait encore à venir, alerte le Royaume-Uni
articles.text:
On peut dire que ces dernières semaines ont été très mouvementées dans le secteur de la cybersécurité. La découverte de deux failles critiques dans le langage informatique PHP a semé la panique au sein de l’Internet mondial, et la situation n’est toujours pas totalement réglée. Des cyberattaques ont par ailleurs ciblé des supermarchés à travers l’Europe, entraînant des montagnes de nourriture jetées. La liste des cyberattaques en France s’allonge quant à elle de jour en jour. Bref, la situation est tendue. Mais le pire est-il encore à venir ? C’est ce que craint le Centre national de cybersécurité britannique (NCSC).
Des craintes de cyberattaques envers des infrastructures critiques au Royaume-Uni
Le Centre national de cybersécurité britannique estime qu’il est « fort probable » que des attaques « de type ransomware », basées sur l’intelligence artificielle, soient menées contre les infrastructures critiques nationales [ICN] d’ici à 2028. Qu’entend-on par des infrastructures critiques nationales [ICN] ? La définition britannique des ICN fait référence à des installations et des services dans divers secteurs : énergie, transport, défense, alimentation, santé ou encore finance. Il serait donc question de cyberattaques menées notamment contre des centrales électriques, des infrastructures financières, des aéroports ou encore des hôpitaux du Royaume-Uni.
Pour rappel, le président du Financial Stability Board (FSB) avait déjà alerté sur l’émergence de modèles d’IA de pointe qui pourraient menacer la stabilité financière et la croissance économique mondiale. Notons que le Centre national de cybersécurité britannique alerte également sur le fait que les pirates russes et chinois commencent à utiliser « systématiquement » l’IA pour mener des cyberattaques.
L’intelligence artificielle rend certaines cyberattaques redoutables
C’est précisément l’intelligence artificielle qui pourrait permettre à des pirates de mener des cyberattaques d’une ampleur jamais vue auparavant, l’IA étant capable de détecter des failles jusqu’alors inconnues. Comme l’explique le Centre national de cybersécurité britannique, l’IA devrait rendre les attaques par ransomwares particulièrement redoutables en aidant les pirates à repérer des cibles, à localiser des failles et à écrire du code malveillant.
Tout l’enjeu est de savoir si les entreprises parviendront à se défendre face à ces menaces. L’agence britannique de cybersécurité appelle justement les entreprises et institutions à pouvoir accéder à des modèles d’intelligence artificielle de pointe afin de se protéger contre les cyberattaques basées sur l’IA. De son côté, Jason Clinton, cadre chargé de la cybersécurité chez Anthropic, a estimé que les perturbations que l’Internet mondial connaît actuellement allaient « fortement empirer avant de s’améliorer » dans environ 18 mois, notamment lorsque les failles découvertes par l’IA seront comblées. Il reste toutefois à voir si les systèmes de défense des entreprises et institutions parviendront bel et bien à suivre le rythme de perfectionnement des cyberattaques.
