articles.title: Synology : des pirates prennent vos fichiers en otage en exploitant des failles déjà corrigées
articles.text:
Des NAS Synology sont la cible d'une vague d'attaques par ransomware, qui chiffre les fichiers de leurs propriétaires et réclame plusieurs milliers de dollars pour leur restitution.
Depuis la mi-octobre, les témoignages d'internautes désemparés affluent sur les Reddit et autre forums d'entraide. Photos, documents personnels, sauvegardes professionnelles… Les fichiers qu'ils avaient confiés à leur NAS sont désormais illisibles, flanqués d’une note de rançon. Dans un communiqué publié le 29 octobre, Synology a confirmé les attaques et exhorté ses clients à mettre à jour leur système d'exploitation sans attendre.
C3RB3R, un ransomware qui n'en est pas à son coup d'essai
Sur les appareils compromis, les fichiers portent désormais l'extension .L0CK3D et s'accompagnent d'un document intitulé read-me3.txt. Les pirates y expliquent avoir chiffré les données et exigent l'achat de C3rb3r Decryptor, un logiciel de déchiffrement proposé sur un portail du dark web contre plusieurs milliers de dollars. Pour convaincre leurs victimes de payer, ils offrent même de restaurer gratuitement un fichier de leur choix.
Cet outil emprunte son nom à C3RB3R, également appelé CerberImposter. Déjà repéré sur des serveurs Atlassian Confluence et GitLab, il a été déployé par le passé dans des opérations exploitant des vulnérabilités connues. Cette fois, les cybercriminels ciblent des NAS Synology exécutant d'anciennes versions de DiskStation Manager (DSM), le système qui assure leur fonctionnement.
Les analyses divergent toutefois sur la façon dont les pirates parviennent à compromettre ces appareils. Synology évoque une vulnérabilité corrigée en décembre 2024, sans la nommer, et renvoie à un bulletin qui en recense trois. La plus grave, CVE-2024-10441 (CVSS 9,8/10), permet d'exécuter du code à distance sans authentification. Les équipes de 360, qui ont examiné des NAS infectés par C3RB3R, attribuent quant à elles les intrusions à deux autres failles critiques, CVE-2026-13639 et CVE-2026-13684, corrigées en septembre dernier.
On ne sait pas encore combien de NAS ont été infectés. Toujours est-il qu’au 1er novembre, Shadowserver recensait plus de 380 000 appareils Synology accessibles depuis Internet, dont près de 200 000 en Europe.
Mettre DSM à jour et sécuriser les accès distants
Face à ces attaques, Synology appelle les propriétaires de NAS à installer sans délai la dernière version de DSM compatible avec leur appareil et à activer les mises à jour automatiques. Une précaution qui concerne aussi les machines ayant reçu les correctifs de 2024, puisque les deux failles pointées par 360 n'ont été corrigées que récemment. Pour vérifier les mises à jour disponibles, il suffit de se rendre dans le Panneau de configuration de DSM, puis dans la rubrique « Mettre à jour et restaurer ».
Les utilisateurs et utilisatrices sont également invités à vérifier les accès ouverts sur Internet, à commencer par l'interface d'administration de DSM, qui ne devrait pas être directement accessible depuis l'extérieur. Cela suppose de contrôler les éventuelles redirections de ports configurées sur le routeur. Pour accéder à son NAS à distance, un VPN ou le service d'accès sécurisé du fabricant constitue une meilleure option. La désactivation du compte administrateur par défaut et l'activation de la double authentification peuvent compléter ces précautions.
Une sauvegarde indépendante, conservée hors ligne ou protégée contre les modifications, offre enfin une possibilité de récupération si les pirates parviennent malgré tout à chiffrer les données du NAS. Car une mise à jour installée après l'infection pourra corriger la vulnérabilité exploitée, mais ne permettra pas de déchiffrer les fichiers déjà pris en otage.

articles.title: OpenAI sumó a Magnite y PubMatic para vender los anuncios de ChatGPT que no logra colocar por su cuenta
articles.text:
OpenAI firmó acuerdos con las empresas de tecnología publicitaria Magnite y PubMatic para que vendan los espacios de anuncios de ChatGPT que la compañía no logra ocupar por su cuenta, según informó The Information. Los pactos no se habían anunciado públicamente.
Magnite y PubMatic operan plataformas que subastan en tiempo real el espacio publicitario de sitios web y aplicaciones. Ahora podrán ofrecer en esas subastas los anuncios sobrantes de ChatGPT, es decir, los que OpenAI no vendió mediante contratos directos con anunciantes.
Según el resumen que hizo Investing.com del reporte, los anunciantes podrán usar el software de ambas empresas para fijar presupuestos, hacer ofertas y subir sus piezas publicitarias directamente a ChatGPT. El sistema propio de OpenAI conserva el control de dónde y cuándo se muestra cada anuncio.
Un vocero de OpenAI dijo a The Information que los acuerdos hacen más fácil para los anunciantes “comprar y gestionar anuncios en ChatGPT con herramientas que ya usan”. La compañía no respondió con cifras sobre el alcance de los pactos.
Las acciones de ambas empresas subieron en Wall Street
El lunes 2 de noviembre, tras conocerse el reporte, las acciones de PubMatic subieron 4,5% y las de Magnite 5% en la operación bursátil, según Investing.com. El medio añadió que, de acuerdo con The Information, el volumen de transacciones que pasa por las dos empresas es por ahora modesto.
Las personas familiarizadas con los acuerdos, citadas por The Information, esperan que ese volumen crezca a medida que avance la integración técnica. Las condiciones económicas de los pactos no figuran entre los datos publicados en los resúmenes consultados.
Para los usuarios, el cambio no altera lo que ven en pantalla: según el reporte, OpenAI mantiene el control de la colocación y la entrega de los anuncios, y solo cambia el canal por el que los anunciantes los compran. Los acuerdos se suman a una estrategia que OpenAI no había planteado así en sus inicios.
Una red de socios publicitarios que crece
Magnite y PubMatic se suman a otros socios de publicidad de OpenAI. El reporte menciona acuerdos previos con Criteo, LiveRamp, StackAdapt y Amazon Ads, y señala que la compañía bajó los precios de sus anuncios y lanzó formatos conversacionales, en los que el usuario interactúa con la marca mediante texto.
OpenAI había abierto esa vía el 5 de mayo de 2026. Ese día informó en su sitio que los anunciantes podían crear anuncios en ChatGPT a través de socios o de un administrador de anuncios de autoservicio, en versión de prueba, y que sumaba la compra por clic.
En esa publicación, la empresa mencionó a las agencias Dentsu, Omnicom, Publicis y WPP, y a socios tecnológicos como Adobe, Criteo, Kargo, Pacvue y StackAdapt. También afirmó que los anuncios deben seguir siendo útiles, privados y estar claramente separados de las respuestas de ChatGPT.
OpenAI sostuvo entonces que los anunciantes reciben datos agregados sobre el rendimiento de las campañas, sin acceso a las conversaciones individuales ni a datos personales de los usuarios. La compañía no ha publicado un comunicado propio sobre los acuerdos con Magnite y PubMatic, según las fuentes consultadas.
La publicidad en ChatGPT: cómo funcionan los anuncios contextuales y quiénes los ven
En ChatGPT (a partir de su implementación en 2026), la publicidad funciona mediante anuncios altamente contextuales que aparecen en tarjetas claramente identificadas debajo de las respuestas de la IA, lo que garantiza que los anunciantes no puedan influir ni alterar las respuestas que genera el modelo.
El sistema analiza el contexto de tu conversación actual (y tus preferencias generales, si has habilitado la personalización) para mostrar recomendaciones relevantes de productos o servicios justo en el momento en que estás explorando ideas o tomando decisiones.
Las empresas gestionan sus campañas a través de una plataforma de autoservicio donde pueden pujar por clics o impresiones basándose en “pistas de contexto” en lugar de palabras clave exactas.
Finalmente, esta publicidad está dirigida de forma exclusiva a los usuarios de los planes gratuitos (Free y Go) para subsidiar el costo de la plataforma, mientras que los suscriptores de pago (Plus, Pro, Enterprise, etc.) mantienen una experiencia libre de anuncios, todo esto bajo el principio de que los chats privados nunca se comparten con las marcas.

articles.title: Hostinger Premium : 48 mois d’hébergement pour seulement 119,52 €
articles.text:
Black Friday Hostinger : 48 mois d’hébergement à 119,52 €, mais attention au renouvellement
Avec 80 % de réduction pour le Black Friday, Hostinger Premium passe à 2,49 €/mois sur quatre ans. Une offre intéressante pour créer un site et démarrer une activité en ligne.
Hostinger Premium : 119,52 € à payer pour quatre ans d’hébergement
Hostinger Premium est proposé à 2,49 €/mois pendant 48 mois, soit 119,52 € à régler en une seule fois. Affiché habituellement à 12,19 €/mois, le pack bénéficie d'une remise de 80 % à l'occasion du Black Friday. Une réduction qui permet de limiter les dépenses au lancement d'un site, notamment lorsqu'il s'agit de tester une activité commerciale sur Internet.
Le forfait donne accès à plusieurs outils pour construire et administrer une présence en ligne. Il autorise notamment la création de trois sites web, avec un nom de domaine offert pendant la première année. Le stockage SSD atteint 20 Go et des sauvegardes hebdomadaires sont également incluses. De quoi disposer d'une première base pour présenter une marque, publier des contenus ou commencer à vendre des produits.
Pour une boutique en ligne, Hostinger met aussi à disposition une solution e-commerce et un assistant IA dédié. Ce dernier peut accompagner la création de la boutique et faciliter certaines étapes de sa mise en place. La plateforme propose également plusieurs environnements de création :
●Créateur de sites IA : pour concevoir un site sans partir d'une page blanche.
●WordPress : pour profiter d'un système de gestion de contenu largement répandu.
●Node.js : pour développer des projets web dans cet environnement.
●Assistant IA e-commerce : pour accompagner la création de la boutique.
●Emailing IA : pour préparer et gérer des campagnes de communication.
Le pack comprend par ailleurs deux boîtes mail par site, gratuites pendant un an. Le support expert prioritaire reste accessible 24 h/24 et 7 j/7, un point appréciable lorsqu'un problème technique survient au moment de mettre un site en ligne.
Une offre à anticiper avant de souscrire
Le tarif de 2,49 €/mois mérite toutefois d'être replacé dans la durée. Les 119,52 € sont prélevés dès la souscription pour couvrir les 48 mois. À l'issue de cette période, le renouvellement automatique est annoncé à 9,99 €/mois pour une nouvelle durée de 48 mois. La résiliation reste possible à tout moment.
La garantie satisfait ou remboursé de 30 jours laisse également une période pour découvrir la plateforme et ses outils. Cependant, les besoins doivent être évalués avant de s'engager sur quatre ans, notamment si la boutique prévoit de gérer rapidement un catalogue important ou un trafic élevé.
Au final, Hostinger Premium constitue une porte d'entrée abordable pour lancer un premier site marchand ou développer une petite activité en ligne. Son tarif promotionnel permet de maîtriser le budget d'hébergement pendant quatre ans, avec plusieurs outils de création et d'administration réunis dans une même interface.

articles.title: Apple faces unprecedented memory cost increases as RAM prices continue to surge, manufacturing bill climbs by $33 billion — rising component expenses threaten margins through the holiday quarter and into 2027
articles.text:
Apple faces unprecedented memory cost increases as RAM prices continue to surge, manufacturing bill climbs by $33 billion — rising component expenses threaten margins through the holiday quarter and into 2027
AI demand is tightening DRAM and NAND supply, pushing up costs for device makers and leaving less memory available for consumer electronics
Apple is about to feel the squeeze from rising memory prices, with the cost of RAM climbing just as the company heads into its busiest shopping season. According to Reuters, Apple expects to pay more for memory in the December quarter, with the CEO, John Ternus, describing the current price increases as “unprecedented. The company has so far managed to soften the blow by using memory bought at lower prices, cutting costs elsewhere and raising prices on some products. However, it is reported that its manufacturing bill has climbed by $33 billion in just a few months.
But that cushion is getting thinner, and Apple expects memory purchases to become even more expensive into 2027. “What we're seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented. And as we said earlier in the September quarter, we did see higher memory costs as compared to the June quarter, which were partly offset by the benefit of carrying inventory and lower costs on certain non-memory components. Now for the December quarter, we expect even higher memory costs, partly offset by a few factors. So as you know, we changed the price on many of our products, including Mac and iPad at the end of June and iPhone in September, and these price increases provided some offset.” Ternus said during Apple’s November 2 earnings call.
Memory is used across Apple's hardware lineup, so sustained price increases could affect manufacturing cost for several product categories—although Apple has not announced another round of price increases. Absorbing higher components could, however, indefinitely become difficult. Dave Nicholson, Chief Research Officer at the Futurum Group, also identified memory prices as a growing pressure point for Apple's margins and hardware pricing through the holiday season and into 2027. According to him, Apple is in a different position from companies pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into AI data center infrastructure. The impact of higher component costs is easier to quantify than the eventual returns on massive AI capital expenditure, he said.
And the warnings from Apple's suppliers suggest that the cost pressure is unlikely to ease quickly. Last month, Samsung, a major supplier of RAM(DRAM), NAND flash storage and OLED displays for Apple, said that memory demand would far exceed supply as AI infrastructure continues to expand. Its memory division also reported a quarter-on-quarter increase in DRAM average prices during the third quarter, while NAND prices rose by high-teen percentages. Senior executive vice president of its memory business warned the supply crunch could extend to 2028 and beyond. Elsewhere, SK Hynix delivered a similar warning, saying it had secured long-term agreements covering more than Half of its production capacity for2027 and 2028. Micron, the third major supplier for Apple aside from Samsung and SK Hynix, is also benefiting from the surging demand for memory. Its latest published outlook warns that supply shortages in memory and storage could take “considerable time” to improve.
We have previously reported several signs of the pressure now confronting Apple. In January, the company was already scrambling to secure memory supplies amid strong demand, with then CEO Tim Cook warning that rising prices could have a greater impact on earnings. By June, rising component expenses had translated into higher retail prices. Apple increased prices across several Mac and iPad models, including a $400 increase to the starting price of the MacBook Pro, due to the RAM crisis. In July, Cook described the memory market as a “hundred-year-flood” and said Apple expected to pay more for memory in the September quarter. The company had also increased its inventory to $11.09 billion as it built a buffer against supply and price pressures.

articles.title: Researchers warned of North Korean hacking tactics years before record $6.3B Binance heist | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Crypto giant Binance says North Korean hackers used fake social media profiles and the lure of a potential job offer as part of a months-long scheme aimed at tricking an employee into downloading malicious software onto their laptop.
Researchers have repeatedly warned about long-running social engineering attacks that can go on for months.
This latest attack allowed the hackers to patiently worm their way into Binance’s systems to steal a record $6.3 billion in crypto last week, the company has now confirmed. The hack, disclosed in an updated statement posted on X on Tuesday, prompted the world’s largest crypto exchange to suspend customer withdrawals across its network.
The FBI and blockchain investigators have blamed North Korea for the heist. The country has been long accused of carrying out massive cryptocurrency thefts in recent years to fund its internationally sanctioned nuclear weapons program.
In its latest statement, Binance said that North Korean hackers, posing as recruiters hiring for a job, contacted a software engineer who works on wallets at the company. Following two interviews with the purported company, the engineer was instructed to download an apparent coding assignment as part of the interview process. When opened, the assignment contained malicious code that compromised the engineer’s work-issued laptop. Binance said its security tools did not detect the malware.
That foothold in Binance’s network allowed the hackers to access an internal tool capable of taking over the work computers of two other engineers on the wallet team. One of those engineers had unwittingly downloaded a tampered app containing password-stealing malware months earlier after searching for the software in search engine results. While Binance replaced that compromised engineer’s laptop, the hackers used the engineer’s stolen credentials to break into the computer of a third engineer, whose job allowed them access to systems capable of controlling billions of dollars in crypto.
Binance said the attack “should not have happened,” and that it had improved its network security following the theft.
The hack underscores an ongoing tactic in the North Korean regime’s repertoire of attacks targeting the crypto industry and high-net worth individuals. Researchers have warned for years that North Korean hackers pose as venture capitalists, investors, and recruiters using dossiers of stolen American identities to trick employees into granting access to their systems.
These attacks are widely known across the crypto industry and have been the subject of repeated warnings from the U.S. government and cybersecurity giants in recent years. Some half of all intrusions at U.S. tech companies last year were attributed to North Koreans posing as remote IT workers and fake recruiters.
By Binance’s own account, the company faced at least 57 suspected attacks from North Korea, which it said reflect the “persistent threat posed by state-sponsored actors targeting the cryptocurrency industry.”
But how the hackers were able to convince the engineer into downloading malware given the highly publicized threat, and bypass security weaknesses in Binance’s own network, will likely be the focus of investigators’ attention.
While the case exposes how North Korean hackers use social engineering, such as offers of employment, to trick employees into granting access to their systems, it’s ultimately the responsibility of the company to ensure its systems cannot run unauthorized or untrusted software that could cause a compromise.
Binance spokesperson Ross O’Leary referred to the company’s public statement but declined to answer TechCrunch’s questions on the record about the incident. Those questions included how Binance prevents unauthorized or malicious code from running on its employees’ laptops, if at all, and whether any third parties had performed cybersecurity audits of Binance’s network prior to the hack.
The company said it would bring in cybersecurity experts to review the incident and has put new security measures in place to prevent a repeat incident.
The heist remains the largest theft of crypto in history.

articles.title: Exclusive: Cogent Security’s VR-1.1 model outscores Claude Code and Codex on vulnerability repair - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: Cogent Security’s VR-1.1 model outscores Claude Code and Codex on vulnerability repair
Vulnerability management startup Cogent Security Inc. today released VR-1.1, a new version of its frontier reasoning model that writes fixes for newly disclosed software vulnerabilities.
On a public repair benchmark, the model outscored Anthropic PBC’s Claude Code and OpenAI Group PBC’s Codex.
The release goes after the part of vulnerability management that has not sped up. In July, research group Epoch Artificial Intelligence Inc. counted about 2,500 high- and critical-severity disclosures from major organizations, roughly five times the monthly record set before Anthropic announced Claude Mythos Preview in April.
Each repair still needs an engineer who understands the flaw well enough to change the code without breaking something else. Co-founder and Chief Executive Vineet Edupuganti called that stage “where security teams are stuck.”
To test the model on that repair work, Cogent turned to LiveCVEBench. Researchers at Harbin Institute of Technology and Kuaishou Technology built the benchmark from vulnerabilities disclosed in recent months and add new ones regularly. VR-1.1 produced a working repair for 57.9% of the benchmark’s 190 tasks. Claude Code and Codex tied at 45.3%.
Each task drops an agent into a real development environment with a vulnerability report and the affected codebase, in one of 14 programming languages. To pass, a patch has to close the vulnerability without breaking the software, which the benchmark checks with separate security and functionality tests.
Cogent blocked outbound network access during repairs and hid the grading tests until each agent was done. Inference budgets differed across the three systems, according to the full methodology Cogent Research has published.
Where the environment allows, VR-1.1 starts by writing its own proof of concept that triggers the reported flaw. From there the model follows the vulnerability through the affected code, including related paths that share the same weakness. The fix itself stays small, for example checking an index before use.
Every patch goes to a separate review that starts from a fresh context and hunts for a way around the fix. New bugs introduced by the change are part of that check. The model also leaves behind regression tests, which fail if a later code change reopens the flaw. When an attempt fails, the diagnosis and failure details carry into the next try.
“A patch might block the exact payload from a bug report, but leave the same vulnerability open via a different endpoint or break core functionality for users,” said Geng Sng, co-founder and chief technology officer of Cogent. “We designed VR-1.1 to check its own work for both problems before it finishes.”
Cogent introduced VR-1 in July to find and prove the attack paths an adversary could reach inside an enterprise. The new release extends the remediation capabilities that model introduced.
Founded in 2025, the company sells artificial intelligence agents that detect and fix vulnerabilities, with customers choosing whether a human signs off on each change. According to Cogent, Fortune 500 users have cut the exposure window for critical vulnerabilities by 97%.
Greylock Partners backed its $11 million launch round in July 2025, and Bain Capital Ventures led the $42 million Series A in February that took total funding to $53 million.

articles.title: Macronix Adds Hardware Security to NOR Flash Ahead of EU CRA - EE Times
articles.text:
The European Union’s Cyber Resilience Act (CRA), which becomes mandatory in December 2027, is raising the bar for cybersecurity in connected devices. Rather than relying on software patches to address vulnerabilities after they emerge, manufacturers are under growing pressure to build security into products from the outset. For connected devices, that shift puts flash memory in a new role: alongside storing code and data, it must help protect device identity, data integrity and software updates.
Donald Huang, director of product marketing and cybersecurity manager at Macronix International, said software updates alone cannot adequately address threats such as physical attacks and the interception or manipulation of communications. The CRA’s Security by Design principle calls for protection to be built into products from the earliest stages of development, extending a hardware root of trust (ROT) beyond the processor and into storage components.
Donald Huang, director of product marketing and cybersecurity manager at Macronix International
Why Security Must Extend Beyond Software
Securely Update Millions of DevicesThe CRA sets requirements for secure product design, protection of critical assets, and identity and supply-chain authentication. Manufacturers must ensure that components are trustworthy and that keys, code and data are protected from the beginning of the design process. Products must also be built to withstand cyberattacks at the system level. These requirements are putting the hardware ROT, which combines physical protection with cryptographic authentication, in the spotlight.
As Huang explained, attackers have several ways to get around software-based defenses. They can manipulate voltage, temperature or clock signals to launch physical attacks, tap the bus between flash memory and the host to intercept data, or replay previously valid commands. Security measures confined to software leave potential entry points in the hardware and communication interfaces.
Macronix developed its ArmorFlash family to address these threats by building security functions directly into NOR flash. Huang noted that the company introduced its security memory portfolio in 2019, embedding security into the storage architecture instead of relying on a separate security chip alongside conventional flash.
A conventional design pairs standard NOR flash with a separate secure element (SE), requiring additional hardware and an interface between the SE and the system-on-chip (SoC). ArmorFlash takes a different approach, integrating a secure engine, authentication functions and security protocols into the flash device itself. It connects to the host through a standard Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) and provides both general-purpose storage and a configurable secure area.
The integrated approach can also ease the addition of security to existing products. Because redesigning an established system’s SoC and circuitry can be costly and disruptive, ArmorFlash uses a standard SPI interface and pin-compatible design to add hardware security without extensive circuit changes. This can reduce both the hardware cost and the design complexity associated with a separate secure element.
ArmorFlash Combines Secure Boot, PUF and Data Protection
Macronix offers several products to address different security needs. For instance, ArmorBoot (MX76) supports secure boot, while ArmorFlash (MX75/MX78) provides data security.
The ArmorBoot MX76 verifies the integrity of boot code stored in flash when a system starts up, helping prevent code tampering and unauthorized execution. The same protection can extend to over-the-air (OTA) updates: before new code runs, the system verifies its source and integrity. A recovery mechanism can then restore a secure version if an update or startup process encounters an abnormal condition.
The MX78 ArmorFlash focuses on protecting data and communications. It supports multiple independent data regions, each associated with a root key, with access controls configurable for ordinary reads, authenticated reads or encrypted reads. A 128-Mbit device, for example, can be divided into 32 independent 4-Mbit regions, allowing access privileges to be separated at the storage level.
The MX78 also supports encryption of host access requests and message authentication using mechanisms such as Hash-based Message Authentication Code (HMAC). These features help guard against data and command exposure through bus snooping. Its monotonic counter, which can only increment, also helps prevent rollback attacks during OTA updates by blocking the reuse of older software versions or commands.
Another key technology in ArmorFlash is the physically unclonable function (PUF), which gives each chip a unique fingerprint. A PUF derives distinctive identification information and keys from minute physical and electrical variations that naturally occur during chip manufacturing. Beyond device authentication, it can help bind hardware to a host by establishing a cryptographic relationship between the flash device and an authorized SoC.
ArmorFlash also incorporates physical defenses. An active metal shield and environmental tamper-detection sensors monitor conditions such as voltage surges, temperature changes and clock anomalies. When abnormal conditions are detected, the device can trigger protective responses to help reduce the risk of physical probing and other attacks.
Automotive Qualification Opens Doors for Secure Flash
Automotive and industrial systems are among the main markets for secure flash, where reliability and long-term product support are essential. The ArmorFlash family meets AEC-Q100 Grade 1 automotive reliability requirements and has passed ISO 26262 ASIL D functional safety and ISO/SAE 21434 automotive cybersecurity standards. It also supports compliance with FIPS 140-2/140-3 cryptographic module requirements.
Huang said ArmorFlash is in mass production, with cumulative shipments exceeding several million units. The devices have been adopted in autonomous driving and advanced driver-assistance systems development platforms from multiple major international companies. Demand could expand beyond automotive as networking and communications equipment place greater emphasis on device identity, data protection and secure updates. Other potential applications requiring long-term data protection include medical equipment, financial services, digital rights management, and AI systems.
With the EU CRA deadline approaching, connected-device manufacturers face the challenge of adding hardware-level protection to existing designs while meeting the requirements for access to the European market. By combining high-performance storage, a secure engine and chip-level trust mechanisms in a single device, Macronix aims to offer a more cost-effective way to strengthen the security of existing systems and support their transition toward zero-trust architectures.
As connected-device security requirements evolve, the integration of hardware protection and nonvolatile memory (NVM) is becoming more consequential. Macronix will showcase its latest NVM technologies and application solutions at electronica 2026, taking place in Munich, Germany, from November 10 to 13. The portfolio will cover automotive electronics and edge AI, including security Flash technologies. Macronix will exhibit at Hall C5, Stand 279.

articles.title: Google Warns LLMjacking Attacks Are Costing Some Enterprises Up to $1 Million in Cloud Charges
articles.text:
Google on Monday warned that threat actors are hijacking enterprise access to Large Language Models (LLMs) to fraudulently leverage expensive computing resources and AI services.
The tactic is called LLMjacking, a form of resource hijacking adapted for the LLM era, where an attacker obtains an API key through phishing, source code leaks, misconfigured environments, or exposed client-side code to gain unauthorized access to an organization's LLM accounts, while the legitimate owner covers the consumption costs.
Such attacks have a wide geographical footprint, with impacted entities located in North America, South America, and Asia Pacific across the financial services, retail, technology, and transportation sectors.
"Unlike the gradual resource consumption associated with cryptojacking, LLMJacking can generate large spikes in fraudulent cloud charges in a matter of hours," Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant said in a report shared with The Hacker News.
"Across individual incidents, we observed fraudulent charges associated with resource consumption exceeding $100,000 USD in a single day, with cumulative charges at some organizations reaching $1 million USD before access was revoked."
On one end of the spectrum are low-level resource theft that involves the manipulation of customer support chatbots to conduct unauthorized tasks like code generation. LLMjacking is on the other end, as they target the backend model resources directly by identifying publicly exposed LLM endpoints or obtaining valid LLM API keys.
The most common initial access vector has been exposed or stolen cloud identity tokens, including IAM credentials, Service Account keys, GitHub Personal Access Tokens (PATs), and active session tokens, which allow an attacker to establish an initial foothold into target organizations' infrastructure.
This includes a threat actor called UNC6993, which is said to have breached a cloud instance through a misconfigured Service Account key and used it to obtain access to an LLM API.
"UNC6993 also hosted a session hijacking page masquerading as an application portal to join a group of LLM users," Google said. "This page tricks users into navigating to the legitimate LLM service website, and pasting their raw JSON payload containing an active access token, which was then posted to the backend API to bypass password and multi-factor authentication (MFA) controls."
In another case, an unknown attacker has been observed leveraging a stolen Personal Access Token to access private code repositories, following it up with the exploitation of a suspected web application vulnerability in a package running within a containerized cloud environment.
Other initial access routes include the compromise of IAM credentials of corporate users to programmatically generate fresh access keys to bypass MFA safeguards, as well as the use of a hacked cloud Service Account key with broad project permissions and LLM API keys obtained from public GitHub repositories.
Upon successfully gaining a foothold, the threat actors waste no time escalating privileges, burrowing deeper into the network, establishing persistence, and conducting internal reconnaissance to identify targets and further cloud credentials for lateral movement.
Some of the observed tactics are listed below -
- Enumerate cloud services, code repositories, and data stores for sensitive credentials.
- Perform internal reconnaissance across multiple cloud regions to map available services and identity policies.
- Clone sensitive codebases to search for hard-coded secrets, configuration variables, and developer credentials.
- Scan access logs to identify credentials for secondary cloud environments.
- Run targeted database queries to harvest additional credentials.
- Abuse cloud identity permissions and virtual machine configurations to escalate privileges and maintain persistent access.
- Exploit token-creation privileges associated with service accounts to generate temporary credentials for high-privilege service accounts and exfiltrate infrastructure credentials, internal database passwords, and third-party API keys from cloud secret managers.
- Create unauthorized IAM and service accounts and inject SSH keys into compute instances for persistence.
- Create backdoor service accounts disguised as internal billing optimization utilities.
- Exploit vulnerabilities targeting LLM routing software, such as CVE-2026-40217 in LiteLLM, to escalate privileges.
"The ultimate objective of LLMJacking is the monetization and resource-hijacking of foundation models, which actors achieve through token proxying, automated model streaming, and GPU hardware provisioning," Google said. "Threat actors also leveraged their access to host their own proxy endpoints and agentic workloads."
UNC6993, for instance, has created additional API keys to scale their operations within victim cloud projects, racking up over $100,000 USD in billing charges. Some threat actors attempt to bypass rate limits by adopting a "burn and rotate" strategy that involves continuously creating and deleting short-lived service accounts
The maturation of the LLMjacking ecosystem has also paved the way for the emergence of a new category of actors called LLM Mixers, highlighting a division of labor between attackers who establish initial access and those who manage downstream monetization infrastructure.
LLM Mixers function as illicit routing gateways that proxy, aggregate, and resell unauthorized LLM access to other criminal actors via underground storefronts. One such service is Jet Night ("jet-night[.]com"), which offers an unlimited token plan with alleged access to a frontier model for approximately $60 per month.
By fueling an illicit resale marketplace, it permits bad actors to siphon enterprise quotas while passing the billing costs to victims before compromises are detected.
Jet Night is far from the only token routing offering. According to a report published by Broadcom-owned Symantec and Carbon Black last week, there exists a grey market relay service that installs the genuine OpenAI Codex and Anthropic Claude Code CLIs on enterprise systems, only to reconfigure them to route every request through third-party infrastructure instead of the vendors' own servers.
The service is assessed to be active since at least early 2026, primarily impacting a dozen organizations located in Mainland China, along with multi-national subsidiaries based in South Korea, Taiwan, and Malaysia. Targeted sectors include industrial automation, electronics manufacturing, semiconductors, pharmaceuticals, shipping, tire manufacturing, petrochemicals, and data center services.
"Rather than building its own client software, the service repurposes the genuine CLI tools," Symantec said. "It installs them normally, then rewrites their configuration to switch sandboxing off, in Codex's case by setting it to 'danger-full-access,' and routes every request through its own servers instead of OpenAI's or Anthropic's."
The service appears to mainly target markets where Anthropic and OpenAI do not operate, with the installation driven by an employee attempting to try out a Western AI coding assistant by turning to an unauthorized reseller.
Notably, the service does not distribute a modified or trojanized client. Shortly after the legitimate install of the Codex or Claude Code CLI through npm, users are likely instructed to run a one-line command to fetch fileless PowerShell or bash setup script from a lookalike domain ("vibe.aiok[.]me") that's used to override the configuration.
The reconfiguration, which targets "~/.codex/config.toml" for Codex or "~/.claude/settings.json" for Claude Code, disables the CLI's execution sandbox, enables network access for the write sandbox, replaces the user's real API credentials with relay-issued tokens, and disables telemetry and error reporting.
The script also checks the Windows locale setting to confirm it's running on a system in the region it serves before the setup is completed. It's suspected that the operators behind the service are not only circumventing regional restrictions imposed by Western AI vendors, but are also reselling capacity below market rates similar to Jet Night.
Although there is no evidence to suggest that the service is abusing its position to harvest prompts entered by employees or fabricate or alter responses, the findings demonstrate the security risks associated with using such tools.
"Threat actors will increasingly prioritize LLMJacking over traditional resource theft like cryptojacking, driven by the immediate, high-margin monetization enabled by emerging underground LLM Mixers," Google said.
"As enterprises integrate higher-tier models and agentic workflows into production environments, cybercriminals will likely refine automated reconnaissance to target exposed API tokens and exploit vulnerabilities in model routing middleware."

articles.title: Apple's new Siri AI isn't going to be unlimited — and you'll eventually have to pay to use more of it
articles.text:
Apple confirms plans to charge for expanded Siri AI access — so how much of its new AI will you actually get for free?
You'll have to pay to get the full Siri AI experience
- Apple might place usage limits on Siri AI in the future, with the option to pay for expanded access
- What the cost will be or how pricing will be structured remains to be seen
- On-device inference will still be free, but the heavier tasks such as AI image editing would likely count towards your daily usage limit
In the Apple earnings call for Q4 2026, new CEO John Ternus joined CFO Kevan Parekh and COO Sabih Khan to discuss the results of the previous quarter. Within the discussion the trio quietly confirmed that Siri AI may soon have usage limits.
Now, we’ve put Siri AI through its paces and found it to be a remarkably good life assistant across Apple’s fleet of devices after years of Siri directing tricky questions to ChatGPT. But a usage limit could seriously hinder the effectiveness of your Apple assistant.
Those looking to use Siri as their go-to resource for AI answers and make full use of Apple’s AI photo editing features will have to pay for expanded access. So far, there are no details on how much users will have to fork up at each iCloud+ tier to make full use of Siri AI.
Server-side inference could raise costs
“The mix of [on-device and cloud Siri] is very early days, and so it's hard to predict exactly what the mix of those costs are going to look like,” Parekh explained. “Obviously, on device, you know, it's very very efficient. No real costs associated with that. But on the server side, we have some inference costs.”
Siri AI has had a somewhat limited rollout, being released mid-September in English as part of the iOS 27 update. Siri AI runs on a mix of on-device and Private Cloud Compute, so until Apple gets to grips with how much demand they might expect from Siri AI users the costs aren’t really known.
“I think again, we've just recently launched it and made it available to more users,” Parekh added. “And so we're in the very very early stages of understanding the kind of mix of those costs, as well as further requirements we might have on the compute side.”
Obviously there is some reasoning behind Apple’s decision to use Private Cloud Compute for some tasks. Given that your phone holds some pretty sensitive personal information that Siri AI may need to access, Private Cloud Compute offers a way to process that data in an anonymized, privacy-focused format.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Much of Siri AI’s inference happens on-device, but tasks that exceed the resource restrictions of an iPhone can be offloaded onto Private Cloud Compute. But with that comes processing costs that Apple has to cover.
“As far as agentic capabilities, you know, we think these are promising tools for users,” Tetanus said. “We just want to make sure that users are aware of what they're giving access to. We want to make sure this is done in a way that protects security and privacy.”
“You know, whether it's your contacts, your communications, health data, financial data, all of that, and Siri can tap into that and help you access it in a way that's very secure and private, and that nobody else has access to.”
What will you actually get for free?
As far as using Siri AI for free goes, light tasks that run on-device should remain accessible to all users. But if you have a more complex task or want to make use of Apple’s AI image editing features that need to be performed on more robust hardware, you could end up hitting the daily usage limit.
As Apple disclosed in the footnotes of the Siri AI release, the use of Apple’s cloud models specifically is what will count towards the usage limit. “Daily limits may vary by feature, request complexity, system demand, system policies, and other factors. Expanded access to such features will be available for a fee in the future.”
What these costs look like remains to be seen, but just drafting an email or asking Siri to find a video your friend mentioned in a message a few days ago shouldn’t be too much of an issue.
However, be aware of utilizing any features that require the use of Apple’s AFM 3 Cloud models moving forward, such as the intelligent photo editing tools and Image Playground.

articles.title: India's data centre capacity set for 5x surge by 2030: Crisil
articles.text:
India's data centre capacity set for 5x surge by 2030: Crisil
The growth of data centres in India will also depend on factors like timely power supply, regulatory clearances and project execution capabilities.
India's data centre industry is poised for an unprecedented investment boom, with installed capacity expected to increase five-fold to around 7.5 gigawatts (GW) by March 2030, attracting investments of more than Rs 3 lakh crore over the next four financial years, Crisil Ratings said in a report on Tuesday.
The expansion, fuelled by generative artificial intelligence (GenAI), enterprise digitalisation and rising data consumption, is set to transform the country's digital infrastructure landscape.
However, the industry's ability to translate demand into sustainable returns will depend critically on timely power connectivity, regulatory clearances and disciplined project execution.
"Nearly half of the upcoming capacity is already committed under long-term contracts, limiting speculative development and reducing offtake risk," Crisil Ratings said. "Upfront tie-ups with hyperscalers, driven by cloud adoption and compute-intensive GenAI workloads, provide revenue certainty from the outset. This helps de-risk projects, even as the scale and speed of the planned build-out intensify execution requirements."
Strong demand from global hyperscalers, driven by cloud adoption and increasingly compute-intensive GenAI workloads, is also supporting investment decisions and reducing offtake uncertainty.
India's competitive cost structure is adding to its appeal as a data centre destination. Development costs are around 20 per cent lower than in several competing Asia-Pacific markets, reflecting relatively competitive land, construction and labour costs. Combined with lower power tariffs, this enables rental rates to be 30-35 per cent below those in peer markets. The availability of large campuses powered by renewable energy also strengthens India's proposition for hyperscalers seeking to meet sustainability commitments.
Says Anand Kulkarni, Director, Crisil Ratings, "India's structural cost advantages further strengthen its attractiveness as a data centre destination. Development costs are around one-fifth lower than in several competing Asia-Pacific markets owing to more competitive land, construction and labour costs.”
He further said, “Combined with lower power tariffs, this translates into rentals that are 30-35 per cent lower than in peer markets. The ability to develop large, renewable-powered campuses also aligns well with the sustainability goals of hyperscalers, reinforcing India's competitive positioning."
However, the scale of the planned expansion is placing considerable pressure on power infrastructure. Nearly three-fourths of the approximately 6 GW of upcoming capacity is expected to be concentrated in Visakhapatnam, Mumbai and Hyderabad, Crisil said.
By fiscal 2030, data centre capacity in these cities could be equivalent to around 80%, 60% and 20%, respectively, of their current peak electricity demand. This concentration makes timely grid connectivity and transmission capacity augmentation critical to avoiding commissioning delays and cost overruns.

articles.title: Windows fica até 40% mais rápido em PCs com 8 GB de RAM • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Windows fica até 40% mais rápido em PCs com 8 GB de RAM
Atualização do Windows 11 diminui alocação de dados no armazenamento e economiza até 900 MB em cenário de uso intenso.
A Microsoft segue tentando otimizar o Windows 11 para máquinas com apenas 8 GB de RAM. Uma nova atualização reduz o consumo de memória e diminui a necessidade de recorrer ao SSD ou HD quando vários programas estão abertos ao mesmo tempo.
Segundo Pavan Davuluri, chefe da divisão de Windows e Dispositivos, os ajustes deixaram algumas interações do sistema até 20% mais rápidas e melhoraram em até 40% a alternância entre tarefas pesadas nos testes da empresa.
As tentativas de otimização no Windows, que é constantemente criticado por isso, ocorrem num momento de crise na indústria de componentes eletrônicos. Com a expansão de data centers para empresas de inteligência artificial, o foco do setor de semicondutores tem sido alimentá-los, destinando maior parte da capacidade produtiva para chips usados nos servidores.
Enquanto isso, peças chegam ao consumidor cada vez mais caras: o preço de memórias DDR5 saltou cerca de 500% entre 2025 e 2026, limitando a montagem de PCs com mais RAM.
Boa parte das mudanças está na forma como o Windows administra o esgotamento de memória disponível. Quando a RAM fica cheia, o sistema precisa transferir parte dos dados temporários para SDD ou HD, que são mais lentos e diminuem o desempenho na execução de programas.
A Microsoft afirma ter ajustado o algoritmo de compressão do Windows especialmente para computadores com 8 GB de RAM, mantendo até 2 GB adicionais de dados ativos na memória, comprimindo informações em segundo plano antes de recorrer ao armazenamento.
Nos testes internos, ações como abrir o menu Iniciar ou carregar o Explorador de Arquivos ficaram até 20% mais rápidas em comparação com uma compilação do Windows 11 de janeiro desde ano.
A atualização também otimizou o consumo de apps de terceiros. Em outro teste que simulava uma rotina mais pesada, a Microsoft diz ter diminuído o comprometimento da memória em até 900 MB. No caso, foram abertas 20 abas no Edge, um vídeo em 4K, documentos grandes no Word, Excel e Powerpoint e outras atividades.
Os Widgets também deixaram de ser carregados antecipadamente em computadores com essa configuração de memória, consumindo recursos apenas quando aberto pelo usuário.
Outro foco da atualização foi diminuir o tempo para que uma aba no navegador Edge seja considerada inativa. O programa passa a colocá-las em suspensão após 15 minutos, contra as duas horas de antes. Nesses casos, vale lembrar, a página continua aberta, mas reduz o consumo de recursos.
O Microsoft Teams também ativa o Modo de Eficiência por padrão em computadores com 8 GB de RAM. Segundo a empresa, o app passa a iniciar até 20% mais rápido e reduz o uso do processador, podendo reduzir automaticamente a resolução da câmera, por exemplo, para preservar a qualidade de outros recursos durante uma videochamada.
As otimizações fazem parte do Windows 11 26H2, compilação 26300.9818 ou posterior. Para verificar se a versão está disponível, o usuário pode acessar o painel de atualizações em Windows Update, nas Configurações do sistema.
Alguns dos ganhos também dependem de versões atualizadas dos apps. No caso do navegador, é preciso usar o Microsoft Edge 150 ou posterior.
A empresa afirma que continuará trabalhando para diminuir o consumo de RAM no Windows e prevê, no futuro, melhorias na Busca e aplicativos como OneDrive e Fotos.

articles.title: Samsung devrait bientôt lancer ses premières lunettes connectées, mais l’Europe va devoir patienter
articles.text:
En juillet dernier, lors de l’événement Unpacked 2026, Samsung a dévoilé ses premières lunettes connectées. Pour rappel, ces lunettes connectées, sans écran, intègrent une caméra, des haut-parleurs et des micros pour discuter avec Gemini. Elles tournent sous Android XR et disposent du processeur Snapdragon AR1 Gen 1 de Qualcomm. Autant dire que les premières lunettes connectées du géant sud-coréen sont très attendues. Bonne nouvelle : elles devraient être commercialisées bientôt. Moins bonne nouvelle : l’Europe, et donc la France, ne seraient pas concernées. En réalité, les premières lunettes connectées signées Samsung seraient lancées dans seulement deux pays. Du moins, dans un premier temps.
Un lancement seulement dans deux pays
Certaines rumeurs avaient évoqué une date de lancement pour l’automne 2026. Selon le média sud-coréen Chosun Biz, les premières lunettes connectées de Samsung sortiront finalement à la mi-décembre. Bonne nouvelle, leur lancement serait donc pour bientôt. Cependant, ce lancement concernerait seulement deux pays : la Corée du Sud et les États-Unis. Les Américains et les Sud-coréens devraient donc avoir l’opportunité de placer les premières lunettes connectées de Samsung sous le sapin. L’Europe devra quant à elle attendre. En effet, un responsable du secteur a expliqué au média Chosun Biz que Samsung veut étudier la demande et les retours des premiers utilisateurs avant de considérer un lancement sur d’autres marchés.
Pour rappel, Samsung a d’abord commercialisé son casque de réalité augmentée Galaxy XR en Corée du Sud et aux États-Unis. Neuf mois plus tard, soit le 8 juillet 2026, l’appareil a fait son arrivée au Royaume-Uni. Il faudra maintenant voir si les premières lunettes connectées de Samsung connaîtront un calendrier de commercialisation similaire.
Nous ne disposons toujours pas de prix
À l’heure où nous écrivons ces lignes, Samsung n’a communiqué aucune information officielle concernant le lancement de ses premières lunettes connectées. Nous ne connaissons d’ailleurs pas leur prix, ni en dollars américains ni en wons. Toujours selon le média sud-coréen Chosun Biz, Samsung n’aurait toujours pas fixé de tarif définitif. Rappelons que Xreal a modifié le prix de ses lunettes connectées Aura le jour de leur lancement. Tout est donc possible.

articles.title: KI im Orbit: Google-Satellit meldet sich aus dem All – mit einem Gedicht über den Weltraum
articles.text:
KI im Orbit: Google-Satellit meldet sich aus dem All – mit einem Gedicht über den Weltraum
Nach einer dreiwöchigen Inbetriebnahme konnte der Satellit seinen Betrieb aufnehmen: Laut Google wurden in den drei Wochen die KI-Beschleuniger sowie die übrige Hardware hochgefahren und erste Machine-Learning-Tests absolviert. Wie Techcrunch berichtet, übermittelten die Ingenieure am Boden jetzt ihren ersten Befehl: Das auf dem Satelliten vorinstallierte Deepmind-Modell „Gemma 4“ sollte ein Haiku – also ein dreizeiliges Gedicht – über den Aufenthalt im Weltraum dichten. Das Ergebnis war folgendes Kurzgedicht (sinngemäß aus dem Englischen übrsetzt):
„Die blaue Murmel da unten,
Datenströme in stiller Anmut,
Sternenlicht nährt mein Innerstes.“
Googles Projekt Suncatcher
Der Satellit stammt aus dem Google-Projekt „Suncatcher“. Das Forschungsprojekt soll laut Google untersuchen, ob der Weltraum eines Tages eine skalierbare Infrastruktur für maschinelles Lernen beherbergen könnte.
Er beherbergt vier Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) mit Solarpaneelen. Seine Solarmodule liefern zwar eine Leistung von bis zu einem Kilowatt, doch genau da liegt das Problem: Laut Google kann wegen des Strombedarfs der Chips jeweils nur eine TPU gleichzeitig laufen. Außerdem rechnet der Chip nur in kurzen Intervallen von etwa 15 Minuten. Ein Dauerbetrieb würde die Stromversorgung und die Kühlung des Satelliten überlasten. Sollten sich die TPUs an Bord des Satelliten als leistungsfähig erweisen, will Google 2027 zwei weitere Satelliten ins All schießen, die mehr Strom erzeugen können. Perspektivisch sollen mehrere Satelliten ein zusammenhängendes orbitales Rechennetzwerk bilden.
Die Zukunft von orbitalen KI‑Rechenzentren
Der US-Konzern ist mit seiner Vision von Rechenzentren im All nicht allein. Im Januar reichte etwa Elon Musks Unternehmen SpaceX bei der US-amerikanischen Telekommunikationsaufsicht Federal Communications Commission (FCC) einen Antrag ein: Die Firma will bis zu eine Million Rechenzentren in die Erdumlaufbahn bringen. Im vergangenen Winter startete Starcloud, ein Startup mit Sitz in den USA, mit einem Satelliten und Nvidia-Chip an Bord ins All. Das Unternehmen strebt an, bis 2030 ganze Rechenzentren im Orbit zu betreiben, die genauso groß sind wie jene auf der Erde.
Die Befürworter:innen halten schwebende Rechenzentren im Weltraum für sinnvoll, da der KI-Boom die Stromnetze belaste und den Wasserbedarf auf der Erde erhöhe, der zur Kühlung der Server benötigt werde. Gleichzeitig könne die erzeugte überschüssige Wärme in das kalte Vakuum des Weltraums abgeleitet werden. Kritiker:innen warnen hingegen vor den Folgen orbitaler Rechenzentren, da ihr CO₂‑Fußabdruck höher ausfallen könnte als der von Anlagen auf der Erde, wenn Herstellung, Start und Entsorgung berücksichtigt werden.

articles.title: Los empleados que usan IA trabajan hasta 90 minutos más por día que quienes no la usan
articles.text:
Los empleados que usan inteligencia artificial en su trabajo tienen jornadas de entre 8,42 y 9,08 horas diarias, frente a 7,58 horas de quienes no la usan: una diferencia de hasta 90 minutos por día. Es el resultado de un análisis de la empresa ActivTrak.
ActivTrak vende software que mide la actividad digital de los empleados. Su equipo de investigación, el Productivity Lab, revisó datos de 9.140 trabajadores de oficina en 467 empresas entre el 1 de abril y el 25 de septiembre de 2026. No se trata de una encuesta: los datos provienen del registro del uso real de aplicaciones.
Bloomberg difundió las cifras el 2 de noviembre en uno de sus boletines. El informe original usa un lenguaje prudente: afirma que los resultados “pueden sugerir” que los empleados aprovechan la capacidad liberada para asumir más tareas, pero no demuestra que la IA sea la causa de las jornadas más largas.
La comparación incluye a los usuarios más intensivos. La plataforma de software define como usuario ligero a quien emplea IA menos de 10 minutos al día, y como usuario intensivo a quien le dedica más de 45 minutos repartidos en al menos cinco sesiones diarias.
Menos concentración y más cambios de aplicación
Los usuarios intensivos mantienen 37,8 minutos de concentración continua por sesión, frente a 48,2 minutos de los ligeros. La diferencia de 10,4 minutos equivale a un 22% menos de tiempo ininterrumpido. También cambian de aplicación 1,09 veces por hora, contra 0,95 de quienes no usan IA.
El informe distingue según dónde viva la herramienta. Con IA integrada en los programas habituales, los empleados cambian de aplicación 0,6 veces por hora. Con asistentes en el navegador, lo hacen entre 1,7 y 4,2 veces por hora, hasta cuatro veces más que quienes no usan IA. ActivTrak llama a ese costo el “impuesto de la silla giratoria”.
Los usuarios de IA dedican menos tiempo a reuniones: el 3% de su tiempo activo, frente al 5% de quienes no la usan. Aun así, trabajan más horas. Según la plataforma de software, los usuarios intensivos suman unos 18 minutos diarios de trabajo fuera del horario habitual, lo que el informe llama un “tercer turno”.
El efecto cambia según el puesto. Los ingenieros de software, que suelen tener la IA dentro de sus herramientas de programación, realizan el 16,8% de su trabajo por la noche. Entre los gerentes de operaciones, que coordinan equipos con varias plataformas, esa proporción sube al 30,5%.
Otros estudios apuntan en la misma dirección, pero no todos
La propia ActivTrak había publicado un análisis anterior, que The Wall Street Journal resumió en marzo: con datos de 164.000 trabajadores en 1.111 empleadores, el tiempo en correo y mensajería se duplicó con creces después de que los empleados empezaran a usar IA.
En febrero, investigadores de la Universidad de California en Berkeley publicaron en Harvard Business Review un estudio de ocho meses en una empresa tecnológica de 200 personas. Hallaron que los empleados trabajaban más rápido, asumían más tareas y extendían el trabajo a más horas del día, muchas veces sin que nadie se lo pidiera.
Un trabajo de la Oficina Nacional de Investigación Económica de Estados Unidos (NBER), con datos de uso del tiempo entre 2004 y 2023, asocia una mayor exposición de una ocupación a la IA con jornadas más largas y menos ocio, sobre todo donde los trabajadores tienen poco poder de negociación.
Un experimento con 7.137 trabajadores de 66 empresas, publicado por la Asociación Económica Estadounidense, arrojó un resultado distinto. El 80% que usó la herramienta dedicó dos horas menos por semana al correo y redujo su trabajo fuera del horario regular. Los autores no detectaron cambios en la cantidad de tareas.
Solo el 2% integra la IA a fondo en su trabajo
La plataforma de software recuerda que su informe de madurez del primer semestre de 2026 encontró que apenas el 2% de los trabajadores tiene la IA integrada de forma profunda en sus flujos de trabajo. La empresa recomienda priorizar la IA incrustada en las aplicaciones sobre las herramientas independientes.
La recomendación coincide con el negocio de la compañía, que vende productos para medir cómo se usa el tiempo en las empresas. El análisis compara grupos de usuarios y no un antes y un después: no mide qué pasaría con los mismos empleados si dejaran de usar IA.

articles.title: Roborock F25 Ultra Steam Gen 2 : la vapeur brûlante peut-elle vraiment remplacer les produits ménagers ?
articles.text:
Roborock F25 Ultra Steam Gen 2 : la vapeur brûlante peut-elle vraiment remplacer les produits ménagers ?
Présenté à l'IFA 2026, le Roborock F25 Ultra Steam Gen 2 mise tout sur la chaleur pour repenser une corvée que l'automatisation avait jusqu'ici à peine effleurée : le lavage des sols en profondeur. Derrière la fiche technique, ce nouveau robot aspirateur-laveur offre une promesse concrète pour le quotidien, à savoir celle de venir à bout des taches tenaces et des résidus graisseux sans avoir à multiplier les produits d'entretien.
Roborock aborde ce salon berlinois en position de force : la marque revendique la première place mondiale des aspirateurs robots sur le premier semestre 2026, en volume comme en valeur, sur la foi du classement IDC du deuxième trimestre. Mais à Berlin, le constructeur ne présente pas que des robots : avec le F25 Ultra Steam Gen 2, aspirateur laveur qui succède au F25 Ultra, il s'attaque à une tâche que beaucoup continuent de faire à la main, faute d'un appareil vraiment efficace.
La chaleur comme argument central
L'idée directrice de cette deuxième génération tient en un mot : la température. Là où un aspirateur laveur classique se contente d'humidifier le sol à l'eau froide voire tiède, le F25 Ultra Steam Gen 2 génère une vapeur stable à 180 °C en seulement 30 secondes une fois préchauffé. Son mode Turbo Steam délivre jusqu'à 2,5 fois plus de vapeur que la génération précédente, ce qui permet en essence de ramollir et décoller les taches incrustées plutôt que de simplement les étaler, comme beaucoup d’appareils le font encore. Concrètement, cette mécanique répond à une frustration bien connue : celle d'un sol qui paraît propre après un passage, mais qui reste collant ou marqué là où une tâche a séché. Pour une cuisine grasse ou un carrelage marqué par le passage répété, l'eau chaude fait une vraie différence, en évitant d'avoir à récurer à genoux après le passage du robot.
Cette montée en température sert aussi un argument hygiène : Roborock avance l'élimination de la quasi-totalité des bactéries présentes au sol : voilà qui parlera aux foyers avec de jeunes enfants qui jouent par terre ou avec des animaux de compagnie (voire les deux, soyons fous !).
Nettoyer sans y penser, jusqu'aux plinthes
Au-delà de la vapeur, le F25 Ultra Steam Gen 2 cherche à faire disparaître les micro-contraintes qui rendent le ménage pénible. Une technologie intelligente adapte automatiquement la puissance de nettoyage au type de sol détecté (parquet, carrelage ou autre) sans que l'utilisateur ait à jongler entre les réglages. Son design à plat lui permet par ailleurs de se glisser sous les meubles bas, ces zones qu'on repousse toujours au prochain grand ménage, tandis que le bras robotisé SensEdge s'ajuste aux mouvements de l'utilisateur pour nettoyer au plus près des murs grâce à la technologie 0 mm Triple-Edge Cleaning. Les bordures et les plinthes, angle mort historique de ce type d'appareil, sont donc mieux prises en charge.
L'entretien de l'appareil lui-même, souvent le vrai point de bascule qui décourage l'usage régulier, a aussi été pensé : au terme du nettoyage, les fonctions de lavage et de séchage automatiques du rouleau limitent les mauvaises odeurs et gardent la machine prête à l'emploi.
Une sécurité des sols certifiée
Reste une inquiétude légitime face à de la vapeur à 180 °C : le risque pour les sols fragiles, le parquet en tête. Roborock met en avant une certification indépendante de l'organisme TÜV SÜD pour y répondre. Selon ces tests, un parquet en bois massif n'a présenté ni gonflement, ni déformation, ni fissure après 18 000 allers-retours simulant cinq années d'usage en mode vapeur. Voilà un repère utile, distinct du seul discours commercial de la marque, pour qui hésite à passer un appareil chauffant sur un revêtement coûteux.
Disponibilité
Roborock n'a pas encore communiqué le prix ni la date de commercialisation en France du F25 Ultra Steam Gen 2, puisque ces informations seront précisées au moment du lancement de l’appareil. La première génération se positionnant dans le haut du panier des aspirateurs laveurs, il faut s'attendre à un tarif du même ordre.
Pour plus d'informations, rendez-vous sur le site officiel de Roborock.

articles.title: Óscar Puente, ministro de Transportes, sobre los cinturones de seguridad: "Valoramos medidas adicionales de seguridad pasiva"
articles.text:
El accidente ferroviario de Urda (Toledo), en el que han fallecido al menos 69 personas, deja varias incógnitas sobre cómo se trabaja la seguridad ferroviaria. Nos hemos preguntado sobre el sistema LZB y si es o no más seguro que el más moderno ERTMS. También sobre el papel de los controladores. Y, por supuesto, sobre el uso o no de cinturones de seguridad.
De esto último ha hablado el ministro de Transportes Óscar Puente.
Seguridad pasiva. "Vamos a valorar la instalación de medidas adicionales de seguridad pasiva en los coches", ha señalado Óscar Puente en la intervención de esta mañana ante los medios. Esta decisión se acometerá en función de las respuestas de los expertos a los que se les encargará el estudio técnico.
Desde que se produjera el choque de trenes en Urda (Toledo) el pasado 28 de octubre, la idoneidad o no de llevar cinturón de seguridad y compartimentos separados para el equipaje es algo que se ha puesto encima de la mesa.
Despedidos.
"Pedí un café en la cafetería del tren a Sevilla. La camarera me lo sirvió. Otro camarero pregonó que estaba listo un sándwich mixto para alguien. Es lo último que recuerdo. Noté un empujón brutal del que no me acuerdo bien y sentí un golpe en la cabeza mientras me preguntaba qué pasaba. Después me vi en el suelo del vagón, en el otro extremo de la cafetería. Alguien dijo que era un accidente y eso me hizo reaccionar y comprender lo que me pasaba"
El relato es de Antonio Jiménez Barca, periodista de El País que viajaba a bordo de uno de los trenes accidentados la pasada semana. En el inicio del mismo señala cómo, en un instante, pasó de estar en extremo de la cafetería del tren al otro, a causa del brutal impacto causado por un tren que choca a otro a una velocidad de entre 160 y 200 km/h.
Además de los pasajeros, los equipajes también salieron despedidos. Y eso preocupa porque a esa velocidad, el impacto de una mochila, por pequeña que sea, es como el de un proyectil. En un coche, a 50 km/h, un objeto multiplica por 50 veces su peso en caso de impacto.
El maletero. En su declaración, Puente ha hecho hincapié en preguntar a los expertos sobre la idoneidad de dejar las maletas y mochilas en un portaequipajes cerrado. Actualmente, las maletas de mayor tamaño van en un portaequipajes abierto en los extremos del vagón. Por encima de las cabezas hay espacio para almacenar, incluso, pequeñas maletas de cabina.
El Gobierno, ha asegurado en rueda de prensa, preguntará si se debe obligar a las compañías a ofrecer trenes donde el portaequipajes sean "compartimentos cerrados que eviten proyecciones en caso frenazos bruscos o impactos. Estamos tomando ideas de medidas de seguridad del ámbito aéreo".
Puente asegura que la idea es evitar que el equipaje pueda convertirse en "misiles" que salen despedidos cuando se produce un choque como el de la semana pasada.
El cinturón de seguridad. A lo que no ha hecho alusión Puente durante su declaración es a la posibilidad de obligar a los trenes a contar con cinturones de seguridad. Esta pregunta ya se puso encima de la mesa pasado el accidente de Adamuz (Córdoba).
El objetivo de un cinturón de seguridad es mantener amarrado al pasajero en caso de accidente y así evitar que salga despedido. Sin embargo hay que tener en cuenta que el comportamiento de un coche y un tren es muy diferente por eso algunos estudios se muestran contrarios al uso del cinturón de seguridad en el transporte ferroviario, al contrario que en coches y aviones.
En un coche existe una jaula de supervivencia que debería mantenerse intacta en caso de accidente. Por fuera, el chasis tiene que absorber el impacto para que la energía que llegue hasta la jaula no la deforme y el pasajero pueda ser rescatado a pesar de sufrir un accidente grave. En el caso de los aviones se utiliza porque si hay grandes turbulencias o un descenso brusco de altura, el pasajero puede salir despedido.
¿Y en un tren? La diferencia entre un coche y un tren es que los estudios demuestran que el cuerpo del pasajero se somete a una desaceleración mucho mayor cuando un coche sufre un impacto, por eso es esencial mantener al pasajero atado al asiento.
En un tren, por brutal que sea el choque, los estudios demuestran que el pasajero se somete a fuerzas de entre 2 g y 3 g (se multiplica dos o tres veces, respectivamente, el peso del pasajero). En un coche, la desaceleración equivale a 30 g. Lo que se hace, al contrario que en un coche, es que los asientos y las mesas estén pensadas para absorber el impacto de una persona en caso de accidente en lugar de afianzarla en el sitio.
Además, se ha analizado si es útil contar con cinturones de seguridad con dos o tres anclajes. En ningún caso se observaron ventajas bien por lesiones en la cadera (el primer caso) o porque el asiento pierde la capacidad de absorción de impactos (el segundo). Además, las labores de extracción del pasajero serían mucho más complicadas en un tipo de accidente que suele convertir algunos coches en un enorme amasijo de hierros.
