articles.title: « On est arrivés un peu tard sur le marché » : conçu par l’inventeur de la poussette Yoyo, le vélo électrique Bastille est en redressement judiciaire
articles.text:
Depuis trois ans, l’industrie du cycle ne fait pas de cadeau à ses acteurs, et cela continue en cet automne 2026. Alors que les regards sont tournés vers la revente du groupe Accell, une start-up française est également touchée par la santé morose du marché. Bastille Cycles, créatrice du vélo pliant « plein format », adapté en vélo pliant électrique en 2025, a été placée en redressement judiciaire le jeudi 29 octobre par le tribunal des activités économiques de Paris. Nous avons échangé avec son cofondateur, Gilles Henry, pour en savoir plus.
Proche du but, mais un financement très difficile dans un contexte morose
« C’est difficile pour le vélo urbain en ce moment et les distributeurs sur lesquels on s’est appuyés », nous confie Gilles Henry, « ainsi on n’est pas sur la trajectoire qui était la nôtre, malgré un objectif raisonnable. »
Il révèle que le Bastille est « arrivé un peu tard sur le marché », marché qui a chuté au moment du lancement. « On n’est pas très loin du niveau où l’on voulait être, mais cette petite différence suffit à dériver de la trajectoire », explique le dirigeant, sans détailler le volume de ventes. Il ajoute que la situation tient aussi aux difficultés de financement de l’entreprise.
Après les déconvenues de nombreux acteurs à partir de 2023 – dont la spectaculaire descente aux enfers de VanMoof qui avait pourtant levé près de 200 millions d’euros – les investisseurs sont devenus frileux, tandis que les autres acteurs du secteur, qui auraient pu investir ou racheter, sont aussi en mauvaise passe.
Bastille n’est pas la seule marque française en difficulté cette année. La marque dijonnaise Cycles Lapierre a elle aussi été placée en redressement judiciaire fin août, avec une période d’observation de six mois pour convaincre un investisseur.
« Objectivement, la marque attire beaucoup de monde, les clients sont super contents, la qualité est superbe, on est fiers de ce que l’on a accompli », exprime Gilles Henry. « Il nous faudrait passer cette première marche difficile à franchir, celle d’un niveau suffisant pour être visible », ajoute-t-il, tout en assurant « avoir tenté le marché de l’export ».
Bastille, une pépite française sur le marché du vélo
Retour aux origines. 2023, un soir d’octobre dans un musée parisien, Gilles Henry nous convie à une inauguration. Le créateur de la célèbre poussette pliable Yoyo – – 2 millions d’exemplaires – – officialise son projet après plusieurs années de développement, dans lequel il a mis à profit son expertise pour créer le vélo Bastille.
Après une petite prise en main nécessaire – chaque modèle possède sa cinématique –, on a immédiatement apprécié ce vélo d’un genre nouveau. Le Bastille est un vélo au format classique de 27,5 pouces, avec l’avantage de se plier comme un « petit » modèle 20 ou 16 pouces, assez compact pour monter dans un TGV ou dans le métro.
Dès la présentation, le créateur nous avait confié développer une version électrique. Nous avions ainsi testé le Bastille E en 2025, muni d’un moteur arrière modeste de 25 Nm qui intègre une petite batterie de 210 Wh. Son poids reste contenu, avec 16,7 kg annoncés. Son prix, en revanche, peut freiner, puisque le Bastille E est affiché à 3 190 €, soit 600 € de plus que la version mécanique (2 590 €).
Bastille Cycles juge ce tarif justifié par son positionnement haut de gamme, avec un assemblage en France, une fourche carbone, ainsi que des composants réputés : roues Mach1, pneus Continental, freins hydrauliques Shimano, éclairage Spanninga, courroie Gates.
6 mois pour « tirer notre épingle du jeu »
Un redressement judiciaire s’ouvre quand une entreprise est en cessation des paiements, mais son activité continue pendant la procédure. Ainsi, pour ceux qui hésitaient encore, les ventes du vélo pliant électrique et mécanique Bastille continuent, même si le Bastille E apparaît épuisé sur le site de la marque ce mardi 3 novembre ; une version reconditionnée est proposée à partir de 2 590 €. La période d’observation de Bastille Cycles est fixée à 6 mois, soit jusqu’au 29 avril 2027, et le tribunal peut la renouveler. À son terme, trois issues sont possibles : un plan de redressement, appuyé sur de nouveaux financements pour prolonger l’activité, la liquidation judiciaire, ou le rachat.
Pour ceux qui roulent déjà en Bastille, rien ne change dans l’immédiat : l’activité continue et le jugement d’ouverture ne résilie pas, à lui seul, les contrats en cours. La marque vend et entretient ses vélos via un réseau de magasins partenaires, qui restent le premier interlocuteur. C’est l’issue de la procédure, au printemps 2027, qui dira qui assurera ensuite la garantie de 2 ans et le suivi des pièces propres au Bastille, comme son moyeu électrique tout-en-un.
On souhaite bon courage et une issue favorable à l’équipe de Bastille Cycles. « On reste optimiste pour tirer notre épingle du jeu dans les mois à venir », conclut Gilles Henry, notamment via des investisseurs probables dont les contacts étaient pris en amont de cette situation, et au travers de « nombreux projets dans les cartons ».

articles.title: 'What we're seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented': new CEO issues Apple's bleakest warning on the RAM crisis yet — and that's a big worry
articles.text:
Apple's CEO John Ternus warns RAM cost increases are now 'unprecedented' — and it makes me fear the worst for further Mac price hikes
Another notable warning in a climate of negativity
- John Ternus has warned that: "What we're seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented."
- The Apple CEO cautioned that RAM costs are going to climb higher in this final quarter of 2026
- It sounds even bleaker than Apple's previous statements on the RAM crisis, and follows many other warnings that 2027 is set to be a miserable year price-wise
Apple is warning of an 'unprecedented' rise in the cost of RAM, adding to the cacophony of alarm bells that have been ringing about the price of memory chips (and other PC components besides) recently.
The Guardian reports that in a conference call following Apple's fiscal Q3 results — which were better than analysts expected, driven by the iPhone, Mac mini and sales in China — Apple's new CEO John Ternus touched on the subject of the RAM crisis.
Ternus, who recently took the reins from Tim Cook, cautioned bleakly that: "What we're seeing with memory pricing right now is unprecedented."
He then observed that memory costs would climb even higher in the final quarter of 2026 compared to the rest of the year, during which, as you've doubtless seen, we've already witnessed a steep climb in pricing.
Despite its financial results outperforming analyst forecasts, Apple informed investors that these higher memory costs are going to erode some of its profit margins, which meant the company's stock dropped.
Apple raised the prices of Macs earlier this year, as well as iPads and more recently iPhones, and Ternus acknowledged that this had "provided some offset" for Apple in terms of the ongoing cost crisis around components.
Analysis: Ternus takes a turn for the sterner
It's an ominous utterance from Ternus, and sounds more severe than the warning Apple issued back before the Mac (and other) price hikes happened in June 2026. Back then, when Cook was still chief executive, he warned about "significantly higher memory costs" that would "drive an increasing impact" on Apple's products, which, as noted, came to pass.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Now we're hearing the word "unprecedented", which sounds a lot more concerning than "significant"; although in fairness, this is referencing what's already happened this year as much as what's to come. But we're clearly being primed for more price-hike misery by Ternus here, and it's difficult to see how this won't have a further impact on Macs, iPhones and iPads, if not in this quarter, then in 2027.
We don't, of course, know to what extent profits might be eroded by more expensive memory chips, or how this might be balanced by consumers having to foot that bill. Only time will tell on that score.
Mac mini sales were mentioned in the report — which quoted Ben Barringer, the head of technology research at investment management firm Quilter Cheviot — as being responsible for part of Apple's boosted earnings for the most recent quarter, and that's down to the increasing demand for local AI.
The Mac Studio is major part of that picture, too, and this particular PC just popped up as an example of how ridiculous RAM pricing has just become at the very top end of the Apple product tree. If you want a Mac Studio with 512GB of RAM, you'll now pay more than double the cost of a Mac Studio that has 256GB of memory, meaning that it's cheaper to buy two of the latter computers (while getting two CPUs/GPUs in the process).
It's a bizarre situation, but this is what we've arrived at with memory upgrades, which were always seriously pricey with Apple, even before the RAM crisis kicked off (that goes for storage, too).
And this situation is only going to get worse, seemingly, according to Ternus, which is also, of course, the view of the wider industry and various analysts. I can't begin to count the warnings we've had in the past couple of months about the RAM crisis becoming even more dire, so at this point it's just a question of how much worse things might get.
I fear that some categories of tech and PC components are going to become increasingly unaffordable next year, and I recently wrote about why Black Friday could be a good time to move on certain purchases.

articles.title: Engineer creates retro FPGA Game Boy console that can rip your cartridges to an SD card natively — features HDMI, USB-C, and even has Game Link Cable support
articles.text:
Engineer creates retro FPGA Game Boy console that can rip your cartridges to an SD card natively — features HDMI, USB-C, and even has Game Link Cable support
The project was nearly abandoned until a supportive retro enthusiast financed the equipment needed to bring it to life.
Joining the retro console revival movement is the SGBC, a new console that can play Nintendo Game Boy cartridges natively using an FPGA core. Built by Thomas Sanfourche, a French electronics engineer studying in Taiwan, the SGBC aims to give players a way to preserve and play their games with the full Game Boy experience, including a link port for multiplayer and trading.
The SGBC uses a Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA), a reprogrammable chip that can be configured to replicate the hardware logic of another chip, in this case, the Game Boy’s hardware. It can replicate not just the CPU, but multiple other components of a Game Boy as well, but Sanfourche has yet to specify which of the original Game Boy’s ICs have been consolidated into the FPGA.
The SGBC doesn’t just replicate the Game Boy as a console; it has plenty of features that retro gamers would appreciate — the most interesting among them being the built-in cartridge ripping function. If you insert your favorite Game Boy cartridge into the SGBC’s slot, you can preserve it by copying the ROM onto the microSD card in the console, digitizing your collection. It also outputs in 1080p 16:9 without stretching, and uses integer scaling to keep the game's pixels aligned with the pixels on your monitor or TV through HDMI. The SGBC also features an SNES controller port and a Game Boy Link port for multiplayer and trading.
Thomas Sanfourche almost ditched the SGBC entirely; in an interview with French retro gaming YouTuber GyuGyu, he said he went to Taiwan to study electronics engineering after discovering his strong interest in electronics. He didn’t know the local language and couldn’t enrol without certification, so he gave himself two years but ended up getting the language certification in six months. In his second year, he chose to enrol in the FPGA course after being intrigued by the name, and eventually chose it as the subject of his final-year project — a Game Boy FPGA core.
Sanfourche said his project was dismissed when he presented it to his professors: “What’s the point of doing this on an FPGA?” he was asked. This discouraged him and stopped him from working on it — until one day he went to a warehouse to buy a PVM monitor and struck up a conversation with a fellow customer who was a retro product seller and very active in the local retro scene. The discussion eventually led to his FPGA core Game Boy project, to which the seller asked, “Why don’t you market it?” The supportive stranger then offered, on the spot, to finance the equipment needed to market it or at least bring the project to life. The financier told Sanfourche he doesn’t want to be a part of the business, but that he wants to resell the product when he releases it, further supporting the project by sharing updates and teasers to local retro enthusiast Facebook groups.
The SGBC is yet to be released, but the project joins other FPGA consoles by the likes of retro gaming modding YouTuber Taki Udon’s SuperStation One, ModRetro’s M64, and Analogue’s SuperNT+ and MegaSG+. Not only are projects like these reviving the platforms, but they are also giving them modern features and comforts, bringing the question “What if these consoles were built today?” to reality.

articles.title: Pope Leo XIV urges governments to ban lethal AI weapons, says tech must be used for common good
articles.text:
Big quote: Pope Leo XIV has called for artificial intelligence to be "disarmed," urging governments meeting in Geneva for a UN weapons conference later this month to take concrete steps toward banning lethal autonomous weapons systems in warfare. Decisions affecting human life, freedom, and the use of force, the pontiff said, must always remain under human oversight.
The pope also made the Catholic Church's position clear on the debate over whether AI systems should be granted rights or legal personhood, saying the Vatican sees machines as tools, not sentient beings with a claim to legal rights of their own. AI is developed by human beings, he added, and granting it rights or personhood would obscure human accountability.
The future of artificial intelligence is not predetermined, according to the pope, but depends on the choices people make. "We therefore have the responsibility to guide, change and, when necessary, reject its applications," he said, adding that the decisive question about AI is not what it can do, but "What purpose should it serve?"
In an address on Friday, the Chicago-born pontiff also voiced strong reservations about the use of AI in warfare and border control, saying certain decisions "must never be delegated" to technology. Humans, he said, should always be in charge of target lists, border control databases, and autonomous weapons.
Explaining his stance, the pope said advanced technologies must be directed toward the greater good of humanity, a goal he said is only achievable if international institutions and governments work in unison to ensure that ethical principles, rather than corporate profits, guide the development of AI.
It isn't the first time Pope Leo has spoken out against handing lethal decisions to AI. When he made similar remarks in his May encyclical, Mistral co-founder and CEO Arthur Mensch pushed back, arguing that Europe needs its own military AI capabilities because its adversaries are already using the technology.
Pope Leo is not the first pontiff to denounce the use of autonomous weapons in warfare. In a 2024 address to the G7, Pope Francis stressed the importance of keeping decision-making in human hands, noting that a machine makes a technical choice based on defined criteria or statistical inferences, while humans "not only choose, but in their hearts are capable of deciding."

articles.title: Trump wanted to give No Kings no air. Then, Meta suspended its Instagram.
articles.text:
Mark Zuckerberg in Menlo Park, California on Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026. Donald Trump in Fort Myers, Florida on October 23, 2026.
Credit:
Aurich Lawson | Getty Images | Minh Connors | Alex Wong
Mark Zuckerberg in Menlo Park, California on Wednesday, Sept. 23, 2026. Donald Trump in Fort Myers, Florida on October 23, 2026.
Credit:
Aurich Lawson | Getty Images | Minh Connors | Alex Wong
Over the weekend, the No Kings Coalition said Meta declined to commit to taking steps to prevent automated systems from suspending one of Instagram’s most prominent pro-democracy accounts if activity surged around the page during the midterm elections.
A demand for action came after Meta apologized for temporarily suspending the No Kings Instagram account and disabling access for four hours at the peak of an early voting push from the group. In a post on X, Meta’s Andy Stone said the account had been using a Claude AI tool in a way that made it appear to be a bot. But even though automated review detected the error within an hour, Stone acknowledged that additional hurdles kept admins locked out. State and federal lawmakers—as well as a coalition of 14 attorneys general—have asked Meta to further explain its actions.
In a letter to No Kings, Meta offered to arrange a meeting with a technical expert who could better explain the mistake. But No Kings rejected the response, saying it failed to address any of the group’s ongoing concerns and requesting a meeting with Meta senior leadership instead. The group stressed that the issue goes beyond its Instagram account, saying that Americans who rely on Meta’s platforms need assurance that voting content won’t be suppressed ahead of or on election day. Among eight questions, the coalition asked Meta to publicly disclose any communications with the Trump administration about the No Kings account or the historic early voting day event.
On October 30, Meta executives met with No Kings. According to the coalition’s account of the meeting, Meta said it has “no plans” to change policies that lead to harmful over-enforcement, a problem that even the independent Oversight Board, which reviews Meta’s content decisions, worries could result in suppression or censorship of No Kings and other pro-democracy content during this critical period.
“Meta acknowledged that it made a mistake, but an apology without action does nothing to ensure that this kind of censorship won’t happen again,” No Kings said, calling Meta’s laissez-faire attitude “unacceptable.”
Ars has found no evidence that the Trump administration asked Meta to restrict the No Kings account or that anyone at Meta intentionally targeted the account for political reasons. Meta told No Kings that it planned to post a public reply to the coalition’s demands, but the company did not respond to Ars’ request for comment, and Stone has yet to post an update on X. His account did, however, apologize for another accidental enforcement action impacting a Republican-controlled account the day before the No Kings meeting. “We automatically removed the @MOSenateGOP Facebook account because our systems mistakenly assessed the account was impersonating another one,” Stone said.
“This was never simply about a technical glitch or one Instagram account,” No Kings’ press release said. “It’s about whether millions of Americans can rely on these platforms to organize, communicate, and access critical voting information without disruption.”
Meta’s AI explanation seems incomplete
Formed in 2025 after Donald Trump returned to office for a second term, the No Kings Coalition is best known for organizing some of the largest coordinated protests in recent US history. Using social media channels to coordinate nationwide demonstrations against Trump policies viewed as anti-democratic, organizers estimated that more than 5 million people participated in its first protests in June 2025 and say attendance has only increased since. No Kings estimates 7 million people attended the second protests in October 2025, and more than 8 million showed up for the third demonstration last March.
For the fourth event, however, No Kings sought to get more than 9 million people into the streets, and then directly to the polls, by organizing an early voting event on October 17. Unlike the family-friendly protests where Americans held up signs demanding “No Kings in America,” this event focused on driving voter turnout. Although No Kings describes itself as a pro-democracy coalition with no interest in building up the Democratic Party, turnout for its events is driven by those who oppose Trump’s most controversial policies—including domestic ICE enforcement and US military involvement in Iran.
Hundreds of civil rights organizations, including Black Voters Matter and the American Civil Liberties Union, make up the No Kings Coalition. Initially, there was no centralized Instagram account where the groups could coordinate their social media messaging. But as the November 3 election approached, the coalition got more organized, hoping that an official No Kings account with a large following would help it identify and amplify content ahead of the fourth event.
That’s when No Kings decided to use Claude as a “keyword and hashtag search tool to track conversations across social media platforms,” the group’s social media team told Ars.
According to Stone, the Claude tool was “reading profiles, posts, and hashtags,” which “sharply” increased the account’s activity in “intense bursts” that “resembled automated bot traffic rather than an ordinary human browsing our systems.”
Ars could not determine what specific Claude-powered tool the coalition was using, how it accessed Instagram, or whether it was an Anthropic service or a third-party integration built using Claude. Ars asked both Anthropic and Meta whether there was anything unusual about the way No Kings was using Claude, but neither company responded.
Ezra Levin, co-founder of Indivisible, a progressive nonprofit in the No Kings Coalition, told Ars that the volume of posting increases because organizers understand a basic principle of advertising: “You’ve got to reach people seven different times in seven different ways, and it’s the seventh time that they hear, and they’re like, ‘Oh right, there is an early vote action going on. I should get out there.’”
The high volume shouldn’t matter, though, Levin said, emphasizing that “it seems pretty absurd that a social media company that doesn’t go down during the Super Bowl or during the World Series or during the Oscars shuts our account down during an early vote push.”
“We’re not using any boutique tools that nobody has developed before,” Levin said. “These are all nonprofits. We’re putting things together with popsicle sticks and glue. We’re not developing our own sophisticated apparatus. So there is nothing that I’m aware of that is unique about how we were using the social media platform that day.”
Meta’s closer ties with Trump fuel suspicion
Levin pointed to a series of episodes dating back to at least 2016 that raised questions about Meta’s role in protecting democratic processes. That year, Facebook acknowledged that it sold election-related ads to a shadowy Russian company. More recently, Meta faced questions from Congress in 2021 after turning off election-related safeguards and failing to detect “Stop the Steal” groups from gaming its algorithm to spread disinformation. After Trump’s 2024 election and shortly before his inauguration, Meta announced that it would end its US third-party fact-checking program. Zuckerberg also said Meta would work with Trump to push back against what he characterized as censorship by foreign governments. Critics warned that the move amounted to Meta declaring that “the truth doesn’t matter.”
To Levin, Meta’s playbook for handling controversies like the No Kings Instagram suspension is to lawyer up, offer technical explanations, and issue “empty apologies.”
Levin also pointed to Meta’s decision to donate $1 million to Trump’s inaugural fund and later $5 million for Trump’s ballroom project, which Levin said were blatant efforts to curry favor with the president.
Given what Levin sees as Zuckerberg’s alignment with Trump, he said it’s difficult for No Kings to accept that a technical glitch, rather than deliberate action by someone at Meta, was behind the suspension. Levin acknowledged that some posts that appear to be suppressed on Meta platforms may simply fail to get traction. But given Meta’s history with election content and its failure to make changes to protect pro-democracy content, he said, it’s difficult for outsiders to not be skeptical.
For example, Levin said Meta never acknowledged that at least one No Kings creator’s account was also suspended on the day the No Kings account was disabled. Other No Kings creators have reported that some Instagram posts seemingly receive no views.
“This is why the history does matter,” Levin said. “The context matters here because if I believed Meta to be a corporation that was operating above-board and was stridently pro-democracy and always erred in the defense of people organizing, I would say, ‘Look, it’s Meta. You know Meta, they wouldn’t do that. Probably there’s something else going on.’ But you would have to not have your head screwed on straight to believe that based on the publicly available information.”
Trump seems to shift No Kings tactics
Levin told Ars that one of his biggest remaining questions is whether Meta had any interactions with the Trump administration ahead of the suspension.
To No Kings, the Trump administration had been vocal in its opposition to the protests during the coalition’s first two events. Last October, Trump controversially posted an AI-generated video of a jet labeled “King Trump” flying over protesters while blasting the Kenny Loggins song “Danger Zone.” He has also directly dismissed protesters as an “ineffective” “joke,” echoing comments from others in his administration.
But Trump may have realized that such comments were only drawing more attention to the movement, and there has since been a “notable tactical shift,” Levin suggested. Trump and his supporters now seem to pointedly refuse to discuss No Kings, perhaps hoping to deny the movement oxygen, he said.
“It’s not absurd to think they were also talking to their friends in social media and asking them to not cover this as much or tilt the algorithm a certain way,” Levin said.
Although four hours may not seem like a long time, any disruption that makes it harder for No Kings to reach people has a significant impact, Levin said.
“We are forced to use these platforms that are privately owned in order to reach these folks,” Levin said. “And in using the platforms, we are vulnerable to this kind of pressure, and that directly undermines our ability to reach these people.”
If the same thing happened “in the middle of election day, where pro-democracy accounts are suppressed or shut down,” that could be “cataclysmic,” Levin said.
Lawmakers, AGs probe Meta
David Greene, senior counsel for the digital rights group the Electronic Frontier Foundation (EFF), told Ars that the timing of the No Kings Instagram suspension is “suspicious” and that Meta’s technical excuse is “a really incomplete answer.”
As No Kings continues to demand that Meta release any communications with Trump, Meta also faces increased pressure from lawmakers and state officials to make changes to support accounts like No Kings during election day.
Last week, a coalition of 14 state attorneys general sent a letter to Meta demanding a more transparent explanation of the suspension. By October 29, they asked Meta to “detail its plans to ensure that legitimate election activity on Meta platforms is not disrupted.”
“This is particularly concerning given the proliferation of AI agents marketed to consumers, including by Meta, as compatible with social media accounts,” the attorneys general wrote.
Ars could not confirm whether the coalition’s deadline was met, but the attorneys general weren’t alone in expressing concern that Meta may be “unable to differentiate between legitimate political activity and bot activity that harms users” in the age of AI.
Democratic Maryland Senator Chris Van Hollen sent a similar request, The New Republic reported, specifically asking why it took so long for Meta to help admins regain access. In Congress, Robert Garcia and Jamie Raskin, members of the House Oversight Committee and House Judiciary Committee, also probed Meta for answers. Levin noted that these lawmakers could become future chairs of those committees if the elections swing No Kings’ way.
In Levin’s ideal world, “the next Congress” would “take a very different approach” to regulating the tech industry. He believes that could have significant consequences ahead of the next presidential election. Rather than seeing tech CEOs aligned with the executive branch, there could finally be a more “healthy” public debate, where “different presidential candidates” may adopt “different positions of their orientation towards Silicon Valley,” Levin said.
The path Meta is not taking
Greene suggested that Meta could take steps such as requiring human review of election-related content or creating emergency support channels to quickly address automated throttling, inadvertent suspensions, or content removals.
Although Meta has no legal obligation to do so, Greene said, “they certainly have an obligation to their users to anticipate these things and to be ready for them.”
Greene told Ars that he agreed with Meta’s Oversight Board, which directed Meta to take proactive steps to protect election-related content rather than simply waiting to fix problems after an account is automatically suspended. One possible solution, Greene suggested, would be a notification system allowing No Kings to notify Meta when major events are planned so the company can prepare.
“Clearly if it was a technical problem, it’s a technical problem that should have been expected and thought about ahead of time and anticipated and addressed ahead of time,” Greene said. “The No Kings stuff was not secret in any way.”
Like Levin, Greene pointed to Meta’s history of mishandling election content, not just in the US but around the world. Levin noted that No Kings worked with election organizers in Brazil, where Meta also recently faced allegations of electoral interference.
“These are technical glitches that happen around elections all the time, and Meta just needs to have an affirmative plan for this and not just try to respond as they happen,” Greene said. “And I think until they do that, they’re not going to dispel suspicion that things are politically motivated.”
The EFF believes the Trump administration should disclose all its communications with Meta, but so far neither side is clarifying whether Trump may be influencing how Meta handles election-related content, Greene said.
Greene said it’s difficult to determine whether Meta was engaged in “jawboning,” with the Trump administration pressuring the platform to silence dissidents. However, “the explanation they’ve given is so inadequate that it’s hard to discount the [idea] that there was political influence,” he said.
And he agreed that a four-hour admin lockout was too long.
“Because as we know, when you’re organizing a protest, even if you shorten this to a three-minute delay from a three-hour delay, that could be consequential,” Greene said. “And so, the idea is to avoid these things in the first place.”
Kate Ruane, director of the Center for Democracy and Technology’s Free Expression Project, told Ars that Meta must explain not only why its automated systems flagged accounts like the No Kings Instagram account but also why the “mistake prevention systems” it designed to avoid such situations “were not triggered in this circumstance.”
Ruane noted that the CDT supports the JAWBONE Act, which “would require the government to be transparent with the public about communications from the government to online speech intermediaries related to the constitutionally protected speech they distribute.” If the next Congress passes that law, Meta could face greater scrutiny if questions about the No Kings suspension remain unanswered. Levin suggested that “a pro-democracy Congress” would send subpoenas, hold hearings, and use legislative processes to hold Meta accountable.
“Large-scale political speech events are frequently organized using Meta’s services,” Ruane said. “It is critical for users engaged in those activities to understand exactly what happened and how they and Meta can avoid it in the future.”
Ashley is a senior policy reporter for Ars Technica, dedicated to tracking social impacts of emerging policies and new technologies. She is a Chicago-based journalist with 20 years of experience.

articles.title: Hacienda obliga a tributar por las propinas que reciben los trabajadores, pero cotizarán si lo recoge el convenio o las gestiona la empresa
articles.text:
Cualquier tipo de propina que reciban los trabajadores de bares y restaurantes tiene repercusiones fiscales. Es decir, que aunque los clientes den la propina de manera voluntaria, esto va a suponer que los trabajadores deben tenerlo en cuenta a la hora de calcular los rendimientos del trabajo (impuesto sobre la renta de las personas físicas). Además de ello, debe analizarse si deben cotizar a la Seguridad Social.
El IRPF alcanza a las propinas
En primer lugar, en el artículo 17.1 de la Ley del IRPF están incluidas las cantidades que provienen directa o indirectamente de la relación de trabajo o del propio trabajo personal. Es decir, que además de los salarios se incluyen otros rendimientos relacionados con el trabajo (utilidades). En este sentido, las propinas que reciben de los clientes van a estar sujetas al IRPF.
Además, están previstas las retenciones. En efecto, en el artículo 76 del Reglamento del IRPF se habla de los casos en que el que realiza la actividad económica tiene que abonar a sus trabajadores las cantidades que los terceros le entreguen en concepto de propinas. En el caso de que sean repartidas por la empresa, deberá realizar en su caso la correspondiente retención (que se ingresará en Hacienda).
Es importante destacar que estar sometido a IRPF quiere decir que están en la base de dicho impuesto. Sin embargo, no es necesario que haya obligación de presentar la declaración (ver artículo 96 de la ley).
La propina voluntaria queda fuera de la base del IVA
En el impuesto sobre el valor añadido (IVA) es diferente. En efecto, las cantidades que el cliente entrega de manera voluntaria (y que no son exigibles por el servicio) no entran en la contraprestación que el restaurante recibe.
En este sentido, la Dirección General de Tributos en consulta 2174-03 de 11 de diciembre de 2003 ha indicado que estas cantidades no entran en la base imponible del servicio de hostelería.
Cuándo puede haber cotización
Para ello es necesario analizar la naturaleza de este ingreso. En primer lugar, en el artículo 147 de la Ley General de la Seguridad Social se indica que en la base están incluidas las remuneraciones que corresponden al trabajador por su empleo. Por otro lado, la gratificación que hace el cliente de manera voluntaria puede ser extrasalarial y, si se configura como una remuneración empresarial, será diferente.
Carlos Déniz, del departamento laboral de Garrigues, indica que en el caso de que sea el propio cliente el que la entrega al trabajador (sin que intervenga la empresa), es diferente. En el caso de que se configure como retribución, es salario (y, por tanto, debe cotizar).
También es importante analizar cómo se gestiona el reparto y cómo está previsto en el convenio que resulte de aplicación. Sin embargo, no es cierto que todo bote gestionado por la empresa sea salario. Es necesario ver qué se paga y bajo qué condiciones.

articles.title: Safari gets Siri AI actions and Vertical Tabs with macOS 27.3
articles.text:
Apple’s iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3 and macOS 27.3 betas are now available, sporting several updates to Apple apps, like the Health app, and more.
But Safari is also getting a few notable upgrades, so let’s do a deep dive into what’s new with Safari.
Vertical Tabs
A new vertical layout for navigating and managing your tabs lets you maximize your space. The tabs on the side appear as icons so they take up less room, and hovering over the icon will show the name first, but hover a little longer and Safari will show a small preview of what’s open in that tab.
Vertical Tabs will be available on MacBook, iPad and the iPhone Duo. You can turn it on by heading to Safari settings on these platforms.
Adaptive Dark Mode
Safari can automatically apply Dark Mode to webpages that don’t support it natively. When you’re in Dark Mode and hit a page with a bright background, Safari will have a pop-up saying ‘Try Adaptive Dark Mode.’ Tapping it will render a Dark Mode version of the webpage.
However, for webpages that must be bright for some reason, developers can exclude their site from Adaptive Dark Mode.
This update is coming to iOS, macOS, and iPadOS.
Siri AI Actions
With Siri AI custom actions on Safari, you can ask the assistant to sort your tabs, move them around, sort, organize and close them by asking. Further, Siri AI is aware of your webpage and even other tabs, so if you’re shopping for shoes and land on a page with a pair you like, but have five other tabs open, you can ask Siri to compare the ones you’re looking at to the other ones on your tabs.
This feature is coming to Apple Intelligence-supported devices.

articles.title: “Je veux leur offrir une meilleure fin” : Johnny Depp prêt à revenir dans Pirates des Caraïbes 6
articles.text:
“Je veux leur offrir une meilleure fin” : Johnny Depp prêt à revenir dans Pirates des Caraïbes 6
L'acteur a confirmé qu'il serait partant pour remettre le tricorne de Jack Sparrow dans la franchise Pirates des Caraïbes, mais à une seule et unique condition.
Près d'une décennie après la sortie de son dernier volet en date, Pirates des Caraïbes n'a jamais été aussi proche de revenir sur grand écran... et peut-être bien avec Jack Sparrow à la barre. C'est en tous cas ce qu'a laissé entendre l'acteur Johnny Depp, confirmant les plans de reboot de la franchise dans les tuyaux de Disney depuis des années.
Le retour du capitaine Jack Sparrow ?
En pleine promotion de son prochain film Scrooge (en salles le 11 novembre), Depp en a profité pour répondre à la question de nos confrères américains d'Entertainment Tonight sur la possibilité d'un retour de Jack Sparrow dans un Pirates des Caraïbes 6 :
"Je suis prêt à travailler avec Jerry Bruckheimer (producteur de la franchise Pirates des Caraïbes, ndlr) dès demain. Peu importe ce que c'est, s'il s'agit de Jerry, je lui fais confinace. Nous avons une amitié profonde".
Il poursuit : "Si tout est parfaitement en place pour conclure en beauté la franchise Pirates des Caraïbes... La seule chose que je souhaite vraiment, au fond, c'est de leur offrir une meilleure fin".
- Regardez l'interview d'Entertainment Tonight :
On peut comprendre la volonté de Johnny Depp de revenir pour corriger le tir tant le cinquième film - Pirates des Caraïbes : La Vengeance de Salazar - avait reçu un très mauvais accueil critique à sa sortie en 2017, et est souvent considéré par le public comme l'opus le plus faible de la saga.
En 2024, Jerry Bruckheimer confirmait que le scénariste Jeff Nathanson (Le Roi Lion version 2019, Arrête-moi si tu peux) était en train de terminer le script de ce Pirates des Caraïbes 6, et se montrait particulièrement enthousiaste : "nous avons encore besoin de peaufiner les première et seconde parties, mais il a écrit un troisième acte vraiment génial."
Si rien n'a encore été officialisé, ces différentes déclarations laissent donc penser que ce n'est qu'une question de temps avant que la franchise de pirates repartent en mer. Et ce n'est pas étonnant : avec 4,5 milliards de dollars générés au box-office mondial en cinq longs-métrages, c'est l'un des joyaux de la couronne de Disney, qui compte bien en faire quelque chose.
Outre ce potentiel Pirates des Caraïbes 6 avec Jack Sparrow, un autre reboot a longtemps été en développement avec Margot Robbie en tête d'affiche. Mais le projet a été mis en pause, sans aucun signe de vie depuis plusieurs années.
L'intégralité de la franchise Pirates des Caraïbes est disponible en streaming sur la plateforme Disney+.

articles.title: La carrera espacial privada tiene cada vez más “juguetes”: pronto tendrá también un telescopio en el espacio
articles.text:
La carrera espacial ya no es solo cosa de las grandes agencias públicas, como la NASA o la ESA. Las compañías privadas están teniendo un papel cada vez más relevante, especialmente en lo que respecta al desarrollo de cohetes y satélites. Hasta ahora, uno de los pocos terrenos inexplorados para el sector privado era el de los telescopios espaciales. Sin embargo, si todo va bien, eso cambiará muy pronto con el lanzamiento de Lazuli, el telescopio desarrollado por Schmidt Sciences para estudiar los exoplanetas que otros no han podido analizar en profundidad.
23 colores. Lazuli dispondrá de un espejo primario de 3 metros, por lo que es más grande que el del Hubble, y será capaz de observar el cielo en 23 colores, desde la luz visible hasta el infrarrojo cercano. También dispondrá de un espectrógrafo, que le permitirá discernir la composición de los objetos celestes gracias al análisis de la luz que estos emiten o reflejan.
Su instrumento principal. Más allá de su amplio rango de colores y su análisis espectral, Lazuli destaca por un instrumento llamado ExtraSolar Coronagraph (ESC). Su objetivo es bloquear la luz de estrellas lejanas para que esta no interfiera con la luz que reflejan los planetas que giran en torno a ellas. Dicho a muy grosso modo, creará pequeños eclipses artificiales para centrar toda la atención en los exoplanetas que se quieran analizar.
27 candidatos. Dos científicos de las Universidades de Michigan y Arizona han publicado recientemente un estudio en el que se exponen 27 exoplanetas gigantes que serían candidatos ideales para que Lazuli los estudie. Esto no quiere decir que sean necesariamente los que se van a estudiar, pero sí parecen ser buenos candidatos.
Gigantes fríos. Por limitaciones técnicas relacionadas con el tiempo y el enfoque, la mayoría de exoplanetas en los que se centran los telescopios espaciales son Júpiter calientes. Estos exoplanetas están muy cerca de su estrella, por lo que tienen tránsitos más cortos y dan más vueltas alrededor de la estrella por unidad de tiempo que un planeta que se encuentra más lejos. Esto hace más fácil detectarlos.
El problema es que los gigantes de nuestro sistema solar, Júpiter y Saturno, están mucho más lejos del Sol. Por lo tanto, sus características son bastante diferentes. Lo ideal sería estudiar los gigantes gaseosos fríos. Hasta ahora era un reto técnico, pero Lazuli sí está mejor preparado para hacerlo gracias a su coronógrafo, que le permite captar la luz tenue de planetas lejanos. Los 27 candidatos son precisamente de este tipo.
Más instrumentos. Lazuli trabajará en equipo junto con otros instrumentos desarrollados también por Schmidt Sciences: los arrays ópticos terrestres Argus y LFAST y el radiotelescopio Deep Synoptic Array. Todos ellos compartirán software y datos, de modo que un hallazgo de uno pueda seguirse fácilmente con otro.
También agencias públicas. En el estudio que han hecho estos científicos, aún sin revisión por pares, señalan que otros telescopios que ya están en funcionamiento podrían trabajar igualmente sobre los mismos candidatos. Es, por ejemplo, el caso del recién estrenado Nancy Grace Roman o del veterano Very Large Telescope (VLT). De nuevo, los datos podrán compartirse, para que telescopios públicos y privados trabajen en equipo.
La fecha. Aún no hay una fecha definitiva para la puesta en marcha de Lazuli. No obstante, si todo va bien, Schmidt Sciences espera poder lanzarlo en 2028 o, como mucho, 2029. Hasta entonces, se seguirá trabajando tanto en su desarrollo como en la búsqueda de candidatos para que pueda analizarlos.

articles.title: PowerUp Money raises $10M to expand AI-led wealth management
articles.text:
PowerUp Money raises $10M to expand AI-led wealth management
The Bengaluru-based company plans to use a significant portion of the capital to develop its AI-powered wealth management platform and expand its managed advisory business.
PowerUp Money, a wealthtech platform offering mutual fund advice and digital wealth management services, has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Flourish Ventures, an early-stage investment firm.
Existing investors Peak XV Partners, Accel, Blume Ventures, Kae Capital, 8i Ventures and DeVC also participated.
The Bengaluru-based company plans to use a significant portion of the capital to develop its AI-powered wealth management platform and expand its managed advisory business.
PowerUp claims more than 1.5 million users track mutual fund portfolios worth over Rs 2.5 lakh crore on its platform. Its paid subscription service, Elite, provides research-backed mutual fund advice and is said to have crossed 1,00,000 paid members in less than a year.
The company has now introduced Elite Prime, an AI-enabled digital wealth advisory service designed to provide a more comprehensive financial planning experience. It assesses investors’ financial goals, risk appetite and existing holdings to suggest asset allocation, systematic investment plans (SIPs), lump-sum investments, portfolio rebalancing and withdrawal strategies. It can also identify gaps in portfolios and suggest diversification into assets such as gold, silver and international investments.
An AI wealth coach and personal assistant are intended to help users understand recommendations and make informed decisions.
Founder and chief executive officer Prateek Jindal said, “AI makes it possible to deliver a much more comprehensive, wealth-manager-like experience digitally”, bringing personalised guidance within reach of investors who may not be able to afford traditional wealth management services.
PowerUp is also looking to expand Infinite, its managed wealth advisory offering. The service combines financial planning, portfolio construction, multi-asset allocation and ongoing portfolio management with dedicated human advisers.
According to the company, Infinite has accumulated nearly Rs 500 crore in assets under management (AUM) within around nine months of launch, despite being available to a limited customer base. Making the service accessible to more investors is another priority for the new funding.
The expansion comes amid sustained growth in India’s mutual fund market. According to the Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI), industry AUM stood at Rs 82.64 lakh crore at the end of September 2026, up from Rs 15.8 lakh crore a decade earlier. Monthly SIP contributions also reached Rs 32,490 crore in September, reflecting the growing adoption of regular, long-term investing.
Investor interest has encouraged further funding across the wealthtech sector. Debt investment platform Wint Wealth raised Rs 250 crore in a Series B round in January, while wealth management firm Centricity secured Rs 280 crore in August. AI-focused advisory startup Novelty Wealth also announced a $1.4 million seed round in March.
However, growth brings its own challenges. Digital advice must remain suitable, transparent and compliant as platforms expand their customer base. SEBI issued an updated Master Circular for Investment Advisers in February, reinforcing the regulatory framework governing investment advice.
The opportunity, as Flourish Ventures’ Asia head Ravi Kaushik noted, lies in helping investors manage increasingly complex financial lives.

articles.title: Bouygues Telecom débarque dans ChatGPT, et même les comptes gratuits peuvent en profiter, on l'a testé
articles.text:
Bouygues Telecom lance ce mardi une application intégrée à ChatGPT, une première revendiquée chez les opérateurs français. Les forfaits, smartphones et éligibilité à la fibre se discutent désormais en langage naturel, y compris avec un compte gratuit.
L'opérateur Bouygues Telecom propose désormais ses offres directement dans ChatGPT, avec une application dédiée accessible à tous les utilisateurs du chatbot d’OpenAI, comme il l'annonce ce mardi 3 novembre 2026. Reliée en temps réel aux API de l'opérateur, elle permet de comparer les forfaits, de choisir un smartphone ou de tester son éligibilité à la fibre, sans quitter la conversation avant l'étape du panier. Bouygues Telecom affirme être le premier opérateur français à franchir ce pas, sur un marché où l'IA prenait jusqu’ici surtout la forme d’abonnements offerts.
Un conseiller Bouygues Telecom niché dans ChatGPT
OpenAI a lancé les applications dans ChatGPT en octobre 2025, d'abord hors de l'Union européenne, et désormais, des marques y proposent leurs services, un peu à la manière d'une boutique d'apps, comme on l'a récemment vu avec Chronopost. Celle de Bouygues Telecom se trouve dans la liste accessible depuis la page d'accueil, en cherchant simplement son nom. Ensuite, on discute, à l'écrit ou en s'aidant de la voix. On peut comparer les offres fixe et mobile, choisir un smartphone selon sa capacité ou sa couleur, étudier le financement associé, tester son éligibilité à la fibre ou aux autres offres Box, directement depuis la conversation dans ChatGPT.
La bonne nouvelle, c'est que la version gratuite de ChatGPT y a accès. Et pour éviter que l'IA ne s'emmêle les pinceaux avec un tarif périmé, l'application est branchée en temps réel sur les API sécurisées de l'opérateur. Les réponses reposent donc sur les informations fournies directement par Bouygues Telecom, et non sur ce que le chatbot croit savoir.
On a fait le test en simulant une recherche de forfait mobile doté d'une grosse enveloppe data pour la France et à l'étranger, et le parcours se fait dans la fenêtre de ChatGPT jusqu'au bout, ou presque. Le site de l'opérateur ne prend le relais qu'à l'ultime étape, typiquement pour valider son panier, et effectivement, ça fonctionne ! Nous avons été jusqu'à la redirection sur le site Bouygues Telecom, et en quelques clics, nous aurions pu effectivement souscrire à l'offre.
Romain Moloney, le directeur du Digital de Bouygues Telecom, explique l'arrivée de l'opérateur sur ChatGPT par sa volonté « d'offrir à nos clients une expérience toujours plus fluide et enrichie ». Et il ne boude pas son plaisir, d'ailleurs. « Nous sommes fiers d'être le premier opérateur en France à proposer nos services directement au sein de ChatGPT », ajoute-t-il.
Bouygues Telecom, un pari sur l'IA qui ne date pas d'hier
Il n'est pas franchement étonnant de retrouver Bouygues Telecom ici, dans ChatGPT. L'opérateur glisse de l'intelligence artificielle dans ses outils de relation client depuis 2017, avant d'accélérer avec l'IA générative. En 2023 sont arrivés les résumés automatiques d'appels, puis en 2024 un assistant d'aide au choix du smartphone sur le site, étendu à tout le catalogue en 2025. Cette année, il a été rejoint par un vendeur virtuel 100 % vocal sur le site web et par des assistants d'aide dans l'application mobile. ChatGPT vient compléter cette sorte de panoplie, un peu comme un canal de contact de plus avec les clients.
Jusqu'ici, sur le marché français, l'IA a surtout pris la forme d'un cadeau glissé dans les forfaits. En février 2025, Free a offert un an de Le Chat Pro, l'assistant du français Mistral AI, à ses abonnés mobiles, et Bouygues Telecom a répliqué dans la foulée avec douze mois de Perplexity Pro. Orange a suivi en incluant un an de ChatGPT Plus dans une offre 5G+. Quant à son partenariat avec OpenAI, noué en 2025, il porte sur le déploiement de modèles ouverts dans ses infrastructures et sur son support client, pas sur une application dans ChatGPT.
Le pari de Bouygues Telecom est d'une autre nature. Ici, il s'agit de chercher et convaincre les clients là où ils posent déjà leurs questions. Pour un opérateur qui compte 27,4 millions de clients mobile (objets connectés inclus) et 5,5 millions de clients fixe, c'est un virage très important. « Notre présence sur ChatGPT confirme notre leadership en matière d'intelligence artificielle », affirme Romain Moloney, pour qui l'IA constitue « un axe majeur » du plan stratégique CAP 2030. À notre connaissance, aucun rival n'a encore sauté le pas. Si cela se confirme, le titre de pionnier lui revient, au moins jusqu'à ce que la concurrence se réveille.

articles.title: Tallia raises €4 million to bring AI-powered research and review to tax firms | EU-Startups
articles.text:
London-based AI startup Tallia, formerly known as Revax, has secured €4 million ($4.5 million) in Seed funding to expand its AI-powered research and drafting platform for tax and accountancy professionals.
The round was co-led by Outward VC and the Institute of Chartered Accountants in England and Wales (ICAEW), with participation from Portfolio Ventures, Expedite Capital, Paul Forster, Angus Miln and several angel investors.
“We are delighted to support co-founders Jack Mander and Alex Bartlam, building trusted AI systems for ambitious tax teams,” said Outward VC in a public statement.
The funding follows several European investments in AI-powered tax and accounting technology during 2026.
Germany’s mika raised €6 million to develop its AI-native accounting and tax platform, while Belgium’s Dytto secured €1.5 million for an AI assistant supporting accounting firms. Italy’s A-Cube attracted €4 million for digital tax compliance, and UK-based Zalos raised €3.1 million for AI-driven enterprise finance automation.
Together with Tallia, funding in this space during 2026 reached approximately €35.6 million in financing.
Founded in 2025 by school friends Jack Mander and Alexander Bartlam, Tallia combines experience in professional tax advisory with expertise in engineering and technology.
The founders established Tallia to address a challenge facing tax professionals: how to use generative AI to accelerate research and drafting without compromising the accuracy, traceability and professional judgement required when advising clients.
Unlike general-purpose AI assistants, Tallia has been designed around the requirements of tax practices, where answers must be supported by legislation, regulatory guidance and case law. Its platform uses a custom retrieval system to connect AI-generated responses with relevant tax authorities, helping advisers verify the information before incorporating it into client deliverables.
One of the platform’s central features is its ability to combine external tax knowledge with a firm’s internal expertise. By connecting to existing documents, contracts, templates and previous work, Tallia aims to enable advisers to produce research and drafts that reflect their organisation’s established practices and knowledge.
The technology also incorporates structured review workflows, allowing senior professionals to examine the reasoning and supporting evidence behind AI-generated work.
The platform supports workflows across Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook, allowing tax professionals to incorporate AI-assisted research and drafting into familiar software. According to Tallia, its system can produce a fully cited first draft in an average of 30 seconds, while teams using the platform save an average of five hours per fee earner each week.
With its new funding, Tallia intends to expand adoption of its platform among tax and accountancy firms, helping professionals spend less time on repetitive research and initial drafting while retaining control over the advice delivered to clients.

articles.title: Exclusive: Rivian spinout Also was working on an e-moto project in Kenya — until it walked away
articles.text:
Also, the micromobility startup spun out of Rivian in 2025, quietly started and then walked away from an electric two-wheeler pilot project in Kenya earlier this year, as it sought to focus its resources on its consumer e-bike and autonomous vehicle ambitions, TechCrunch has learned.
The project received grant funding from the Shell Foundation, an independent charity established by the British oil and gas giant Shell plc. A section of the Shell Foundation’s website that has since been removed said the project’s goal was to “enable and de-risk global OEM entry into Africa’s EV market by piloting a locally integrated electric two-wheeler platform in Kenya, with potential to scale across East Africa.”
According to the deleted section, Also was expected to work on modular battery designs and distributed EV charging, and planned on “developing a purpose-built electric motorcycle for African riders.”
The opportunity for electric motorcycles seems ripe on the continent, which has a massive two-wheeler market. African mobility company Spiro recently said it has more than 130,000 electric motorcycles operating across seven countries, along with 2,500 battery-swapping stations. This boom has drawn interest from Chinese mobility companies and investors, which are pouring resources into the space.
In a September email, Also told TechCrunch that it had “explored this project” with an unnamed partner, but ultimately “decided to focus on its core roadmap” after completing only “some early-stage work.” Also said the grant funding it received from the Shell Foundation “will follow the project to support its ongoing development,” but declined to offer specifics.
The Shell Foundation told TechCrunch in an email that the project was “intended to generate evidence on driver income uplift potential, operational performance and commercial viability to deepen the company’s understanding of the market opportunity.” But when TechCrunch asked for more specifics, the Shell Foundation declined, citing a nondisclosure agreement with Also. Days later, the project disappeared from the Shell Foundation’s website.
During an interview last month at TechCrunch Disrupt, Also co-founder and president Chris Yu said the Kenya pilot project initially made sense given Also’s mission to build small, purpose-built vehicles that are “first and foremost cost-optimized to do the job that needs to be done in a particular market.”
But other projects took precedence, Yu said, especially the development of small autonomous vehicles — which Also is working on as part of a partnership with DoorDash.
“We piloted and ultimately decided, largely because of just urgency and pace around autonomy, frankly, that our attention would be best, in the near term, served fully focused” on that, he said, adding that he thinks there’s a “high chance that autonomy will show up first, and at a broader scale in these types of purpose-built smaller vehicles than at scale in passenger vehicles.”
Also walked away from the Africa project during a somewhat rocky first year of independence.
Supply chain problems forced the company to repeatedly delay deliveries of its first product, a premium e-bike called the TM-B, frustrating customers who had reserved one. What made matters worse was Also’s relative silence. The company said little for much of 2026 about when the bikes would arrive — a communication failure its leadership now acknowledges was a mistake.
“I think we did a pretty poor job communicating to our reservation holders through the summer when they were all waiting, and we got called out for that,” Yu said in the interview. “But I think it’s actually great. It’s really hard to earn the opportunity for people to care, and to tell us what they think, and to help us improve.”
Getting its first product launch back on track is crucial for Also, which has ambitions far beyond e-bikes. The company plans to sell commercial cargo bikes to companies like Amazon, including four-wheeled models, and has the partnership with DoorDash. These products are next in the company’s pipeline, Yu said, and represent bigger revenue opportunities.
But the TM-B comes first. It’s Also’s most visible product to consumers, and its striking design has drawn plenty of curiosity.
Yu said no single problem was responsible for delaying the bikes, which finally started shipping to customers in early October. Instead, Also spent much of the year playing supply chain Whac-A-Mole, a particularly difficult challenge given the TM-B’s complexity. Yu described the bike as “kind of a computer on wheels.”
At one point, Also found itself competing for the same raw materials used to make printed circuit boards for AI data centers. At other times, the company struggled to navigate certification requirements with different government agencies.
Yu said the scope of these problems, and the pace at which new ones popped up — almost weekly — made it difficult to give customers reliable updates about why their bikes were delayed.
“The entire team is like running at a million miles an hour to get these things produced and shipped to customers, and then it’s also really dynamic as well,” he said. “I think what we could have done better is just [say], straight up: ‘We’re chasing down these things, we’ll have an update shortly.’”
That didn’t happen at first, but Also has steadily improved its communication, earning some goodwill from customers on Reddit. The company will need it as it works through the inevitable kinks that come with a first product. Early customers have already reported problems, including delivery damage and noticeable battery drain.

articles.title: Board makers are running out of GeForce RTX 50 GPUs, so distributors are pushing old RTX 3060s instead
articles.text:
Facepalm: Nearly two years after launch, it should be easy for a graphics card distributor to order Nvidia's RTX 50-series cards in bulk. In China, however, some board makers reportedly can't supply enough of them anymore. They're now steering distributors toward the RTX 3060 and RTX 3050 instead, two cards that first hit shelves back in 2021 and 2022, respectively.
Chinese supply chain outlet ChannelGate first reported the shift. According to the outlet, some manufacturers have already run out of RTX 50 stock. The ones that haven't are reportedly shipping what's left in small batches at higher prices.
Essentially, rather than leave distributors with nothing to sell, makers are pointing them toward the RTX 3060 in its 12GB and 8GB versions. The RTX 3050 makes the cut as well. So do a few AMD Radeon cards, though the report doesn't name them. Even so, ChannelGate doesn't expect any of these cards to become cheaper. If anything, the outlet thinks prices on older products could creep up a little.
As for the shortage itself, ChannelGate blames a fresh wave of demand from cryptocurrency miners. China's busy online shopping season is reportedly draining stock, too. It also doesn't help that the RTX 50 lineup was already running thin, since Nvidia reportedly cut production earlier this year amid the AI-driven memory crunch.
In fact, the RTX 3060 only came out of retirement a few months ago. In July, the card landed on Newegg in the US for $329.99, the same price it launched at in 2021.
That price didn't last long, though. By August, the same MSI model had climbed to $479.99. That's about $180 more than Newegg was charging for the newer and faster RTX 5050 at the time.
Meanwhile, the RTX 3060 has also reclaimed the top spot in Valve's October Steam Hardware Survey. It now sits on 3.62% of surveyed systems, just ahead of the RTX 5070 at 3.56%. The newer card had grabbed the lead in September before dropping 2.30 points this month.
System memory flipped back, too. 16GB of RAM is once again the most common amount, found in 41.42% of systems. 32GB had overtaken it in September but now sits at 37.06%.
The October numbers don't mean gamers suddenly ditched their RTX 5070s, though. Hardware Busters traced the swing to Steam's language breakdown. Users running the client in Simplified Chinese dropped from roughly 31% of respondents in September to just under 22% in October. Valve doesn't adjust its results by region, so when fewer players from China take part, the newer midrange cards popular there slide down the charts. A similar spike in Chinese respondents briefly put the RTX 5070 on top back in February, too.

Black November: Galaxy S25 Ultra (512 GB) despenca de preço na Amazon
Galaxy S25 Ultra (512 GB) traz tela de 120 Hz e câmera de 200 MP; celular premium da Samsung sai por menos da metade do preço no Pix no mês da Black Friday
O Galaxy S25 Ultra de 512 GB está em oferta por R$ 5.698 no Pix na Amazon. O celular premium da Samsung, que conta com tela AMOLED de 120 Hz e câmera wide de 200 MP, sai 53% mais em conta em comparação ao preço original de R$ 11.999.
O S25 Ultra entrega processamento de ponta com o chip Qualcomm Snapdragon 8 Elite e os 12 GB de RAM, um kit que sustenta apps pesados e soluções do Galaxy AI localmente. Os 512 GB de espaço interno dão e sobram para guardar vídeos e fotos.
Seu kit principal de câmeras filma em 8K. Ele inclui wide de 200 MP com OIS e ultrawide de 50 MP, que captam belas cenas ao ar livre, telefoto de 10 MP com zoom óptico de 3x e periscópica de 50 MP e 5x para aproximações com qualidade. A frontal de 12 MP tira ótimas selfies e filma em 4K a 60 fps.

O corpo de titânio do S25 Ultra é revestido de ambos os lados pelo vidro Gorilla Armor 2, resistente a riscos e arranhões, enquanto a certificação IP68 confere proteção contra poeira intensa e mergulhos acidentais.
Sua bateria de 5.000 mAh resiste a até 31 horas de reprodução de vídeo, segundo a Samsung. O suporte ao carregamento rápido de 45 W via USB-C e de 15 W sem fio permite uso prolongado por um dia inteiro, e não deixará o usuário na mão.
O Galaxy S25 Ultra de 512 GB (R$ 5.865 no Pix) será atualizado até o Android 22 e possui conectividade 5G, Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 5.4 e NFC.

articles.title: Global Semiconductor Sales Increase 24.1% From Q2 2026 to Q3 2026
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 3rd 2026
Global Semiconductor Sales Increase 24.1% From Q2 2026 to Q3 2026
The Semiconductor Industry Association (SIA) today announced global semiconductor sales were $517.7 billion during the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 24.1% compared to the second quarter of 2026. Global sales were $172.6 billion during the month of September 2026, an increase of 146.8% compared to September 2025 and 7.9% more than sales in August 2026. Monthly sales are compiled by the World Semiconductor Trade Statistics (WSTS) organization and represent a three-month moving average.
Michael Robbins, SIA president and CEO"The global chip market grew substantially throughout the third quarter of this year, with worldwide sales increasing by more than 20% quarter-to-quarter for the third consecutive quarter. Year-to-year semiconductor sales remained strong across all major regional markets, highlighting the industry's global reach and its indispensable role in powering innovation, productivity, and economic competitiveness."
Regionally, year-to-year sales in September were up in the Americas (191.7%), Asia Pacific/All Other (141.4%), China (124.9%), Europe (102.5%), and Japan (73.4%). Month-to-month sales in September increased in the Americas (11.0%), Japan (8.7%), Europe (8.1%), Asia Pacific/All Other (6.9%), and China (4.2%).

articles.title: EPA throws in the towel on policing air pollution from factory farms
articles.text:
The Environmental Protection Agency late last week announced it would end a 20-plus-year effort to develop methods to monitor air pollution from factory farms, effectively shuttering the agency’s stop-and-start attempts to regulate the potentially pollutant-spewing facilities under the Clean Air Act.
The announcement came just days before the midterm elections and was characterized by the agency as a long-awaited reprieve for farmers, a historically important constituency for Trump and the Republican Party.
When tens of thousands of animals are packed into one place, pollution from their waste is blown from ventilation fans or emanates from giant lagoons of liquid effluent. Livestock facilities emit fine particulate matter, ammonia, nitrogen oxides, sulfur dioxide, and volatile organic compounds, all contributing to a toxic mix. Research has shown that emissions from these operations are a major cause of air pollution, causing nearly 12,700 deaths in the United States a year.
Strictly speaking, concentrated animal feeding operations, or CAFOs, are required to get permits under the Clean Air Act and report emissions of these pollutants under the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation and Liability and Act and the Emergency Planning and Community Right-to-Know Act. But through a deal crafted in tandem with the EPA and the livestock industry, they’ve been given amnesty from doing so for more than 20 years.
The arrangement goes back to the early 2000s when the agency attempted to prosecute CAFOs for exceeding limits on some of these pollutants. The industry pushed back, arguing there was no adequate way of measuring them. So the agency worked with industry groups to develop what was dubbed the Air Consent Agreement, through which the EPA granted thousands of CAFOs safe harbor from legal action in exchange for their participation in a study that was funded by the industry.

articles.title: 'GTA 6' confirma fecha y hora de la precarga: desde cuándo lo podrás instalar en tu PS5 o Xbox
articles.text:
Cada día que pasa, el hype por GTA 6 está un poco más alto. El nuevo juego de Rockstar Games estará disponible a partir del jueves 19 de noviembre y tiene todo para ser el lanzamiento más grande de la historia de los videojuegos. Con tamaña expectativa, toda noticia sobre su lanzamiento dispara la ilusión de los fanáticos.
Hoy, Rockstar ha confirmado la fecha y el horario de inicio de la precarga de GTA 6; es decir, desde cuándo se podrá descargar el juego completo en PS5 y Xbox Series X|S antes de que se libere para comenzar a jugarlo.
El estudio menciona que la precarga de GTA 6 se iniciará el próximo martes 10 de noviembre. Esto significa que el nuevo Grand Theft Auto VI podrá residir en tu consola con poco más de una semana de antelación a su debut formal, lo que seguro no será de mucha ayuda para tu ansiedad.
Tengamos en cuenta que la precarga o descarga anticipada de un juego implica que este se puede instalar al completo en la plataforma, pero que no se puede jugar hasta el día de lanzamiento. Lo que esto permite es disminuir las horas de espera, algo crucial cuando se trata de propuestas tan anticipadas como GTA 6, así como evitar un potencial colapso de las tiendas al momento de su debut. Así, el día del estreno solo tienes que instalar un pequeño parche que quita el cifrado de los archivos y desbloquea el acceso.
Los horarios de precarga de GTA 6 en PS5 y Xbox Series X|S
Como ya dijimos, la precarga de GTA 6 estará disponible tanto en PS5 como en Xbox Series X|S el próximo 10 de noviembre. Sin embargo, los horarios no serán los mismos para las dos plataformas. En el caso de la consola de Sony, los usuarios podrán comenzar a descargar el juego a partir de la medianoche de su zona horaria. Esto quiere decir que en Oceanía y Asia serán los primeros en poder iniciar el procedimiento, que gradualmente se abrirá al resto del mundo.
Por su parte, los usuarios de Xbox Series X|S sí tendrán de un horario único a nivel global a partir del cual la precarga de GTA 6 estará habilitada. Para ser más específicos, el inicio de la descarga se activará a las 00:00 horas GMT; es decir:
- 01:00 horas de España;
- 21:00 horas del 9 de noviembre en Argentina;
- 18:00 horas del 9 de noviembre en México.
Tanto la fecha como el horario de la precarga de GTA 6 corresponden a las descargas digitales desde las tiendas de PS5 y Xbox. Rockstar ha menciona que las versiones en "físico", que no incluyen un disco sino que traen un código de descarga dentro de la caja, deberían estar disponibles en tiendas minoristas a partir del 12 de noviembre.
Por último, el estudio también ha confirmado cuánto espacio ocupará el archivo de precarga de GTA 6: 212 GB. Así que asegúrate de desocupar el almacenamiento de tu consola con tiempo para garantizar que podrás instalar el nuevo Grand Theft Auto antes de su lanzamiento oficial.

articles.title: Rockstar a avancé la date : GTA 6 pourra être téléchargé dans 7 jours (il pesera 212 Go)
articles.text:
Préparez-vous à faire de la place sur votre console. Les joueurs qui ont précommandé GTA 6 en version numérique pourront commencer à le télécharger dès le mardi 10 novembre. Rockstar Games l’a annoncé ce 3 novembre dans un billet publié sur son site officiel.
C’est deux jours plus tôt que prévu. En juin, lors de l’ouverture des précommandes, Take-Two, la maison mère de Rockstar, avait annoncé le 12 novembre. Une bonne nouvelle pour les joueurs qui disposent d’une connexion lente, puisqu’ils auront davantage de temps pour récupérer les fichiers du jeu, qui nécessiteront jusqu’à 212 Go d’espace libre.
Le préchargement permet d’installer un jeu à l’avance, sans pouvoir y jouer avant sa sortie officielle, fixée au 19 novembre. Sur PS5, il débutera à minuit, heure locale, soit dans la nuit du lundi 9 au mardi 10 novembre en France. Sur Xbox Series X|S, le téléchargement sera disponible au même moment partout dans le monde, à minuit GMT, soit 1 heure du matin à Paris.
En revanche, les joueurs qui préfèrent les versions physiques devront patienter deux jours supplémentaires. Les boîtes de GTA 6, qui ne contiennent pas de disque mais un code de téléchargement, arriveront chez les revendeurs le 12 novembre.
Combien de place faut-il libérer pour GTA 6 ?
Rockstar Games confirme que le préchargement nécessitera « jusqu’à 212 Go » d’espace libre, selon la console utilisée. L’éditeur ne précise toutefois pas le poids exact de chaque version.
Fin octobre, le compte X PlayStation Game Size, spécialisé dans l’analyse des données du PlayStation Store, avait évoqué un poids de 210 Go sur PS5. L’annonce de Rockstar vient donc conforter cette première estimation, même si l’espace nécessaire au préchargement ne correspond pas forcément à la taille définitive du jeu.
Sur les premières PS5 commercialisées en 2020, comme sur la PS5 Slim révisée vendue en Europe depuis 2025, le SSD de 825 Go ne laisse que 667 Go de stockage utilisable. GTA 6 pourrait donc occuper près d’un tiers de cet espace à lui seul. Les premières PS5 Slim, avec 848 Go utilisables, et la PS5 Pro, équipée d’un SSD de 2 To, disposent d’une marge plus confortable.
La situation pourrait être encore plus compliquée sur Xbox Series S. Sur le modèle doté d’un SSD de 512 Go, seuls 364 Go sont réellement disponibles. Si GTA 6 nécessite bien 212 Go sur cette console, il occupera plus de la moitié de son stockage. Rockstar n’a toutefois pas précisé si cette version sera moins volumineuse que les autres.
L’éditeur recommande donc aux joueurs de libérer suffisamment d’espace avant le début du préchargement. Les précommandes restent ouvertes pour celles et ceux qui souhaitent prendre de l’avance.
Rockstar réserve également un petit bonus pour le jour de la sortie. Le 19 novembre, les joueurs pourront télécharger gratuitement une affiche à imprimer ainsi qu’une carte de Leonida, l’État fictif inspiré de la Floride dans lequel se déroule GTA 6. Une version papier recto verso de l’affiche sera aussi proposée à 0,99 dollar (environ 0,90 €) sur la boutique officielle, ou offerte avec un achat.
Reste une inconnue : l’heure à laquelle le jeu sera jouable, que Rockstar ne communique toujours pas. D’après les fiches du PlayStation Store, GTA 6 devrait se débloquer à minuit, heure locale, dans chaque pays. Selon cette information, les Néo-Zélandais ouvriront donc le bal dès le 18 novembre à midi, heure de Paris, douze heures avant la France. Ce décalage fera le bonheur des spoilers sur les réseaux sociaux, mais aussi des joueurs Xbox prêts à changer la région de leur console pour jouer à GTA 6 avant sa sortie. Pour l’instant, Rockstar n’a pas confirmé ces horaires et le lancement à l’heure locale.

articles.title: Le surprenant Dyson Pencilvac Fluffycones, noté 8/10, est bradé à -30 % au Black Friday — Frandroid
articles.text:
Malgré l’arrivée des robots aspirateurs, Dyson continue de proposer des aspirateurs balais innovants. La marque a sorti l’année dernière le PencilVac Fluffycones, un engin avec un design particulier qui se présente avec un simple tube sans poignée. L’aspirateur est sorti à près de 500 euros. Un prix important que Boulanger essaie d’atténuer pendant le Black Friday avec une réduction de 30 %.
Les points forts du Dyson PencilVac Fluffycones :
- Un design particulier qui détonne avec le reste du marché
- La brosse Fluffycones qui empêche tout emmêlement
- Une puissance de 55 AirWatts avec une aspiration efficace le long des plinthes
Sorti à 499,99 euros, le Dyson PencilVac Fluffycones est actuellement disponible pour 349,99 euros chez Boulanger.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant le Dyson PencilVac Fluffycones. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Un design futuriste
Avec son PencilVac Fluffycones, Dyson propose un aspirateur balai qui sort de l’ordinaire. Ces appareils se composent habituellement d’un manche et d’une poignée pour la prise en main, ce qui n’est pas le cas ici. Le produit de Dyson se présente avec un simple tube. Cette conception permet à l’aspirateur d’être particulièrement maniable puisque l’on a l’impression qu’il s’agit d’une extension de notre bras. Cependant, sans zone de préhension définie, l’aspirateur peut avoir tendance à glisser des mains.
Avant de parler des performances de l’appareil, un petit mot sur sa station de recharge. Dyson a opté pour un support magnétique, il suffit de poser l’aspirateur dessus et il chargera.
Pour l’aspiration, Dyson innove aussi avec la brosse Fluffycones. Il s’agit de quatre cônes motorisés qui ne possèdent pas de bordures en plastique. Par conséquent, les rouleaux touchent directement les plinthes, ce qui offre un nettoyage plus précis.
Un nettoyage en toute fluidité
Si le design particulier de ce Dyson PencilVac Fluffycones peut poser quelques problèmes de prise en main lors des premiers passages, force est de constater qu’une fois que l’on a le coup de poignet, le nettoyage est agréable. La brosse pivote à 360° pour passer facilement autour des pieds de table.
Du côté des performances, l’aspirateur souffle le chaud et le froid. La puissance de 55 AirWatts permettra d’aspirer les poussières et les miettes, mais l’aspirateur montrera quelques faiblesses pour les éléments les plus gros comme les feuilles. Pour ne rater aucune miette, deux lumières vertes sont présentes à l’avant et à l’arrière de la brosse. Si vous possédez un animal de compagnie, la brosse est équipée d’un système anti-emmêlement. À noter que cet aspirateur balai se destine aux sols durs et sera peu efficace sur les tapis et la moquette.
L’autonomie est une petite déception. Selon le mode choisi, l’aspirateur tiendra entre huit et 30 minutes. Pour ne pas être surpris par un arrêt soudain de l’appareil, un écran LCD est présent, indiquant l’autonomie restante.
