articles.title: Why AI-powered intelligence is every winning brand’s secret sauce
articles.text:
Why AI-powered intelligence is every winning brand’s secret sauce
As AI reshapes ecommerce, brands are shifting focus from customer acquisition to intelligent fulfilment, inventory management and customer experience. This article explores how AI and agentic systems enable smarter, faster operational decisions.
For years, the playbook for building a winning consumer brand was simple: a compelling product, a strong brand identity, and smart customer acquisition. Those fundamentals still hold, but they no longer decide who wins.
Today's battle is fought in fragments of attention, where brands have seconds to convert interest into a purchase. And the moment “Buy Now” is clicked, a second, harder battle begins: fast fulfilment, a seamless delivery experience, and effortless handling of queries and returns - the moments that actually earn loyalty.
Amid endless channels and ever-shifting marketing strategies, the real differentiator has moved downstream: it's the intelligence behind every operational decision made after the click.
Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming this intelligence layer. No longer limited to chatbots or content generation, AI is transforming how brands forecast demand, allocate inventory, orchestrate fulfilment, engage customers, and optimise operations in real time.
This shift comes at a time when commerce itself has grown far more complex. Consumers now discover, evaluate, and buy across a maze of touchpoints - brand websites, marketplaces, quick commerce, social commerce, and physical stores - often within a single purchase journey. Powering every one of those purchases is a complex web of inventory nodes, warehouses, logistics partners, and engagement systems that must move in perfect synchronisation.
For brands, this translates into a flood of operational data. Every inventory movement, customer interaction, order update, warehouse scan, and delivery milestone becomes a signal that can influence the next business decision. What begins as a simple online business quickly turns into a web of real-time, interconnected decisions - each one shaping the customer experience.
Until a few years ago, brands and marketplaces operated on Systems of Record - a single source of operational truth that captured transactions and helped manage inventory. Ecommerce enablement SaaS platforms turned these Systems of Insight - real-time dashboards and analytics that let businesses move from reactive to data-driven decision-making.
The next phase of this evolution is now underway. Building on this rich data and technology-enabled processes, these Systems of Record and Insight are becoming Systems of Intelligence - where AI is not just analysing information, but actively framing recommendations and executing decisions across business operations.
Consider a fashion retailer during a festive sale. Thousands of orders may arrive simultaneously across its website, marketplaces, and quick commerce platforms. Instead of relying on manual rules or static workflows, AI can continuously evaluate inventory availability, warehouse capacity, delivery timelines, shipping costs, and customer location before automatically routing each order through the most efficient fulfilment path. It can also spot that a fast-moving product is about to run out in one city while stock sits healthy elsewhere and line up a transfer before availability ever becomes the customer's problem.
This matters even more in an omnichannel world, where customers expect availability wherever and however they shop. Delivering on that promise takes more than inventory visibility - it demands continuous coordination across allocation, order orchestration, warehouse operations, logistics, and customer communication. AI makes that coordination possible at a scale and speed manual decision-making simply can't match.
The next frontier here is Agentic AI. Unlike traditional automation, which follows predefined workflows, Agentic AI can reason across multiple variables, recommend the next best course of action, and autonomously execute routine operational decisions within business-defined guardrails. Whether prioritising high-value orders during peak demand, responding to supply chain disruptions, or flagging fulfilment bottlenecks before they bite, these systems move beyond supporting human decisions to actively driving them.
This marks a fundamental shift in how brands approach growth. Acquiring customers remains critical, but sustainable growth increasingly depends on what happens after demand is generated. Rather than adding operational headcount every time order volumes spike, businesses are investing in intelligent platforms that let them scale without proportionately scaling complexity. The goal is no longer simply to process more orders - it's to make better operational decisions, faster and more consistently.
Ecommerce enablement platforms, with deep data and operational ties into brands, are already building this future. AI-first SaaS tools are no longer just software - they're becoming operational partners, continuously improving how the business runs.
Tomorrow's market leaders won't necessarily be the brands with the biggest marketing budgets. They'll be the brands whose technology lets them operate smarter, adapt faster, and make better decisions every single day. Their competitive advantage will increasingly come from the intelligence behind every business decision they make.
(Kapil Makhija is the MD & CEO of Unicommerce eSolutions Limited)

articles.title: Si acabas de empezar en el gimnasio, esta es la respuesta que buscas: cuánto tarda el músculo en crecer
articles.text:
Cuando comenzamos a ir al gimnasio, buscamos tener resultados cuanto antes, llegando al punto de que se han generado muchos memes alrededor de este fenómeno. Y para resolver este misterio, son varios los estudios que han ido surgiendo sobre cuánto tiempo tenemos que dedicar a nuestro entrenamiento para ver finalmente un poco más de músculo en los brazos o en las piernas.
La ganancia inicial. En redes sociales es bastante frecuente ver cómo se promete que en las primeras semanas es cuando hay una gran ganancia muscular. Esto es algo que puede crear cualquiera, puesto que en el momento de acabar un ejercicio y en las horas posteriores es frecuente ver el músculo 'hinchado'.
Es un espejismo. Aquí un estudio clásico publicado en 2016 analizó a 10 jóvenes no entrenados para entender qué ocurría en las primeras semanas de entrenamiento. Lo que vieron fue que en la semana 3, el área de sus cuádriceps había aumentado un 2,7% y a las 10 semanas un 10,4%. El problema es que este aumento tan prematuro estaba acompañado de edema inducido por el daño muscular, por lo que este cambio en el volumen no debe etiquetarse como hipertrofia pura sin descontar la inflamación.
Esto mismo se vio también en un estudio hecho en 2011, donde tras medir semanalmente a 25 hombres sedentarios se concluyó que la hipertrofia estructural y real no empieza a consolidarse hasta las semanas 3 o 4, alcanzando un +9,6% a las 8 semanas. Pero ese "crecimiento" es en gran medida debido a la reparación del daño que se ha hecho sobre el músculo.
Un gran trabajo. Este mismo año se ha publicado un metaanálisis que se encuentra en proceso de revisión y que está firmado por referentes de la investigación deportiva. En este se analizan 2.237 observaciones extraídas de 480 estudios diferentes, filtrando solo aquellos que midieron el crecimiento muscular mediante resonancia o ecografía, dejando fuera las mediciones más subjetivas con básculas de bioimpedancia.
En este modelo se confirma que el músculo crece con el tiempo, pero arroja una curva de rendimientos decrecientes. Se dice esto porque el aumento medio muscular es de un 8,9% a las 20 semanas, un 9,4% a las 24, un 10,5% a las 36 y un 12,6% al año y medio. Como vemos, no sigue un crecimiento lineal, sino que conforme vamos avanzando en las sesiones de entrenamiento, nos encontramos con un músculo que cuesta más que crezca, lo que puede terminar desmotivando a seguir entrenando.
Interviene la genética. Con estos porcentajes es fácil marcarse unos objetivos claros y decir que si entreno durante 20 semanas, voy a tener casi un 10% más de músculo en el cuerpo, pero la realidad es que cada persona es completamente diferente. Aquí, un estudio publicado en 2005 sometió a 585 personas a 12 semanas de entrenamiento y determinó que el tamaño muscular varió entre una pérdida del 2% y una ganancia del 59%.
Esto hace que debamos concienciarnos de que cada persona va a un ritmo diferente a la hora de hacer un cambio físico que pase por una ganancia muscular y que no hablamos de una ciencia exacta. De esta manera, si dos personas van a entrenar juntas y hacen la misma cantidad de ejercicios, es posible que una de ellas vea antes los resultados esperados.

articles.title: Ya está disponible: Bizum amplía los pagos en España y los compradores pueden pagar en tiendas físicas sin necesidad de tarjeta, siempre que acepten el servicio
articles.text:
Con el pago presencial es posible realizar operaciones en tiendas físicas. Basta con pasar el móvil por el datáfono. Así se carga directamente en nuestra cuenta bancaria. Para poder hacerlo sin tarjeta, es preciso que el servicio esté activado en nuestro banco y en el establecimiento. Tener Bizum para enviar dinero a los amigos no es suficiente para poder pagar en la caja de cualquier tienda.
El despliegue de pago presencial ha empezado el pasado mayo. Después ha llegado el lanzamiento de Bizum Pay para las tiendas de apps (Android e iPhone). Se trata de una transferencia inmediata entre cuentas; por tanto, no pasamos por una tarjeta (Visa/Mastercard) para realizar la operación. Desde nuestra aplicación de banco o desde la cartera de Bizum podemos hacerlo.
Es similar a otros tipos de pago desde móvil. Preparamos el teléfono y lo pasamos por el terminal. En este caso, utilizamos la tecnología NFC (comunicación de corto alcance). Es un pago sin contacto; la diferencia es que el dinero viene de nuestra cuenta vinculada a Bizum.
Para nosotros es gratis. En el caso del comercio, puede haber comisiones pactadas con su entidad; además, que el datáfono esté preparado no significa que nuestro banco nos haya activado el servicio.
Cómo activar y utilizar Bizum Pay
Para empezar a utilizar Bizum Pay, tenemos que instalar la app. Es necesario activarla. En el caso de Bizum, tenemos varias opciones para activar esta función. Una es desde la nueva app, introduciendo nuestro número de teléfono de registro en el servicio, y otra opción es desde nuestra app de banco, en el apartado Bizum Pay. En el primer caso nos lleva a nuestra entidad para finalizar el alta.
Posteriormente, podemos indicar que queremos que sea nuestra aplicación predeterminada de pago. De hecho, en el momento de activarla nos pregunta si queremos hacerlo.
También tenemos la opción de modificarlo posteriormente desde los ajustes de nuestro teléfono. En la guía de cómo configurar Bizum Pay podemos ver cómo hacerlo en Android e iOS.
Es importante saber, como explica CaixaBank en sus condiciones de pago presencial, que en aquellos establecimientos donde no esté disponible el pago desde cuenta, podemos utilizar las tarjetas que hemos añadido en nuestra aplicación. Para ello es necesario que tengamos alguna tarjeta compatible añadida. Si queremos pagar solo con Bizum, debemos asegurarnos de que la tienda lo admite.
En el caso de Bizum, se explica en su documentación de límites que no tienen límites en los pagos en tiendas y establecimientos. Los límites los pueden poner los bancos tanto en Bizum como en las tarjetas que utilicen desde la cartera. El importe máximo hay que consultarlo con nuestra entidad.

articles.title: AMD's Zen 7 "Grimlock" APUs with RDNA 5+ graphics may not arrive until 2029
articles.text:
Rumor mill: The latest rumors and announcements have assembled a tentative roadmap for AMD's mobile hardware lineup over the next few years. Recent reports suggest that Sony's rumored handheld game system will have exclusive access to AMD's highly anticipated RDNA 5 architecture for some time. It might not appear in off-the-shelf form factors until 2029, by which time Zen 7 will likely be ready.
Prominent leaker Kepler_L2 recently claimed that AMD APUs featuring "RDNA 5+" iGPUs and Zen 7 CPU cores will be available in early 2029. The statement amounts to some of the earliest concrete information about Zen 7 chips for consumer devices.
Earlier reports from Kepler and Digital Foundry indicate that a leaked handheld SoC from Sony, codenamed Canis, is currently the only mobile product in development to feature AMD's next GPU architecture, RDNA 5. Kepler claimed that AMD won't offer RDNA 5 to PC manufacturers like Valve, ASUS, or MSI because they couldn't guarantee shipments of at least 10 million units, AMD's minimum threshold. The leaker has since defended the claim, sparking speculation about when RDNA 5 might become available to OEM handhelds and other devices.
In response, Kepler stated RDNA 5+ will come to APUs in 2029 along with "Grimlock," the codename for AMD's Zen 7 CPU architecture. Adding a plus symbol to RDNA 5 indicates that the APUs will feature enhancements following the architecture's initial launch. OEM handhelds released between now and then, potentially including one from Microsoft, will likely use AMD's upcoming Ryzen Z3 series, which combines Zen 6, Zen 5, and RDNA 4m.
AMD is expected to release just one discrete desktop GPU with RDNA 5 next year, an upper-midrange or high-end card to compete with a 24GB variant of Nvidia's RTX 5080. Meanwhile, Canis, which includes Zen 6c CPU cores clocked at up to 2.2GHz with a 15w TDP, could emerge in late 2027. The handheld is expected to be a companion to the PlayStation 6, which will also use RDNA 5 and Zen 6, but the console's release window remains unclear.
The only solid information about Zen 7 concerns AMD's Epyc "Florence" server CPUs, which will launch in 2028. The architecture will shift to TSMC's A16 and A17 process nodes, bringing Ryzen chips into the angstrom era. Zen 7 aims to improve AI performance, reduce system overhead, and minimize security vulnerabilities. Zen 8 Epyc processors, codenamed "Ravenna," are coming in 2030.

articles.title: Razer Unveils the Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition
articles.text:
Tuesday, November 3rd 2026
Razer Unveils the Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition
Razer, the leading global lifestyle brand for gamers, today announced the Razer Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition, its flagship controller officially licensed for the PlayStation 5 console, built for players who want the highest level of performance and craftsmanship that has defined Razer engineering.
Introduced in 2016, the Raiju controller line has been refined over the past decade evolving into Razer's most advanced PlayStation controller ever. The Razer Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition distills that decade of experience into a single form, balancing design, weight, and performance for players on the PlayStation 5 console who refuse to compromise.Limited to an initial release of 1,337 individually serialized units, each Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition is produced through a demanding, precision-driven process - from its magnesium alloy exoskeleton to its finely detailed anodized aluminium accessory tool.
Premium Materials. Elevated Finishes.
Every material on the Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition was chosen for strength, durability, and finish. The exoskeleton is built from magnesium alloy, an exceptionally strong material that is remarkably light.
The handles are wrapped in matte black textured TPU grip that resists oils and abrasion, holding a pristine finish through extended play.
At the center sits a laser-etched glass touchpad, semi-transparent tinted and marked with the Razer logo, offering a subtle view of the open-air polygonal design underneath.
The action buttons, directional pad, and secondary inputs carry a matte black finish with tone-on-tone iconography. All are molded using a double-shot PBT process, so the legends never fade, and the surfaces resist oil build-up.
Charlie Bolton, Global Head of Design at Razer"With the Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition, we set out to illustrate what happens when Razer's engineering and design capabilities are pushed to their absolute limits. It draws on years of experience in high-performance controllers, delivering tournament-grade responsiveness in a design that feels like a statement piece in hand."
Elevated Design. Perfectly Balanced.
Beyond its materials, the Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition is defined by a design language that stands apart in the category. An open-polygonal top and back plate with chamfered edges creates a smooth, seamless feel in hand. A nano coating leaves the internal elements exposed beneath the shell while keeping it safe from debris, for a striking aesthetic. Despite its more resilient material it weighs in at a mere 260 g, delivering a well-balanced feel in hand.
Precision-Engineered. Maximum Performance.
At its core, the Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition carries Razer's lineage of high-performance gaming controllers: reliable precision, exceptional control, and blazing-fast speed. The Raiju V3 Pro features a symmetrical thumbstick layout paired with contactless TMR thumbstick sensors for high-precision aim that tracks fast-moving targets while offering increased durability.
Six mappable multi-function buttons, two claw-grip bumpers and four mouse-click back buttons, let players bind everything from slide to melee to gadgets, so their thumbs never leave the sticks.
Built for PlayStation 5 consoles and optimized for PC, it delivers up to 2,000 Hz polling with Razer HyperPolling Wireless on PC for sharper movement tracking and input registration.
Every input can be tuned to the player. Through Razer Synapse or the Razer PS mobile app, players can remap buttons, adjust thumbstick sensitivity and trigger response, and save custom profiles onboard, carrying a personalized gaming setup from the living room to the tournament floor.
A Carefully Crafted Package
Each Raiju V3 Pro Signature Edition features a suite of premium accessories to custom tailor the controller to the user's precise look and feel.
- Premium Leatherette Carrying Case: For both storage and showcase display.
- Alternative Thumbstick Caps: Short convex for speed and tall concave for precision.
- Four Swappable Back Button Covers: For creating the perfect layout and providing a flush fit and finish.
- Anodized aluminium Back Button Replacement Tool: For easily swapping in and out back buttons.
- Razer HyperSpeed Wireless Dongle: For lossless, low-latency wireless connectivity on PlayStation 5 consoles and PC.
- USB Type-A to USB Type-C Cable: For fast and reliable wired play and rapid recharging.
The Pinnacle of Razer Design and Performance
Premium materials, elevated design, and high-level performance converge in a single controller, built for PlayStation 5 players who want the Razer experience at its absolute peak.

articles.title: Bring structured and unstructured data together with Amazon Quick | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Bring structured and unstructured data together with Amazon Quick
Organizations collect data in many forms. Structured data lives in databases and spreadsheets, whereas unstructured data sits in documents, reports, and files stored across file systems. Analyzing both together typically requires switching between multiple tools, running separate queries, and manually correlating results.
Amazon Quick addresses this with a unified experience. You can connect structured data through enriched datasets and unstructured data through S3-backed knowledge bases. You can then query both through a single conversational AI agent.
In this post, you learn how to:
- Connect Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) as a data source and create a knowledge base.
- Build a Space that combines structured and unstructured data.
- Create and configure a custom chat agent that queries across both data types.
- Ask questions that span structured and unstructured sources in a single conversation.
Solution architecture
The following diagram illustrates how each component connects to deliver a unified data experience through Amazon Quick.
The architecture has three layers:
- Data layer: Your data exists in two forms. Unstructured content (documents, PDFs, reports) is stored in Amazon S3 and indexed through a knowledge base. Structured data (metrics, sales figures, and operational key performance indicators) is loaded as enriched datasets with semantic descriptions that the agent uses to translate questions into SQL.
- Workspace layer: A Space brings both data types together into a single workspace. The Space references your knowledge base for unstructured queries and your datasets for structured queries. It can also include dashboards, file uploads, and action connectors. This is the layer where data from different sources converges into a unified context.
- Agent layer: The custom chat agent links to the Space and uses it as its knowledge source. When a user asks a question, the agent determines whether to query the knowledge base, the dataset, or both, and returns a combined response with citations. Amazon Quick also applies built-in AI guardrails, such as content safety screening, to chat interactions.
With this layered approach, you can expand the solution over time. When you add a new data source to the Space, the agent linked to that Space can use it, and responses respect the permissions of the user who asks.
Prerequisites
To follow along with this walkthrough, you need:
- An Amazon Quick account with an Enterprise subscription for the user who follows this walkthrough (creating datasets requires Enterprise). For details, see Amazon Quick pricing.
- An Amazon S3 bucket for your business documents. To create one, see the Amazon S3 User Guide.
- Amazon Quick access to your S3 bucket, granted by an Amazon Quick administrator. In the admin console, the administrator chooses Permissions, then AWS resources, selects Amazon S3, and chooses Select S3 buckets. Selected buckets have read-only permissions by default.
- Permissions to create integrations, knowledge bases, datasets, spaces, and chat agents in Amazon Quick.
Prepare your sample data
This walkthrough uses two types of data:
Unstructured documents: Upload these to your Amazon S3 bucket for the knowledge base:
- AnyCompany_Business_Review.pdf
- AnyCompany_Market_Analysis_Report.pdf
- AnyCompany_Product_Strategy_Memo.pdf
Structured data: Download this file to your computer. You upload it directly to Amazon Quick in Step 3:
Step 1: Create an Amazon S3 integration
Start by connecting Amazon Quick to your S3 bucket. From the Amazon Quick console, select Knowledge in the left navigation panel.
The knowledge page shows available connector types, including Amazon Q Business, Web Crawler, Amazon S3, and third-party options like Google Drive, OneDrive, and Microsoft SharePoint.
Under Amazon S3, choose Add. In the Create S3 knowledge base dialog, on the Connect S3 bucket page, provide the following details:
- Name: A descriptive name for your integration (for example, “My Data Access Integration”).
- S3 bucket location: Choose Quick Suite instance account to use a bucket in the same AWS account as Amazon Quick, or Other AWS account for a bucket in a different account.
- S3 bucket URL: The S3 URI of the bucket containing your data. The bucket must be in the same Region as Amazon Quick.
Choose Next.
Step 2: Create a knowledge base
After the S3 integration is created, Amazon Quick prompts you to create a knowledge base. The knowledge base indexes your S3 content for AI-powered search.
Configure the knowledge base:
- Name: “Business Knowledge Base”.
- Description (optional): Notes about how the knowledge base will be used.
- Content: Select “Add all content” to index everything in the connected S3 bucket, or “Add specific content” to specify the S3 prefixes for the folders and files to include (prefix filters are case-sensitive).
Next: Additional settings opens optional settings for document-level access control lists (ACLs) and a metadata files folder. Decide whether to use ACLs before you create the knowledge base, because you can’t change that choice later. This walkthrough uses sample data, so the default settings are sufficient. For details, see Set up and manage Amazon S3 integration.
Choose Create. A success banner confirms the S3 integration, and the knowledge base begins indexing in the background.
Step 3: Create and enrich a dataset
A dataset is your structured data file loaded into Amazon Quick. By enriching the dataset with semantic descriptions, custom instructions, and correct data types, the AI agent can interpret your data more accurately. It can then translate natural language questions into SQL queries.
Create the dataset
- From the Amazon Quick home page, navigate to Data in the left navigation.
- Choose Create dataset, then select Upload file.
- Select the Product_Sales.csv file you downloaded earlier and choose Open.
- On the confirmation screen, review the column names and data types. Choose Next to create the dataset.
Amazon Quick ingests the file into SPICE (the in-memory calculation engine) and the dataset appears in your dataset list.
The dataset takes its name from the uploaded file, so it appears as Product_Sales.csv in your account.
Enrich the dataset
Enriching your dataset with semantic information helps the AI understand your data in business context. The agent uses this context to translate natural language questions into more accurate SQL queries. From the dataset page, choose Edit dataset to enter the data preparation view.
Transform: Fix data types
In the Transform tab, update data types for columns that were auto-detected incorrectly. For this dataset:
- Change Order Date and Date Key from String to Date.
- Change Customer ID from String to Integer.
- Change Sales, Discount, and Profit from String to Decimal.
- Change Quantity and Unit Price from String to Integer.
Output: Add semantic context
Select the Output tab to access the dataset-level enrichment fields. Here you provide context that helps the AI understand what your data represents and how to use it.
Description: Add a dataset-level description:
“Product sales transaction data for AnyCompany, covering orders from FY2024-FY2025 across North America, EMEA, Asia Pacific, and Latin America. Includes order details, customer information, product lines, and revenue metrics.”
Custom instructions: Add guidance for how the AI should query this data:
USAGE GUIDELINES:
- Revenue values are in USD.
- When comparing performance, group by Region (North America, EMEA, Asia Pacific, Latin America).
- Order Date should be used for time-based trend analysis. The fiscal year matches the calendar year.
- Date Key is a numeric YYYYMMDD representation of Order Date.
- Sales = Quantity x Unit Price x (1 – Discount)
COMMON USE CASES:
- Regional sales performance comparison.
- Product line revenue analysis.
- Quarterly trend identification.
- Customer segmentation by industry and segment.
TAGS: Sales, revenue, orders, regional performance, product analytics
Column descriptions: Select each column in the left panel and add a description. For example:
- Order ID: “Unique identifier for each sales transaction (format: REGION-YYYY-NNNNNN)”
- Region: “Geographic sales region: North America, EMEA, Asia Pacific, or Latin America”
- Product: “AnyCompany product name: Analytics Pro, Connect, Automate, AI Assistant, Data Catalog, or Integration Hub”
- Sales: “Order revenue in USD after discount”
- Segment: “Customer size segment: Enterprise, Mid-Market, or SMB”
Choose Save & publish to save your changes. The dataset summary now shows the columns with their correct data types and the descriptions you added.
This enriched dataset provides the structured data layer for your solution. When the agent receives a natural language question about sales data, it uses these descriptions and instructions to generate more accurate SQL queries. Combined with the knowledge base from Step 2, you now have both structured and unstructured data ready to bring together in a Space.
Step 4: Create a Space
Spaces in Amazon Quick act as unified data workspaces. A Space can hold file uploads, dashboards, knowledge bases, actions, and datasets, giving your chat agent a single location to query across data types.
From the left navigation, select Spaces and create a new Space. Name it “Business Intelligence Hub”.
Add your knowledge base and dataset to the Space:
- Choose Add knowledge and select Knowledge bases from the list. Select “Business Knowledge Base” from the list.
- Choose Add knowledge again and select Datasets from the list. Select “Product_Sales.csv” from the list.
The Space now shows both your knowledge base (unstructured documents) and your enriched dataset (structured sales data) linked as data sources. This is the central hub where both data types come together, giving your chat agent a single place to query across everything. Figure 7 shows the Space with both resources in the Ready state.
Step 5: Create a custom chat agent
Navigate to Chat agents in the left navigation and choose Create chat agent. Amazon Quick presents a prompt builder where you can describe your agent in natural language or choose from templates like Training Guide, Project Coordinator, and Onboarding Helper.
For this walkthrough, choose Skip to configure the agent manually.
Configure the agent persona
The configuration panel has several sections. Start with the Agent Persona:
- Agent identity: “Business Intelligence Assistant”
- Description: “An AI assistant that breaks down information silos by analyzing business data from your knowledge base”
For Agent Persona instructions, enter:
A note appears confirming that your chat agent comes equipped with enterprise guardrails.
Set communication style
Under Communication style, pick a response style preset. Options include Executive, Technical, and Creative. For a business intelligence use case, select Executive.
Link knowledge sources
Under Knowledge Sources, choose Link spaces and select the “Business Intelligence Hub” Space you created earlier. This gives the agent access to your S3 knowledge base and other data sources in that Space. When you link a Space, the agent answers from large language model (LLM) knowledge and the linked resources only.
You can also attach reference documents (PDF, TXT, HTML, MD, CSV, DOC, DOCX) directly to the agent for additional context. Amazon Quick extracts up to 100,000 characters of text from the reference documents that you upload.
Customize the agent
Under Customization, configure:
- Welcome message: “Hello! I’m your Business Intelligence Assistant. I can help you analyze your sales data and business documents and provide insights by comparing internal information with market trends. How can I help you today?”
- Suggested prompts: “Summarize key insights from our reports” and “Analyze our quarterly sales performance”
Launch the agent
Choose Launch chat agent. The right panel shows a live preview of your agent with the welcome message and suggested prompts displayed.
Step 6: Query across structured and unstructured data
With the agent running, start with a question about your business results:
How did sales change by region in 2025?
For this question, the agent combines results from the Product_Sales.csv dataset with the documents in the S3 knowledge base. It returns a response with regional sales breakdowns, trends, and citations that point back to each source.
Figure 13 shows the response. Each citation marker links a figure back to its source document.
When you ask a question about structured data, the agent uses text-to-SQL to translate your natural language into a SQL query. It runs the query against the dataset and returns the results in a readable format. This means you can ask complex analytical questions without writing SQL yourself.
Next, ask about a specific document:
What are the key strategic priorities outlined in our product strategy memo?
The agent summarizes the strategic pillars, the FY2026 roadmap, and the investment requirements from the Product Strategy Memo, as shown in Figure 14.
Finally, ask a question that needs both data types:
How do our 2025 sales results align with the market trends identified in our analysis report?
The agent compares the trends in the Market Analysis Report with results from your sales data and cites each source, as shown in Figure 15.
This is the core value of combining data types in a single Space. The agent can pull from structured CSV data and unstructured documents in the same response. You don’t need to know where the data lives.
Step 7: Generate artifacts and reports using natural language
The Business Intelligence Assistant can also generate formatted documents, including Microsoft PowerPoint presentations, Microsoft Excel spreadsheets, and Microsoft Word documents. Try these prompts in the chat agent:
- “Create a PowerPoint presentation summarizing AnyCompany’s Q4 2025 sales performance by region, including key trends and recommendations.”
- “Generate an Excel spreadsheet showing the top 10 orders by revenue with Order ID, Region, Product, and Revenue columns.”
- “Create a Word document with a quarterly business review summary based on our annual review data.”
Step 8: Share the agent
When you launch a chat agent, it remains private until you share it. After you test the agent, share it with your team:
- From the left navigation, choose Chat agents.
- In the Actions column for Business Intelligence Assistant, choose the menu icon, and then choose Share.
- Enter the users or groups to share with, assign Owner or Viewer permissions, and then choose Share.
The agent returns permissions-aware responses, and a knowledge base is available only to its creator until you update its permissions. Make sure that the people you share the agent with also have access to the Space, the knowledge base, and the dataset. For details, see Custom chat agents.
What you accomplished
In this walkthrough, you:
- Connected Amazon S3 as a data source through an integration.
- Created a knowledge base that indexes unstructured business documents.
- Created and enriched a Product Sales dataset for structured data queries.
- Built a Space that serves as a unified data hub for your chat agent.
- Configured a custom chat agent with a defined persona and linked knowledge sources.
- Queried the agent across structured and unstructured data in a single conversation.
- Generated a PowerPoint presentation from a chat prompt.
- Shared the agent with your team.
Best practices
Use the following practices as you move from this walkthrough to your own data:
- Organize your S3 data: Use clear folder structures and file naming conventions. A clear structure also makes it more straightforward to scope a knowledge base to specific S3 prefixes.
- Write specific persona instructions: The more specific your instructions, the more consistent the agent responses. Include guidance on how to cite sources and handle ambiguous queries.
- Use Spaces to control scope: Rather than giving an agent access to everything, create focused Spaces with only the data sources relevant to that agent’s purpose.
- Start with suggested prompts: Suggested prompts help users understand what the agent can do. Choose prompts that demonstrate the agent’s range across both structured and unstructured data.
- Test before sharing: Use the preview panel to test your agent with representative questions before sharing it with your team.
Security considerations
Under the AWS shared responsibility model, you are responsible for configuring access to your data, knowledge bases, and agents. Consider the following as you adapt this solution:
- Grant least-privilege S3 access: Give Amazon Quick access only to the buckets that your knowledge bases need. Buckets that an administrator selects have read-only permissions by default. If you create knowledge bases through the API, you can provide a custom AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) role for an individual S3 data source instead of granting account-wide S3 access.
- Control document access: If documents require per-user or per-group access, enable document-level ACLs when you create the knowledge base. You can’t change this choice later.
- Encrypted buckets: If your bucket uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys, follow the AWS KMS steps in the administrator setup guide.
- Add only trusted content: The agent uses the documents in your knowledge base to form responses, so include only content from sources you trust.
- Share selectively: Chat agents and knowledge bases are private by default. Share them only with the users and groups that need them.
- Use guardrails as one layer: Amazon Quick includes built-in content safety screening, and administrators can add up to 50 blocked words or phrases. These controls help reduce risk but don’t replace your responsibility to configure access and permissions. For details, see AI guardrails in Amazon Quick.
Clean up
To avoid ongoing charges, remove the resources you created:
- Delete the chat agent from the Chat agents page.
- Delete the Space from the Spaces page.
- Delete the Product_Sales.csv dataset from the Datasets page.
- Delete the knowledge base and S3 integration from the Knowledge page.
- If you created an S3 bucket specifically for this walkthrough, empty and delete it. Deleting a bucket and its objects is permanent, so back up any data that you want to keep.
Amazon Quick user subscriptions and account fees are billed separately from these resources. For details, see Amazon Quick pricing.
Conclusion
Amazon Quick helps you bring structured and unstructured data together. In this post, you connected S3 as a knowledge base, enriched a dataset, built a Space, and created a custom chat agent. Business users can now query both data types through a single conversational interface, without needing to know where the data lives or how to write queries.

articles.title: Turning pollution into everyday products - Southampton's Virdi raises €2.6 million to transform waste | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Viridi, a British DeepTech that enables the transformation of waste carbon dioxide into chemical products, has closed a €2.6 million (£2.2 million) round to scale their technology, strengthen its team and support its expansion into Asia and the US.
The round was led by Odyssey Ventures, with co-investment from Alphatron Impact Ventures and follow-on commitments from existing angel investors. TOP Ventures, the corporate VC arm of Thaioil, came on board as a strategic investor.
This follows their €3.3 million Seed round in 2023.
Dr Daniel Stewart, CEO of Viridi, says: “Having a strategic partner like TOP Ventures look closely at our technology, see its value and choose to back it at this stage is strong validation of what we’ve built. We’ll be working closely with them to deliver our technology to market, starting in Asia. With Odyssey Ventures supporting our growth in the US, we now have partners who can help us take CO2-based surfactants to the world.”
Viridi’s raise comes amid a series of European investments in carbon utilisation and alternatives to fossil-derived industrial materials in 2026.
Belgium’s D-CRBN secured €17.5 million to convert industrial CO₂ into chemical building blocks, while Switzerland’s Seprify raised €13.4 million for cellulose-based ingredients.
In the UK, Uplift360 secured €7.4 million for composite regeneration, Sparxell raised €4.2 million for plant-based colourants and HexSeed received over €700,000 for CO₂-derived diamond coatings.
Alongside other comparable rounds, these investments and Viridi’s funding total more than €60.3 million, reflecting a defined sample rather than overall sector investment.
Vivat Wongnirund, Vice President-New S-Curve Business Development of Thaioil, adds: “We have followed Viridi’s development since 2024 and have been impressed by its progress, particularly in CO2-based surfactants. The technology has been tested in real manufacturing environments and shows strong potential for integration into existing industrial operations. Viridi’s approach to using captured CO2 as an alternative carbon input is highly innovative.
“This investment gives Thaioil exposure to an emerging technology that fits our future growth strategy in disinfectants and surfactants. We see this technology supporting the future development of surfactant production in Asia and beyond.”
A spinout of the School of Chemistry at the University of Southampton, ViridiCO2 was founded in 2020 and makes a special chemical ingredient (a catalyst) that helps factories turn recycled carbon dioxide (CO₂) pollution into useful materials for everyday products.
Normally, industries use petroleum or chemical processes that harm the environment to make the raw ingredients found in things like liquid detergents, cosmetics, glue, and mattress foams. ViridiCO2’s technology plugs right into existing factory equipment, allowing manufacturers to swap out those dirty fossil fuels for captured CO₂ waste without having to rebuild their facilities.
The technology is designed as a platform that can be applied across multiple classes of chemicals using existing manufacturing infrastructure.
Surfactants, key ingredients across home and personal care, are the first major application, with the potential to extend into other areas of chemical manufacturing, and, ultimately, remove fossil feedstocks from the supply chain entirely.
Ali Mitchell, Managing Partner, Odyssey Ventures, said: “Our commitment is to grow UK and European deep-tech companies that are solving some of the world’s most fundamental problems. Viridi is exactly that kind of company. Combined with a strategic investment from TOP Ventures, our support gives Viridi reach across both the US and Asia as it moves towards commercial deployment.”
Today’s investment builds on the launch of Vireya, Viridi’s first CO2-based anionic surfactant, in 2025 and the company’s Joint Development Agreement with Zschimmer & Schwarz, announced earlier this year, to accelerate the scale-up and market adoption of Viridi’s technology for sustainable surfactants.

articles.title: New York City's Mamdani criticizes Madison Square Garden owner over surveillance tech | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Mayor of New York City Zohran Mamdani has criticized the owner of Madison Square Garden, one of the city’s largest entertainment venues, arguing that the company’s surveillance technology should not be allowed.
Mamdani told Wired in an interview on Tuesday that surveillance technologies are “indicative of much that is wrong in our country today.” He added that City Council member Shahana Hanif introduced two pieces of local legislation aimed at banning the collection of biometric data, such as using facial recognition, in public places across the city. Mamdani said that the draft legislation is “an important response to this kind of an issue.”
The comments come after a stream of reporting from Wired detailing how Madison Square Garden’s owner James Dolan relies on surveillance cameras and face-scanning technology to track people across and outside of its venues.
In one report, Wired revealed that Dolan’s company keeps a database that, among other things, marks some visitors, including celebrity performers, as “LGBTQIA,” for reasons that are unclear. Dolan subsequently sued Wired over its reporting.
In 2021, MSG made headlines after a woman was banned from Radio City, another Dolan-owned venue, after being recognized by facial recognition systems as an attorney at a law firm who was suing Dolan’s company but was not involved in the litigation.
When reached by TechCrunch, Madison Square Garden spokesperson Mikyl Cordova said: “Wired’s reporting is inaccurate and false. MSG is pursuing legal remedies,” without providing evidence for its claim.
Since 2021, New York City has required businesses to disclose when they are collecting biometric data from visitors.
Updated with comment from MSG.

articles.title: GTA VI is starting to take over the GTA
articles.text:
GTA has come to Toronto in a big way.
This week, Torontonians have taken to social media to share images of Grand Theft Auto VI marketing across the city. The most prominent example is a GTA VI takeover of multiple big billboards at Yonge and Dundas, as seen in a video shared by the social media account GTA 6 Countdown. At the end of the video, we also see GTA VI marketing in the Bloor-Yonge TTC station.
Rockstar’s GTA 6 takeover in Toronto, Canada with 3 giant billboards.
(via @TottiN835) https://t.co/zApsJrlwbh
— GTA 6 Countdown ⏳ (@GTAVI_Countdown) November 3, 2026
It remains to be seen what other marketing efforts may come up for the game across Toronto or other parts of Canada. (It’s worth noting that developer Rockstar Games does actually have a Canadian office, Rockstar Toronto, which is based in Oakville. That said, it’s always been low-key about that location, even when people were protesting there last year over layoffs that Rockstar allegedly carried out as part of wider union-busting efforts.)
Either way, this increased marketing push will no doubt make the impending release of GTA VI feel all the more real for fans. After all, the game has been a long time coming, with GTA V having been released in 2013. GTA VI eventually entered early development in 2018 following the release of Red Dead Redemption II and was formally unveiled in 2023 following a major leak. After a couple of delays, the game will now finally launch on Nov. 19 for $109.99.
GTA VI is a Bonnie and Clyde-inspired tale of romantic duo Jason and Lucia as they engage in various criminal activities in the Florida-inspired U.S. state of Leonida. The game will be available on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S at launch, but not PC right away. Pre-loads on console begin on Nov. 10 and will eat up over 200GB of storage.
Image credit: Rockstar Games

articles.title: No eres solo tú: un fallo está drenando la batería de los Pixel Watch (pero tiene solución)
articles.text:
Si tienes un Pixel Watch y has notado que últimamente la batería dura menos de lo habitual, no estás solo. Días atrás comenzaron a circular reportes de usuarios advirtiendo que la energía de su reloj inteligente se agotaba más rápido que de costumbre. Ahora, Google ha confirmado que esto se trata de un fallo y que una solución está en camino.
Curiosamente, la causa del problema todavía no se ha revelado al público. Los usuarios impactados por esta situación simplemente comenzaron a ver que su Pixel Watch tenía una autonomía bastante más acotada de lo habitual. Y si bien las primeras sospechas se posaron sobre una reciente actualización de Wear OS, esto no se ha confirmado ni desmentido por el momento.
Los Pixel Watch afectados por este inconveniente no fueron los de una generación en particular. Básicamente, cualquier modelo desde el Pixel Watch 2 en adelante han presentado este problema. Vale aclarar que, si bien no se trata de un fallo de alcance masivo, sí es un inconveniente de importancia en las unidades donde se presenta.
Algunos de los reportes divulgados en Reddit indicaban que la duración de la batería de los Pixel Watch se había acortado de forma considerable. En los casos más notorios se observaron autonomías máximas de 12 horas, cuando previamente podía superar las 48 horas cuando la función de pantalla siempre encendida permanecía desactivada.
Google ha liberado una solución para los problemas de batería en los Pixel Watch
Desde Google le confirmaron a 9to5Google que ya habían desplegado una actualización para resolver el drenaje de la batería en los Pixel Watch alcanzados. La empresa con sede en Mountain View no reveló la causa formal del inconveniente, aunque remarcó que se hizo presente en un número limitado de unidades.
Un dato que llama la atención es que la solución no llega con una actualización de Wear OS, sino de las apps instaladas. La firma indica que para resolver el fallo hay que ingresar en la Play Store y buscar Administrar apps > Actualizar todas. Una vez que se complete el procedimiento, la duración de la batería de los Pixel Watch afectados debería regresar a la normalidad.
Esto hace pensar que el inconveniente podría estar en la Play Store en sí misma o en alguna de las aplicaciones que Google preinstala en el Pixel Watch. Sea como sea, la resolución ya se encuentra disponible. Los californianos indican que el fix llegará a todos los usuarios en los próximos días, así que si todavía no notas mejoras seguramente debas aguardar un poco más.

articles.title: 'The people deserve to have their RAM too!' Elon Musk mocks OpenAI Sam Altman's claim that people owning home PCs with RAM is 'terrible'
articles.text:
'The people deserve to have their RAM too!' Elon Musk mocks OpenAI Sam Altman's claim that people owning home PCs with RAM is 'terrible'
For once, Musk is right
- Elon Musk mocks Sam Altman's recent claim that people shouldn't own RAM
- "The people deserve to have their RAM too!" Musk's meme on X says
- Altman has been keen to secure more memory for OpenAI recently
Elon Musk has mocked OpenAI CEO Sam Altman following the latter's declaration that owning a PC with RAM is 'quite terrible', as the components should be powering the next generation of AI data centers.
In his typically irreverent manner, Musk shared a meme on X, the social network he owns, showing a version of a scene from Inglorious Basterds with a German WWII officer played by Christoph Waltz apparently hunting for people hiding sticks of DRAM.
"The people deserve to have their RAM too!" Musk's meme declares.
Stopped clock
Altman made his claim during an appearance on the YouTube channel Cheeky Pint, with his beliefs causing widespread condemnation and confusion across the industry.
"From a global allocation perspective, actually, it's quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used 5% of the time," Altman said.
"You want maximum utilization in the cloud if you're trying to deal with this very supply-constrained environment. And somehow many people's intuition is the opposite of that."
Altman's comments come as consumers face rising prices for any kind of computing hardware as the demand for RAM and other components gets passed down.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
In recent months, we've seen the likes of Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan warning of continued shortages and price rises, noting, "AI hardware will stay in short supply for the next 2 to 3 years", a trend he said was "driven by persistent constraints in the underlying tech supply chain."
Dell CEO Michael Dell has also voiced his belief that the memory shortage will get worse through 2027, and that these RAM woes are going to be prolonged for quite some time.
Top DRAM manufacturers Samsung and SK hynix have also warned that AI-driven memory shortages will last until 2027 and beyond, with their supplies rumored to be down to fewer than 10 days of memory inventory.
Interestingly, Altman reportedly recently met with about 50 senior Samsung executives in South Korea, as he looked to secure more hardware for OpenAI to expand its AI capacity.
But no matter what happens, one thing that (probably) won't happen is Altman breaking into your house to steal your PC's RAM...probably.

articles.title: AI chip smugglers exploit trade control loophole to bring banned HBM from South Korea into China — expensive memory chips packaged with cheap, unsanctioned processors to become legal exports
articles.text:
AI chip smugglers exploit trade control loophole to bring banned HBM from South Korea into China — expensive memory chips packaged with cheap, unsanctioned processors to become legal exports
Is it smuggling if it's technically legal?
A memory smuggler has detailed how he gets export-controlled HBM chips from South Korea into China using a loophole. According to The Information, the smuggler owns a chip design firm that build cheap, low-performing processors that fall under the U.S. and South Korea’s export controls. They are then paired with expensive HBM from Samsung and SK hynix, that, on their own, are banned for export to China. But because export control rules only look at the performance of the server processor and not at the other components attached to it, this allows the HBM chips attached inside them to slip under the radar and make their way into China.
It’s not a risk-free operation, though. Once the mediocre processors with high-end memory chips land in Hong Kong and are smuggled across the border into Shenzhen in the luggage of commuters that cross between the two regions daily, they end up in workshops where technicians heat up the boards to soften the solder, gingerly lift the crucial memory chips, and discard the rest of the components. Despite having a high failure rate, the high price of HBM chips makes the procedure quite lucrative.
A Shenzhen-based chip broker has been making big money matching up suppliers such as the smuggler and companies that are desperate for HBM. “A year ago, a single HBM3E unit changed hands in China for several hundred dollars,” he tells the publication. “Today it’s about $4,000.” With an AI chip requiring six to eight high-end memory chips, that means the broker is raking in $24,000 to $32,000 for every AI GPU.
Chinese AI labs face this exact memory chip bottleneck when acquiring AI GPUs. While Chinese memory manufacturer CXMT has already begun risk production of HBM3E and is expected to mass produce them by the end of this year, it’s still reportedly suffering from low yield, which makes their chips expensive to produce and procure. We see this with Huawei’s Ascend 950DT, its current top-of-the-line processor that goes for about $37,000 — it offers similar pricing to Nvidia’s B200 AI GPU but only delivers half the performance of the previous-generation H100.
Huawei has reportedly said that its next-generation flagship AI processor, the 960DT, would deliver a similar performance as the H100. However, since the company cannot purchase HBM from Samsung and SK hynix, and Chinese memory manufacturers do not have the capacity to supply all its chip demands, Huawei told customers that they have to find the HBM that these servers need themselves. This would further fuel the demand for these chips, increase the price and make it more lucrative for smugglers to set up similar operations.
But given that this method of moving HBM chips into China is becoming more popular, the smuggler fears that South Korean and U.S. authorities would clamp down on their operations soon. Washington has been going down hard on activities like this, and we’ve seen high-profile arrests including some Super Micro executives and the CEO of a California-based tech company. Other countries like Taiwan and Malaysia have been ramping up their anti-smuggling activities, too, so it’s probably just a matter of time before Seoul follows suit.

articles.title: Après la pénurie de l’été, les ventilateurs de plafond reviennent pour le Black Friday chez Amazon, jusqu’à -31%
articles.text:
Les canicules de l’été avaient vidé les stocks de ventilateurs, et les modèles de plafond reviennent au moment où le Black Friday a déjà commencé chez la plupart des marchands. Voici 5 modèles repérés chez Amazon, avec ce qu’il faut vérifier pour qu’ils servent aussi cet hiver, en renvoyant vers le sol la chaleur accumulée au plafond.
Cet été, la loongue canicule avait vidé les rayons des marchands, et certaines références de ventilateurs étaient devenues difficiles à trouver. En ce début novembre, les cinq modèles de notre sélection sont de nouveau affichés en stock chez Amazon, alors que le Black Friday a déjà démarré chez la plupart des enseignes.
Acheter un ventilateur en novembre n’a rien d’absurde. Un ventilateur de plafond doté d’une fonction été/hiver sait inverser le sens de rotation de ses pales : l’hiver, il renvoie dans la pièce l’air chaud du chauffage qui stagne sous le plafond. C’est ce qu’on appelle la déstratification. Quatre des cinq modèles retenus l’annoncent sur leur fiche, et les remises atteignent -31 % sur les prix de référence affichés par Amazon.
Les 5 ventilateurs de plafond en promo chez Amazon pour le Black Friday

VPN, logiciels, abonnements : les promos à saisir en ce moment
Quel ventilateur de plafond choisir pour l’été comme pour l’hiver ?
Sur le papier, les cinq modèles se ressemblent : télécommande, minuterie, pales larges. Ils se distinguent sur trois points qui comptent vraiment, le diamètre, le moteur et la présence d’une fonction été/hiver clairement annoncée. Nous ne les avons pas testés : les caractéristiques ci-dessous sont celles que publient Cecotec et Create sur leurs fiches.
- Cecotec EnergySilence Aero 495 : le moins cher de la sélection, avec un moteur de 55 W, cinq pales et 106 cm de diamètre, pour des pièces jusqu’à 25 m² selon Cecotec. Sa fiche annonce des pales réversibles, mais aucune fonction été/hiver : si la déstratification est votre motivation, l’Aero 4500 au même prix est plus sûr. Il se limite aussi à trois vitesses.
- Cecotec EnergySilence Aero 5290 Stone Pro : le plus grand des trois Cecotec, avec 132 cm d’envergure et trois pales, pour un salon ou une pièce de vie. Moteur DC de 35 W, cinq vitesses, hauteur réglable entre 15 et 25 cm, lumière LED à intensité réglable et fonction été/hiver décrite en détail par le fabricant. C’est l’économie la plus forte de la sélection, 47,35 € sur le prix conseillé.
- Cecotec EnergySilence Aero 4500 Puzzle : même prix que l’Aero 495, mais avec un moteur DC de 30 W, six vitesses et la fonction été/hiver. Ses quatre pales se replient quand il est à l’arrêt, ce qui le rend plus discret au plafond d’une chambre ou d’un bureau. Sa minuterie plafonne à 4 heures.
- Create Windlarge Wi-Fi : le plus grand de la sélection, 152 cm, pour les grandes pièces. Il se pilote à la télécommande ou en Wi-Fi, propose six vitesses, la fonction été/hiver et deux hauteurs de fixation grâce à des barres de 25 et 50 cm. Sa fiche ne mentionne pas d’éclairage, et sa remise reste modeste : 15 € sur l’ancien prix affiché par Amazon.
- Create Windcalm S avec lumière : le compromis en 112 cm, avec un moteur DC de 40 W, six vitesses, la fonction été/hiver et une lumière LED de 15 W à trois températures de couleur, dont l’intensité ne se règle pas. Ses pales en ABS autorisent aussi une installation en extérieur selon Create. Il n’affiche en revanche aucune remise au moment où nous écrivons.
Black Friday : faut-il acheter un ventilateur de plafond maintenant ?
Sur les quatre modèles remisés, l’économie va de 15 € à 47,35 €. Les trois Cecotec affichent -28 à -31 %, mais ces pourcentages se calculent sur le prix conseillé par le fabricant, pas sur un prix réellement pratiqué. Le repère le plus parlant est ailleurs : pour ces trois modèles, le prix actuel passe sous le plus bas des 30 derniers jours indiqué par Amazon (72,90 € pour les deux modèles de 106 cm, 129 € pour l’Aero 5290). Le Create Windlarge ne perd que 9 % sur son ancien prix, et le Windcalm S n’est pas remisé.
Pour l’hiver, gardez en tête qu’un ventilateur de plafond ne chauffe pas : il remet en circulation l’air chaud que produit déjà votre chauffage et qui stagne sous le plafond. Dans une chambre, le bruit compte autant que le diamètre, et notre comparatif des meilleurs ventilateurs silencieux retient d’ailleurs un modèle de plafond doté de cette fonction été/hiver. Prévoyez enfin l’installation : un ventilateur de plafond se fixe au plafond et se raccorde au circuit électrique, une opération à confier à un électricien si vous n’êtes pas à l’aise.
Ventilateur de plafond : vos questions
À quoi sert la fonction été/hiver d’un ventilateur de plafond ?
Elle inverse le sens de rotation des pales. L’été, le flux d’air rafraîchit la pièce ; l’hiver, il redistribue l’air chaud du chauffage accumulé au plafond.
Un ventilateur de plafond peut-il remplacer un chauffage ?
Non, il ne produit pas de chaleur. En mode hiver, il remet en circulation celle de votre chauffage, que Cecotec présente comme un complément de votre système de chauffage.
Quel diamètre de ventilateur de plafond choisir ?
Cecotec annonce son Aero 495 de 106 cm pour des pièces jusqu’à 25 m² et présente l’Aero 4500, de même diamètre, comme adapté aux chambres, petits salons et bureaux. Les modèles de 132 et 152 cm visent des pièces plus grandes.

articles.title: Octopus Energy is joining forces with battery experts CATL and Ampace for the 'next generation' of smart home batteries — promising to 'transform home energy storage'
articles.text:
Octopus Energy says it's making 'next gen' home batteries with CATL and Ampace — sodium-ion and high-density cells could make the bill-cutting tech 'far more affordable'
Lower electricity bills ahoy
- Octopus Energy, Ampace, and CATL are joining forces
- They're promising to 'transform' the smart home battery landscape
- We're expecting next-gen tech like sodium-ion batteries
It's a boom time for home energy solutions — from DIY solar kits to smart home batteries — and three of the biggest names in the industry are joining forces to build the next generation of home energy storage solutions.
Energy supplier Octopus and battery manufacturers CATL and Ampace have announced a 'Memorandum of Understanding' (MoU) to work together to produce the best possible combinations of hardware engineering and software intelligence.
Octopus will bring tech such as the smart tariff, mobile app, and customer ecosystem platforms, while CATL and Ampace supply the battery chemistry and hardware nous. Initially, the initiative will be focused on European markets.
At this early stage we don't have details of any actual products, but expect advances in cutting-edge tech like sodium-ion batteries, high-density cell designs, and long battery lifecycles — all of which should benefit customers and reduce electricity bills.
Looking to the future
According to Octopus founder and CEO Greg Jackson, combining the efforts of the three companies will "transform home energy storage", and offer "next-generation batteries where hardware and software work in complete harmony".
Jason Zhu, the President of Energy Storage Systems at Ampace, is equally enthusiastic: the partnership will "fundamentally reshape how energy is delivered and consumed" as systems become "smarter, more connected, and more accessible".
Of course we'll have to reserve judgment until actual products and offers arrive, but Octopus Energy, CATL, and Ampace all have strong track records. The products that we've seen from these companies, we've liked.

The joint press release emphasized the ability for home batteries to charge up during off-peak times and share power back to the grid at times of highest demand, which should mean significant savings for customers — something everyone can support.

articles.title: ServiceNow on-behalf-of token exchange with Bedrock AgentCore Gateway | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
ServiceNow on-behalf-of token exchange with Bedrock AgentCore Gateway
AI agents that interact with enterprise APIs on behalf of users need to maintain user identity throughout the request chain. Without identity propagation, API calls arrive at downstream services as the application itself rather than the user who initiated the action. This breaks audit trails, bypasses user-level access controls, and violates the principle of least privilege.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore is a platform to build, connect, and optimize agents at scale, with any framework or model. This post shows how to configure AgentCore Gateway, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, for an on-behalf-of (OBO) token exchange with Microsoft Entra ID. An AI agent can then call the ServiceNow REST API while preserving the calling user’s identity. You configure the token exchange on the gateway target, and AgentCore Gateway performs the exchange on each request. The pattern can be applied to other REST APIs protected by OAuth.
In production, you can additionally pair identity propagation with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to filter harmful content and validate the agent’s inputs and outputs.
Solution overview
The architecture involves three key components connected through AgentCore Gateway:
- An AI agent application, protected by Microsoft Entra ID through an OAuth application registration.
- A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server, implemented using AgentCore Gateway, sitting between the agent and ServiceNow.
- The ServiceNow REST API, configured with an inbound OAuth integration tied to Microsoft Entra ID.
The following figure shows the end-to-end solution architecture, including components within AWS, Microsoft Entra ID, and ServiceNow.
As shown in Figure 1, the user acquires a JSON Web Token (JWT) to invoke the agent 1. The agent authenticates to the gateway with a JWT token scoped to the agent’s own application registration 2. The gateway then exchanges that token, using the OBO flow, for a new token scoped to the ServiceNow API connector, with the original user’s identity preserved 3. ServiceNow receives a valid token whose preferred_username claim maps to an existing ServiceNow user and applies that user’s permissions to the API call 4.
How OBO token exchange works in this context
When the agent calls the gateway, it presents a JWT with an audience claim matching the agent’s client ID (for example, 3ff88e17-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX). ServiceNow, however, expects a token with an audience claim matching its own API connector client ID (5d4a7a11-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXXXXXXXXXX).
The OBO flow bridges this gap. AgentCore Gateway sends the inbound token to the Entra token endpoint along with the agent application’s client credentials, the target scope, and a parameter requested_token_use: on_behalf_of. Entra validates that the calling user consented to the delegation, then issues a new token for the ServiceNow API with the original user’s claims intact.
Prerequisites
Before you begin, you need the following:
- An AWS account with access to AgentCore Gateway.
- A Microsoft Entra ID tenant with permissions to create application registrations. Your account needs at least the Application Developer role to register applications.
- A ServiceNow instance with administrative access to configure inbound OAuth integrations. You can create a ServiceNow personal developer instance (PDI) at the ServiceNow personal developer instance signup page https://developer.servicenow.com/.
- Two Entra application registrations: one representing the AI agent, and one representing the ServiceNow API connector.
Configuring Microsoft Entra ID
Start by creating an application registration to represent the ServiceNow API connector. The following screenshot shows the application registration page for the ServiceNow API Connector in Microsoft Entra ID.
After creating, in the Overview page note the Application (client) ID.
In the navigation menu expand Manage and select Expose an API and add a scope named user_impersonation using the default Application ID URI. This scope is what the OBO flow requests when exchanging tokens. The following screenshot shows how to expose an API in Microsoft Entra ID.
Next, create an application registration for the AI agent. The following screenshot shows the application registration page in Microsoft Entra ID for the ServiceNow Agent application.
Note the Application (client) ID for the ServiceNowAgent.
Create a client secret on this registration. The gateway needs these credentials to perform the OBO exchange. The following screenshot shows how you can create a client secret on the ServiceNow Agent application registration in Microsoft Entra ID.
Then configure the agent application to have API permissions to call the ServiceNow API connector application. The following screenshot shows the API permissions that you need to configure on the ServiceNow Agent application registration in Microsoft Entra ID.
No changes to the Entra configuration are needed beyond what you would set up for any standard OBO integration between two applications.
Configuring ServiceNow
In the ServiceNow administrative console, navigate to System OAuth > Inbound Integrations and create a new inbound integration (Third party ID token issued by OIDC supporting identity provider). Specify the client ID from the ServiceNow API connector application registration you created in Entra. The following screenshot shows the configuration of the inbound integration in ServiceNow.
In the same screen, create a new OpenID Connect (OIDC) provider configuration and enter the OIDC metadata URL for your Entra tenant. Map the user claim to the appropriate user field. For example, if your Entra tenant places the user’s email in the preferred_username claim, map that to the Email field in ServiceNow. Clear JTI verification if your Entra tenant doesn’t include it in tokens. Entra uses an internal claim named uti on tokens it issues, which is equivalent to JTI. Consider mapping this uti claim to a jti claim to provide additional replay protection and denylisting. The following screenshot shows how to configure the OIDC provider in ServiceNow.
Finally, in the same screen, create an auth scope for the integration (for example, APIConnector). The following screenshot shows how to create a new auth scope in ServiceNow.
Limit the auth scope to the Table API, or whichever ServiceNow APIs your agent needs to access, as shown in the following screenshot.
After this configuration is complete, ServiceNow accepts authorization tokens with an audience of your API connector’s client ID and resolves the calling user from the preferred_username claim.
Configuring AgentCore Gateway
With Entra and ServiceNow configured, you can now set up AgentCore Gateway to handle the OBO exchange natively.
Step 1: Create an outbound auth configuration
Create a new outbound auth configuration (choose Build > Identity > Add Outbound Auth > Add OAuth client) in AgentCore and select Customized provider. Enter the client ID and client secret from your agent application registration, along with the Entra discovery URL as shown in the following screenshot.
Expand Additional configurations and select JWT authorization grant as shown in the following screenshot. This tells the gateway to use a JWT-based grant type for token exchange.
Step 2: Create the gateway with MCP version 2025-11-25
Create a new AgentCore Gateway (Build > Gateways > Create gateway). When defining the gateway details, expand Additional configurations — optional and select MCP version 2025-11-25 as shown in the following screenshot. This version is required for native OBO support. You can’t turn on native OBO for gateways created with earlier MCP versions.
Configure the inbound identity using your agent’s application registration (select Use existing identity provider configurations), as you would for any gateway that accepts Entra-authenticated requests.
Under JWT Authorization Configuration add the Application ID we documented earlier for the ServiceNowAgent as shown in the following screenshot.
Step 3: Add a target with token exchange
Add a target to the gateway pointing to your ServiceNow REST endpoint. Define the schema inline. For example, to expose a tool called ListIncidents that calls the ServiceNow Table API, you can use the following OpenAPI specification (replace the server URL with that for your PDI).
The following screenshot shows how to configure the REST API target in AgentCore Gateway with the OpenAPI schema.
For the Outbound Auth configuration on the target, select OAuth as the outbound identity provider and choose the outbound auth configuration you created in Step 1.
Now expand the Additional configurations section and select Token exchange grant. Configure the following:
Scope: api://5d4a7a11-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx/user_impersonation
This is the scope you exposed on the ServiceNow API connector application registration in Entra.
Custom parameter (key-value pair): requested_token_use:on_behalf_of
This parameter is critical. Without it, Entra doesn’t perform the OBO exchange and the call to ServiceNow fails with an authentication error.
The final configuration is shown in the following screenshot.
Step 4: Save and test
Save the target configuration. AgentCore Gateway now automatically exchanges inbound tokens for valid ServiceNow tokens, preserving user identity, with no custom code.
When an agent calls the gateway, the following happens transparently:
- The gateway receives the agent’s JWT (audience: agent client ID).
- The gateway sends the token to Entra’s token endpoint with the OBO grant type.
- Entra issues a new token (audience: ServiceNow API connector client ID) with the original user’s claims.
- The gateway forwards the request to ServiceNow with the exchanged token.
- ServiceNow resolves the user from the token and applies their permissions.
The following code snippet shows a minimal chat agent that interacts with ServiceNow through the MCP server.
Troubleshooting
If you receive authentication errors from ServiceNow, verify that:
- The preferred_username claim in the exchanged token maps to a valid user email in ServiceNow.
- The auth scope on the ServiceNow inbound integration permits access to the API endpoints your agent is calling.
- The agent application has API permissions to the ServiceNow API connector application in Entra.
Cleaning up
To avoid ongoing charges, delete the following resources if you created them for testing:
- The AgentCore Gateway and its targets.
- The outbound auth configuration.
- The Entra application registrations (if created specifically for this walkthrough).
- The ServiceNow inbound integration and OIDC provider configuration.
Conclusion
The native OBO support in AgentCore Gateway removes the need for custom AWS Lambda interceptors to perform token exchanges. You configure the token exchange directly on the gateway target, and the gateway handles it transparently on every request. This approach maintains user identity across the agent-to-API chain, supports ServiceNow’s user-level access controls, and eliminates custom code that would need to be maintained separately.
To get started with AgentCore Gateway, see the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore documentation. For more on Microsoft Entra’s OBO flow, refer to the Microsoft identity platform documentation.

articles.title: Steam Survey shockwaves felt as proportion of 32GB RAM systems drops by more than 5% — the percentage of PC gamers with 1TB+ total storage also shrunk by nearly 5%
articles.text:
Steam Survey shockwaves felt as proportion of 32GB RAM systems drops by more than 5% — the percentage of PC gamers with 1TB+ total storage also shrunk by nearly 5%
The reduced RAM/storage trends have been set in retail for a number of months already.
The latest Steam Survey appears to show that gamers blessed with systems packing 32GB or more RAM and 1TB or more storage are a dwindling breed. This survey is posted without comment by Valve, as usual, but appears to show a significant proportional rise in gamers using 8GB and 16GB RAM PCs, which occurs largely at the expense of the 32GB brigade. The latest stats also show a noticeable increase in storage capacity poverty in the last month. Are the symptoms of the AI industry-induced components crunch now becoming evident among the PC gaming public?
The AI-pocalypse delivered components crunch has been in the headlines for months but it is still jarring to see it impact the vast PC gaming landscape. When we’ve browsed desktop and laptop PCs for the best gaming PC deals over the past months, the trend is clear. Systems that look like they are designed for gamers or enthusiasts are now frequently fitted with just 16GB of RAM as standard, and also feature smaller storage devices that one might have expected. But to see the Steam Survey suggesting that the share of 32GB systems has now collapsed by -5.16% is startling. Only last month, 32GB was the most popular configuration among gamers according to the same survey.
RAM is probably the hardest-hit component segment of AI-driven demand so far. We maintain a RAM price tracking page at Tom’s Hardware and the current state of the market means that DIYers or upgraders need to spend about $250 for 16GB DDR5 or $450 for 32GB DDR5. Those prices change regularly, as well.
Moving onto the sudden recorded change in storage configurations in use by Steam gamers, and we see that folks with 1TB of total fixed storage space or above shrunk by 4.68%. As the categories are currently defined, this appears to show the reduction in the number of systems coming with either a 2TB and 4TB SSD as standard. That’s because the 750GB to 999GB category grew +2.36%, and Windows registers a '1TB' boot disk as a smaller (a quick check shows ours at 924GB). 250GB to 499GB total storage systems were also up a similar amount (+2.30%). Overall, it looks like systems being used for Steam gaming are increasingly fitted with these smaller capacity SSDs. Enthusiasts, gamers, and DIYers wanting to expand their storage at the best prices are advised to keep an eye on our frequently updated SSD price tracking page.
We are currently seeing some extraordinary things in the GPU market, with reports of RTX 5090 and RTX 5080 cards being removed from retail. In the Steam Survey this month the RTX 5080 is still at position 14. However, the joint most popular GPUs are the RTX 5070 and the aging RTX 3060 – both with 3.78% of the market.
We are aware that there are sometimes some strong undercurrents in the Steam Survey that cause unusual fluctuations in the figures. However, the numbers this month don’t look like they have been impacted by a Chinese user or Chinese internet café PC influx, which have previously shown odd trends (such as a rise in Windows 10 usage). Actually, the Steam Survey shows Chinese (Simplified) language users surveyed are sharply down this month, so the survey should more accurately represent the system configurations typical among gamers in the West.
